sentences.zh: 陳訓

translations.literal: Chen Xun.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Xun.

sentences.zh: 陳訓，字道元，曆陽人。

translations.literal: Chen Xun, courtesy name Daoyuan, was a native of Liyang.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Xun, whose courtesy name was Daoyuan, came from Liyang.

sentences.zh: 少好秘學，天文、算曆、陰陽、占候無不畢綜，尤善風角。

translations.literal: In his youth he loved esoteric learning; in astronomy, calendrical calculation, yin-yang theory, and divination by omens there was nothing he did not master comprehensively, and he was especially skilled in fengjiao (wind-angle divination).
translations.idiomatic: From a young age he was drawn to occult studies, and he commanded the whole range of astronomy, calendar science, yin–yang lore, and omen divination, with particular mastery of wind-angle technique.

sentences.zh: 孫晧以為奉禁都尉，使其占侯。

translations.literal: Sun Hao appointed him Palace Prohibition Commandant and had him perform omen divination.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Hao named him commandant charged with palace prohibitions and set him to reading omens.

sentences.zh: 晧政嚴酷，訓知其必敗而不敢言。

translations.literal: Hao's government was harsh and cruel; Xun knew it was bound to fail but dared not speak.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Hao ruled with pitiless severity; Chen Xun saw the regime was doomed yet held his tongue.

sentences.zh: 時錢唐湖開，或言天下當太平，青蓋入洛陽。

translations.literal: At that time Qiantang Lake opened up, and some said the realm would soon be at peace and the green imperial canopy would enter Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: When Qiantang Lake burst its bounds, people took it as a sign that peace would return and the emperor's green canopy would soon reach Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 晧以問訓，訓曰：「臣止能望氣，不能達湖之開塞。

translations.literal: Hao asked Xun about it, and Xun said, "Your servant can only observe qi; I cannot interpret whether a lake opens or closes."
translations.idiomatic: Sun Hao pressed him for an interpretation. Chen Xun replied, "I can read the vapors in the air, not divine whether a lake is opening or silting shut."

sentences.zh: 」退而告其友曰：「青蓋入洛，將有輿櫬銜璧之事，非吉祥也。

translations.literal: When he withdrew he told his friends, "If the green canopy enters Luo, there will be the business of a bier borne forth and jade held in the teeth—this is not auspicious."
translations.idiomatic: Privately he told friends, "When they speak of the green canopy entering Luoyang, they are really foretelling a surrender procession—bier, coffin, jade between the lips. That is no good omen."

sentences.zh: 」尋而吳亡。

translations.literal: Before long Wu perished.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Wu fell.

sentences.zh: 訓隨例內徙，拜諫義大夫。

translations.literal: Xun, following the usual practice, was moved inland and was appointed Grandee Remonstrant.
translations.idiomatic: He was relocated inland like other former Wu officials and appointed remonstrance grandee.

sentences.zh: 俄而去職還鄉。

translations.literal: Soon he left office and returned to his home village.
translations.idiomatic: He soon resigned and went home.

sentences.zh: 及陳敏作亂，遣弟宏為曆陽太守，訓謂邑人曰：「陳家無王氣，不久當滅。

translations.literal: When Chen Min rebelled, he sent his younger brother Hong as governor of Liyang; Xun said to the people of his district, "The Chen clan has no kingly qi; before long they will be destroyed."
translations.idiomatic: When Chen Min rose in revolt and installed his brother Hong as Liyang governor, Chen Xun told his neighbors, "The house of Chen carries no aura of kingship; it will not last."

sentences.zh: 」宏聞，將斬之。

translations.literal: When Hong heard this, he was about to execute Xun.
translations.idiomatic: Hong, hearing that, meant to put him to death.

sentences.zh: 訓鄉人秦琚為宏參軍，乃說訓曰：「訓善風角，可試之。

translations.literal: Xun's fellow townsman Qin Ju, who was Hong's aide, then urged Xun, saying, "Xun is skilled in fengjiao; you may put him to the test.
translations.idiomatic: Qin Ju of the same town, serving as Hong's adjutant, pleaded, "Chen Xun's wind-angle art is genuine—test him first."

sentences.zh: 如不中，徐斬未晚也。

translations.literal: If he is not accurate, it will not be too late to behead him slowly."
translations.idiomatic: If he fails, you can always kill him later."

sentences.zh: 」乃赦之。

translations.literal: Thereupon he spared him.
translations.idiomatic: Hong relented and spared him.

sentences.zh: 時宏攻征東參軍衡彥于曆陽，乃問訓曰：「城中有幾千人？

translations.literal: At that time Hong was attacking the Eastern Expedition Army staff officer Heng Yan at Liyang, and he asked Xun, "How many thousand men are in the city?
translations.idiomatic: While Hong besieged Heng Yan, the Eastern Expedition staff officer, in Liyang, he demanded of Chen Xun, "How many defenders are inside?"

sentences.zh: 攻之可拔不？

translations.literal: Can it be taken if we attack?
translations.idiomatic: Can we storm it successfully?"

sentences.zh: 」訓登牛渚山望氣，曰：「不過五百人。

translations.literal: Xun climbed Mount Niuzhu to observe the qi and said, "No more than five hundred men.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Xun climbed Mount Niuzhu, read the vapors, and said, "Fewer than five hundred."

sentences.zh: 然不可攻，攻之必敗。

translations.literal: Yet it must not be attacked; if attacked, you will certainly be defeated."
translations.idiomatic: But do not attack; an assault will end in rout."

sentences.zh: 」宏復大怒曰：「何有五千人攻五百人而有不得理？

translations.literal: Hong again raged, "How can there be a case of five thousand men attacking five hundred and yet it not be reasonable to prevail?
translations.idiomatic: Hong flared again: "What sense is there in five thousand men failing against five hundred?"

sentences.zh: 」命將士攻之，果為彥所敗，方信訓有道術，乃優遇之。

translations.literal: He ordered his generals and soldiers to attack; they were indeed defeated by Yan, and only then did he believe Xun had the Way and its techniques, and he treated him generously.
translations.idiomatic: He threw his army at the walls and was crushed by Heng Yan. Only then did Hong concede that Chen Xun possessed true art and began to honor him.

sentences.zh: 都水參軍淮南周亢嘗問訓以官位，訓曰：「君至卯年當剖符近郡，酉年當有曲蓋。

translations.literal: Zhou Kang of Huainan, an aide in the Directorate of Waters, once asked Xun about his official career, and Xun said, "In the mao year you will receive tally authority in a nearby commandery; in the you year you will obtain a curved canopy."
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Kang of Huainan, who served on the waterways staff, asked about his career. Chen Xun said, "In the year of the Hare you will split tallies in a neighboring command; in the year of the Rooster you will earn a curved canopy."

sentences.zh: 」亢曰：「脫如來言，當相薦拔。

translations.literal: Kang said, "If it comes true as you say, I will recommend and promote you."
translations.idiomatic: Kang replied, "If it unfolds as you say, I will see you advanced."

sentences.zh: 」訓曰：「性不好官，惟欲得米耳。

translations.literal: Xun said, "By nature I do not love office; I only wish to obtain rice."
translations.idiomatic: Chen Xun answered, "I have no taste for rank—only for grain."

sentences.zh: 」後亢果為義興太守、金紫將軍。

translations.literal: Later Kang indeed became governor of Yixing and General of the Golden Purple.
translations.idiomatic: Kang later became governor of Yixing and golden-purple general, just as foretold.

sentences.zh: 時劉聰、王彌寇洛陽，曆陽太守武瑕問訓曰：「國家人事如何？

translations.literal: At the time Liu Cong and Wang Mi raided Luoyang; Wu Xia, the governor of Liyang, asked Xun, "How do matters stand for the court and the realm?
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Cong and Wang Mi struck at Luoyang, Liyang governor Wu Xia asked him, "What lies ahead for the dynasty?"

sentences.zh: 」訓曰：「胡賊三逼，國家當敗，天子野死。

translations.literal: Xun said, "The Hu bandits press in thrice; the state will be defeated and the Son of Heaven will die in the open wilds.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Xun said, "The barbarian hosts will close in three times; the state will collapse and the emperor will perish in the fields."

sentences.zh: 今尚未也。

translations.literal: It has not yet reached that point."
translations.idiomatic: That hour has not yet struck."

sentences.zh: 」其後懷湣二帝果有平陽之酷焉。

translations.literal: Afterward the two emperors Huai and Min indeed suffered the cruelty at Pingyang.
translations.idiomatic: The reigns of Emperors Huai and Min ended in the horrors of Pingyang, as he had warned.

sentences.zh: 或問其以明年吉凶者，訓曰：「揚州刺史當死，武昌大火，上方節將亦當死。

translations.literal: When someone asked him about good and ill fortune for the next year, Xun said, "The governor of Yang Province will die; there will be a great fire in Wuchang; a senior general of the upper circuit will also die."
translations.idiomatic: Asked about the coming year, he predicted the death of the Yangzhou governor, a great blaze in Wuchang, and the fall of a high frontier commander.

sentences.zh: 」至時，劉陶、周訪皆卒，武昌大火，燒數千家。

translations.literal: When the time came, Liu Tao and Zhou Fang both died; there was a great fire in Wuchang that burned several thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Tao and Zhou Fang died on schedule; Wuchang burned and thousands of homes were lost.

sentences.zh: 時甘卓為曆陽太守，訓私謂所親曰：「甘侯頭低而視仰，相法名為眄刀，又目有赤脈，自外而入，不出十年，必以兵死，不領兵則可以免。

translations.literal: At the time Gan Zhuo was governor of Liyang; Xun privately said to those close to him, "Lord Gan's head hangs low while his gaze tilts upward; in physiognomy this is called 'the sideways-blade glance,' and again there are red threads in his eyes entering from without; within ten years he will surely die by weapons—only if he does not command troops can he escape.
translations.idiomatic: While Gan Zhuo held Liyang, Chen Xun confided to friends, "Gan's chin is tucked yet his eyes look up—a face called 'blade in the sidelong glance'—and red veins run into the whites from without. Within a decade he will die by the sword unless he lays down command."

sentences.zh: 」卓果為王敦所害。

translations.literal: Zhuo was indeed killed by Wang Dun.
translations.idiomatic: Gan Zhuo was indeed killed on Wang Dun's orders.

sentences.zh: 丞相王導多病，每自憂慮，以問訓。

translations.literal: Chancellor Wang Dao was often ill and worried about himself, and he questioned Xun.
translations.idiomatic: Chancellor Wang Dao, often sick with worry, consulted Chen Xun.

sentences.zh: 訓曰：「公耳豎垂肩，必壽，亦大貴，子孫當興于江東。

translations.literal: Xun said, "Your ears stand straight and reach your shoulders; you are sure to enjoy long life, and you are also greatly noble; your sons and grandsons will rise east of the Yangzi."
translations.idiomatic: Chen Xun told him, "Your ears rise straight to your shoulders—you will live long and rise to the highest honor, and your line will flourish south of the river."

sentences.zh: 」咸如其言。

translations.literal: All came true as he said.
translations.idiomatic: Every detail proved true.

sentences.zh: 訓年八十餘卒。

translations.literal: Xun died in his eighties.
translations.idiomatic: He died in his eighties.

sentences.zh: 戴洋

translations.literal: Dai Yang.
translations.idiomatic: Dai Yang.

sentences.zh: 戴洋，字國流，吳興長城人也。

translations.literal: Dai Yang, courtesy name Guoliu, was a native of Changcheng in Wuxing.
translations.idiomatic: Dai Yang, courtesy name Guoliu, was from Changcheng in Wuxing commandery.

sentences.zh: 年十二，遇病死，五日而蘇。

translations.literal: At age twelve he encountered illness and died, but after five days he revived.
translations.idiomatic: At twelve he fell ill, "died," and returned to life after five days.

sentences.zh: 說死時天使其為酒藏吏，授符錄，給吏從幡麾，將上蓬萊、昆侖、積石、太室、恆、廬、衡等諸山。

translations.literal: He said that when dead Heaven had made him keeper of the wine vaults, had given him tallies and registers, had supplied him with clerks, followers, banners, and standards, and had taken him up Mount Penglai, Mount Kunlun, Jishi, Taishi, Mount Heng (north), Mount Lu, Mount Heng (south), and other peaks.
translations.idiomatic: He described how, in death, heaven appointed him cellar-master for the brews, handed him registers and tallies, gave him a retinue with banners, and led him on a tour of Penglai, Kunlun, Jishi, the central peaks, and the northern and southern Heng and Lu ranges.

sentences.zh: 既而遣歸，逢一老父，謂之曰：「汝後當得道，為貴人所識。

translations.literal: Then he was sent back, and he met an old man who said to him, "Later you will obtain the Way and will be recognized by noble men."
translations.idiomatic: Sent back to life, he met an old man who said, "You will later perfect the Way and be singled out by the great."

sentences.zh: 」及長，遂善風角。

translations.literal: When he grew up, he was then skilled in fengjiao.
translations.idiomatic: As an adult he excelled at wind-angle divination.

sentences.zh: 為人短陋，無風望，然好道術，妙解占侯卜數。

translations.literal: In person he was short and unprepossessing, without commanding presence, yet he loved Daoist arts and wonderfully understood omen divination, divination by milfoil, and numerology.
translations.idiomatic: He was plain, short, and undistinguished in bearing, yet he loved occult arts and had a genius for omens, yarrow, and number-craft.

sentences.zh: 吳末為台吏，知吳將亡，託病不仕。

translations.literal: At the end of Wu he was a clerk in the terrace service; knowing Wu would perish, he pleaded illness and did not take office.
translations.idiomatic: In Wu's last days he served as a terrace clerk; foreseeing the kingdom's fall, he feigned illness and refused appointment.

sentences.zh: 及吳平，還鄉里。

translations.literal: When Wu was pacified, he returned to his home village.
translations.idiomatic: After Wu surrendered he went home.

sentences.zh: 後行至瀨鄉，經老子祠，皆是洋昔死時所見使處，但不復見昔物耳。

translations.literal: Later, traveling to Lai Township, he passed Laozi's shrine; all of it was the place the envoys had brought him when he was dead, only he no longer saw the things of former times.
translations.idiomatic: Later, passing through Lai village, he recognized Laozi's shrine as the very post he had held among the shades—only the old scenery was gone.

sentences.zh: 因問守藏應鳳曰：「去二十餘年，嘗有人乘馬東行，過老君而不下馬，未達橋，墜馬死者不？

translations.literal: Thereupon he asked the keeper Ying Feng, "More than twenty years ago, was there not someone who rode a horse eastward, passed the Lord Lao without dismounting, and before reaching the bridge fell from his horse and died?
translations.idiomatic: He asked the custodian Ying Feng whether, twenty years earlier, a rider bound east had refused to dismount at the Lao shrine and had been thrown dead before the bridge.

sentences.zh: 」鳳言有之。

translations.literal: Feng said there was such a case.
translations.idiomatic: Feng confirmed it.

sentences.zh: 所問之事，多與洋同。

translations.literal: The matters he asked about largely matched what Yang had said.
translations.idiomatic: The details matched Dai Yang's own memory.

sentences.zh: 揚州刺史嘗問吉凶於洋，答曰：「熒惑入南斗，八月有暴水，九月當有客軍西南來。

translations.literal: The governor of Yang Province once asked Yang about good and ill fortune; he answered, "Mars has entered the Southern Dipper; in the eighth month there will be violent flooding; in the ninth month a guest army will come from the southwest.
translations.idiomatic: The Yangzhou governor sought his counsel. Dai Yang replied, "Mars sits in the Southern Dipper: violent floods in the eighth month, an alien army from the southwest in the ninth."

sentences.zh: 」如期果大水，而石冰作亂。

translations.literal: At the appointed time there was indeed great flooding, and Shi Bing rose in rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: The floods came; Shi Bing's revolt followed.

sentences.zh: 冰既據揚州，洋謂人曰：「視賊雲氣，四月當破。

translations.literal: After Bing had occupied Yang Province, Yang said to people, "Looking at the rebels' cloud-qi, in the fourth month they will be broken.
translations.idiomatic: Once Shi Bing held Yangzhou, Dai Yang said, "Their vapors show collapse in the fourth month."

sentences.zh: 」果如其言。

translations.literal: It indeed happened as he said.
translations.idiomatic: So it proved.

sentences.zh: 時陳敏為右將軍，堂邑令孫混見而羨之。

translations.literal: At the time Chen Min was General of the Right, and Sun Hun, magistrate of Tangyi, saw him and envied him.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Min was then General of the Right; Sun Hun, magistrate of Tangyi, saw him and burned with envy.

sentences.zh: 洋曰：「敏當作賊族滅，何足願也！

translations.literal: Yang said, "Min will become a rebel and his clan will be exterminated—what is there to envy!
translations.idiomatic: Dai Yang said, "Chen Min will turn bandit and wipe out his kin—hardly a model to envy!"

sentences.zh: 」未幾，敏果反而誅焉。

translations.literal: Before long Min indeed rebelled and was executed.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Chen Min revolted and paid with his life.

sentences.zh: 初，混欲迎其家累，洋曰：「此地當敗，得臘不得正，豈可移家於賊中乎！

translations.literal: At first Hun wished to bring his family dependents; Yang said, "This place is about to fall; one may reach the La festival but not the New Year—how can one move a household into the midst of rebels!
translations.idiomatic: Sun Hun meant to fetch his family; Dai Yang warned, "This county is lost: you might survive to Laba, not to New Year's Day—why drag kin into a rebel nest?"

sentences.zh: 」混便止。

translations.literal: Hun then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Hun dropped the plan.

sentences.zh: 歲末，敏弟昶攻堂邑，混遂以單身走免。

translations.literal: At year's end Min's younger brother Chang attacked Tangyi, and Hun then fled alone and escaped.
translations.idiomatic: At year's end Chen Min's brother Chang stormed Tangyi, and Hun escaped alone.

sentences.zh: 其後都水馬武舉洋為都水令史，洋請急還鄉。

translations.literal: Afterward Ma Wu of the Directorate of Waters recommended Yang as clerk in the directorate; Yang requested emergency leave to return to his village.
translations.idiomatic: Later Ma Wu of the waterways office nominated him clerk; Dai Yang begged leave and went home.

sentences.zh: 將赴洛，夢神人謂之曰：「洛中當敗，人盡南渡，後五年揚州必有天子。

translations.literal: About to go to Luo, he dreamed a spirit told him, "Luoyang is about to collapse; everyone will flee south; after five years Yang Province is sure to have a Son of Heaven."
translations.idiomatic: As he prepared for Luoyang, a spirit in a dream said, "The capital will fall and the people stream south; within five years a Son of Heaven will arise in Yangzhou."

sentences.zh: 」洋信之，遂不去。

translations.literal: Yang believed it and therefore did not go.
translations.idiomatic: He believed the dream and stayed.

sentences.zh: 既而皆如其夢。

translations.literal: Afterward everything was as in his dream.
translations.idiomatic: Events matched the dream.

sentences.zh: 廬江太守華譚問洋曰：「天下誰當復作賊者？

translations.literal: Hua Tan, governor of Lujiang, asked Yang, "Who in the realm will next become a rebel?
translations.idiomatic: Lujiang governor Hua Tan asked who would next rise in arms.

sentences.zh: 」洋曰：「王機。

translations.literal: Yang said, "Wang Ji."
translations.idiomatic: "Wang Ji," said Dai Yang.

sentences.zh: 」尋而機反。

translations.literal: Before long Ji rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ji soon mutinied.

sentences.zh: 陳眕問洋曰：「人言江南當有貴人，顧彥先、周宣珮當是不？

translations.literal: Chen Zhen asked Yang, "People say a noble man will appear south of the Yangzi—would that not be Gu Yanxian and Zhou Xuanpei?
translations.idiomatic: Chen Zhen asked whether Gu Rong and Zhou Pei were the destined worthies of the south.

sentences.zh: 」洋曰：「顧不及臘，周不見來年八月。

translations.literal: Yang said, "Gu will not last past La; Zhou will not see the eighth month of next year."
translations.idiomatic: Dai Yang answered, "Gu will not outlive Laba; Zhou will not see the eighth month next year."

sentences.zh: 」榮果以十二月十七日卒，十九日臘，珮以明年七月晦亡。

translations.literal: Rong indeed died on the seventeenth day of the twelfth month, the nineteenth being La; Pei died on the last day of the seventh month the next year.
translations.idiomatic: Gu Rong died on the seventeenth of the twelfth month, two days before Laba; Zhou Pei died on the last day of the seventh month the following year.

sentences.zh: 王導遇病，召洋問之。

translations.literal: Wang Dao fell ill and summoned Yang to question him.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dao took sick and called Dai Yang in.

sentences.zh: 洋曰：「君侯本命在申，金為土使之主，而于申上石頭立冶，火光照天，此為金火相爍，水火相煎，以故受害耳。

translations.literal: Yang said, "Your lordship's natal stem-branch is shen; metal is the ruler dispatched by earth, yet on shen they have raised a smelting furnace at Stone Citadel with fire light shining to heaven—this is metal and fire scorching each other, water and fire tormenting each other; for this reason you suffer harm.
translations.idiomatic: Dai Yang said, "Your honor's fate sits in shen; metal serves earth, yet atop shen at Stone Citadel they run a foundry whose glare scorches the sky—metal and fire wear each other down, water and fire clash—hence your illness."

sentences.zh: 」導即移居東府，病遂差。

translations.literal: Dao thereupon moved his residence to the Eastern Offices, and his illness then improved.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dao moved to the Eastern Quarter and recovered.

sentences.zh: 鎮東從事中郎張闓舉洋為丞相令史。

translations.literal: Zhang Kai, adjutant in the Army on the East, recommended Yang as clerk to the chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: Eastern headquarters adjutant Zhang Kai nominated him chancellor's clerk.

sentences.zh: 時司馬颺為烏程令，將赴職，洋曰：「君宜深慎下吏。

translations.literal: At the time Sima Yang was magistrate of Wucheng, about to take up his post; Yang said, "You ought to be deeply wary of subordinate clerks.
translations.idiomatic: When Sima Yang was leaving for Wucheng magistrate, Dai Yang warned, "Guard against petty clerks."

sentences.zh: 」揚後果坐吏免官。

translations.literal: Yang later indeed lost office because of clerks.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Yang later lost his post through clerkly malfeasance.

sentences.zh: 洋又謂曰：「卿雖免官，十一月當作郡，加將軍。

translations.literal: Yang also said to him, "Although you have lost office, in the eleventh month you will become governor and receive general's rank."
translations.idiomatic: Dai Yang added, "Even dismissed, in the eleventh month you will take a command and general's title."

sentences.zh: 」至期，為太山太守、鎮武將軍。

translations.literal: When the time came, he became governor of Taishan and General Who Guards Might.
translations.idiomatic: He became Taishan governor and Guarding-Might general on schedule.

sentences.zh: 颺賣宅將行，洋止之曰：「君不得至，當還，不可無宅。

translations.literal: Yang was selling his house about to depart; Yang stopped him, saying, "You will not reach your post but will return—you cannot be without a house.
translations.idiomatic: As Sima Yang sold his house to leave, Dai Yang stopped him: "You will never reach the post and will need a roof when you turn back."

sentences.zh: 」颺果為徐龕所逼，不得之郡。

translations.literal: Yang was indeed pressed by Xu Kan and could not reach the commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Kan blocked him; he never took up the governorship.

sentences.zh: 元帝增颺眾二千，使助祖逖。

translations.literal: Emperor Yuan added two thousand men to Yang's forces to help Zu Ti.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yuan gave him two thousand extra troops to reinforce Zu Ti.

sentences.zh: 洋勸颺不行，颺乃稱疾。

translations.literal: Yang urged Yang not to go; Yang then pleaded illness.
translations.idiomatic: Dai Yang urged refusal; Sima Yang pleaded sick instead.

sentences.zh: 收付廷尉，俄而因赦得出。

translations.literal: He was seized and handed to the commandant of justice; before long he was released because of an amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: He was jailed at the commandant of justice, then freed by a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 元帝將登阼，使洋擇日，洋以為宜用三月二十四日丙午。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yuan was about to ascend the throne, he had Yang choose a day; Yang held that the third month, twenty-fourth day, bingwu, should be used.
translations.idiomatic: As Emperor Yuan prepared to take the throne, Dai Yang chose the bing-wu day, the twenty-fourth of the third month.

sentences.zh: 太史令陳卓奏用二十二日，言：「昔越王用甲辰三月反國，范蠡稱在陽之前，當主盡出，上下盡空，德將出遊，刑入中宮，今與此同。

translations.literal: Astrological Director Chen Zhuo memorialized to use the twenty-second day, saying, "In olden times the King of Yue, on jiachen in the third month, returned to his state; Fan Li said that before yang it would 'make the ruler all go out, above and below all empty, virtue about to go wandering, punishment entering the central palace'—now it is the same as that.
translations.idiomatic: Grand astrologer Chen Zhuo urged the twenty-second, citing the Yue king's jia-chen third-month return and Fan Li's doctrine of empty courts and wandering virtue—claiming this day matched that case.

sentences.zh: 」洋曰：「越王為吳所囚，雖當時遜媚，實懷怨憤，蠡故用甲辰，乘德而歸，留刑吳宮。

translations.literal: Yang said, "The King of Yue was imprisoned by Wu; although at the time he was submissive and ingratiating, in truth he harbored resentment and indignation; therefore Fan used jiachen, riding virtue to return and leaving punishment in Wu's palace.
translations.idiomatic: Dai Yang objected: "The Yue king was Wu's prisoner; his humility masked rage, so Fan Li chose jia-chen to ride auspicious force home while leaving ill omen in Wu's court."

sentences.zh: 今大王內無含咎，外無怨憤，當承天洪命，納祚無窮，何為追越王去國留殃故事邪！

translations.literal: Now the great king within has no inward fault, without has no resentment and indignation; he should receive Heaven's great mandate and admit blessing without end—why pursue the former king of Yue's tale of leaving the state and leaving behind calamity!
translations.idiomatic: Our prince bears no hidden guilt and nurses no outer grievance; he accepts heaven's great charge and boundless fortune—why copy a defeated king's ill-starred precedent?"

sentences.zh: 」乃從之。

translations.literal: Thereupon they followed him.
translations.idiomatic: The court followed Dai Yang's date.

sentences.zh: 及祖約代兄鎮譙，請洋為中典軍，遷督護。

translations.literal: When Zu Yue succeeded his elder brother in garrisoning Qiao, he invited Yang as central army aide and promoted him to protector.
translations.idiomatic: When Zu Yue replaced his brother on the Qiao garrison, he took Dai Yang as central-army aide and raised him to protector.

sentences.zh: 四月庚辰，禺中時有大風，起自東南，折木。

translations.literal: On gengchen in the fourth month, at the yuzhong double-hour, a great wind rose from the southeast and broke trees.
translations.idiomatic: On geng-chen in the fourth month, at mid-morning, a gale from the southeast snapped trees.

sentences.zh: 洋謂約曰：「十月必有賊到譙城東，至曆陽，南方有反者。

translations.literal: Yang said to Yue, "In the tenth month bandits are sure to reach east of Qiao city, as far as Liyang; in the south there will be one who rebels.
translations.idiomatic: He told Zu Yue, "In the tenth month raiders will reach the east of Qiao and push to Liyang; someone in the south will turn traitor."

sentences.zh: 」主簿王振以洋為妖，白約收洋，付刺奸而絕其食五十日，言語如故。

translations.literal: The chief clerk Wang Zhen, taking Yang for a sorcerer, reported to Yue to seize Yang, hand him to the scourge of malfeasance office, and cut off his food for fifty days—yet his speech was as before.
translations.idiomatic: Chief clerk Wang Zhen called it witchcraft and had him jailed without food fifty days—yet he spoke as clearly as ever.

sentences.zh: 約知其有神術，乃赦之而讓振。

translations.literal: Yue knew he had spirit techniques, thereupon pardoned him and rebuked Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: Zu Yue saw his power, freed him, and scolded Wang Zhen.

sentences.zh: 振後有罪被收，洋救之。

translations.literal: Later Zhen committed an offense and was seized; Yang saved him.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhen later fell foul of the law, Dai Yang interceded.

sentences.zh: 約曰：「振往日相系，今何以救之？

translations.literal: Yue said, "In days past Zhen bound you—why now save him?
translations.idiomatic: Zu Yue asked why he would save a man who had bound him.

sentences.zh: 」洋曰：「振不識風角，非有宿嫌。

translations.literal: Yang said, "Zhen did not understand fengjiao; there was no old grudge.
translations.idiomatic: Dai Yang replied, "He did not understand wind-angle; there was no deep feud."

sentences.zh: 振往時垂餓死，洋養活之，振猶尚遺忘。

translations.literal: In former times when Zhen was about to starve to death, Yang nourished and kept him alive; Zhen still forgot.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhen nearly starved, I fed him—memory is short in the prosperous toward the poor."

sentences.zh: 夫處富貴而不棄貧賤甚難。

translations.literal: For one in wealth and honor not to cast aside the poor and lowly is very difficult."
translations.idiomatic: It is rare for the rich to remember the humble."

sentences.zh: 」約義之，即原振，賜洋米三十石。

translations.literal: Yue deemed him righteous, thereupon pardoned Zhen and granted Yang thirty shi of rice.
translations.idiomatic: Zu Yue honored the sentiment, spared Zhen, and gave Dai Yang thirty shi of rice.

sentences.zh: 至十月三日，石勒騎果到譙城東。

translations.literal: When it reached the third day of the tenth month, Shi Le's cavalry indeed arrived east of Qiao city.
translations.idiomatic: On the third of the tenth month Shi Le's horsemen appeared east of Qiao, exactly as Dai Yang had said.

sentences.zh: 洋言於約曰：「賊必向城父，可遣騎水南追之，步軍于水北斷要路，賊必敗。

translations.literal: Yang spoke to Yue, saying, "The bandits are sure to head toward Chengfu; you may dispatch cavalry south of the river to pursue them, and infantry north of the river to cut off the vital roads—the bandits will certainly be defeated."
translations.idiomatic: Dai Yang urged Zu Yue: "They will make for Chengfu—send horse south of the water to chase them, foot north of the water to block the choke points, and you will shatter them."

sentences.zh: 」約竟不追，賊乃掠城父婦女輜重而去。

translations.literal: Yue in the end did not pursue, and the bandits then plundered the women and dependents and baggage train of Chengfu and departed.
translations.idiomatic: Zu Yue refused to move; the raiders looted Chengfu's families and baggage and rode away.

sentences.zh: 約將魯延求追賊，洋曰：「不可。

translations.literal: Yue's general Lu Yan requested to pursue the bandits; Yang said, "It cannot be done."
translations.idiomatic: General Lu Yan begged leave to pursue; Dai Yang said no.

sentences.zh: 」約不從，使兄子智與延追之。

translations.literal: Yue did not follow this; he sent his elder brother's son Zhi together with Yan to pursue them.
translations.idiomatic: Zu Yue overruled him, sending his nephew Zhi with Lu Yan in pursuit.

sentences.zh: 賊偽棄婦女輜重走，智與延等爭物，賊還掩之，智、延僅以身免，士卒皆死。

translations.literal: The bandits feigned abandoning women, dependents, and baggage train and fled; Zhi and Yan and the others contended for the goods; the bandits returned and ambushed them—Zhi and Yan barely escaped with their lives, while the soldiers all died.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy dropped camp followers and wagons as bait; Zhi and Yan fell to squabbling over the spoil; the riders wheeled back and cut them down—only the two leaders lived.

sentences.zh: 約表洋為下邑長。

translations.literal: Yue memorialized to appoint Yang as magistrate of Xiayi.
translations.idiomatic: Zu Yue had him named magistrate of Lower Yi county.

sentences.zh: 時梁國人反，逐太守袁晏。

translations.literal: At the time the people of Liang state rebelled and drove out their governor Yuan Yan.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Liang princedom rose and expelled Governor Yuan Yan.

sentences.zh: 梁城峻險，約欲討之而未決，洋曰：「賊以八月辛酉日反，日辰俱王，辛德在南方，酉受自刑，梁在譙北，乘德伐刑，賊必破亡。

translations.literal: Liang city was steep and perilous; Yue wished to chastise them but had not decided; Yang said, "The bandits rebelled on xinyou day in the eighth month; day and hour stem are both wang; xin 's virtue lies in the south, you ' receives self-punishment; Liang lies north of Qiao—riding virtue to attack punishment, the bandits are sure to be destroyed."
translations.idiomatic: Liang's walls were formidable; Zu Yue hesitated. Dai Yang read the calendar: the rebels chose xin-you, stems at full strength; xin's power points south while you turns on itself; Liang sits north of Qiao—virtue striking self-destruction means their ruin.

sentences.zh: 又甲子日東風而雷西行，譙在東南，雷在軍前，為軍驅除。

translations.literal: Moreover on jiazi day the east wind blew while thunder moved westward; Qiao lies southeast; thunder is before the army—it is the army's clearing away.
translations.idiomatic: On a jia-zi day an east wind carried thunder west—Qiao lies southeast of that path, thunder marching ahead of the host clears the way.

sentences.zh: 昔吳伐關羽，天雷在前，周瑜拜賀。

translations.literal: Formerly when Wu attacked Guan Yu, heaven's thunder was in front, and Zhou Yu bowed in congratulation.
translations.idiomatic: When Wu struck Guan Yu, lightning led the van and Zhou Yu hailed it as a good omen.

sentences.zh: 今與往同，故知必克。

translations.literal: Now it is the same as in the past; therefore I know we are sure to prevail.
translations.idiomatic: The signs match that campaign—we cannot lose.

sentences.zh: 」約從之，果平梁城。

translations.literal: Yue followed him, and indeed pacified Liang city.
translations.idiomatic: Zu Yue attacked and took Liang as predicted.

sentences.zh: 正月，有大流星東南行，洋曰：「至秋，府當移壽陽。

translations.literal: In the first month a great meteor traveled southeastward; Yang said, "By autumn the headquarters will shift to Shouyang."
translations.idiomatic: A bolide streaked southeast; Dai Yang said the command post would relocate to Shouyang by autumn.

sentences.zh: 」及王敦作逆，約問其勝敗，洋曰：「太白在東方，辰星不出。

translations.literal: When Wang Dun acted rebelliously, Yue asked about victory and defeat; Yang said, "The Great White is in the east; the Chronograph Star does not appear.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Dun rebelled, Zu Yue asked the outcome. Dai Yang answered: Venus shines in the east while Mercury stays hidden.

sentences.zh: 兵法先起為主，應者為客。

translations.literal: In military doctrine he who rises first is host, he who responds is guest.
translations.idiomatic: In the art of war the first mover is host, the reactor guest.

sentences.zh: 辰星若出，太白為主，辰星為客。

translations.literal: If the Chronograph Star appears, the Great White is host and the Chronograph Star is guest.
translations.idiomatic: Were Mercury to show, Venus would be host and Mercury guest.

sentences.zh: 辰星不出，太白為客，先起兵者敗。

translations.literal: If the Chronograph Star does not appear, the Great White is guest—he who first raises troops will be defeated.
translations.idiomatic: With Mercury absent, Venus plays guest—whoever strikes first loses.

sentences.zh: 今有客無主，有前無後，宜傳檄所部，應詔伐之。

translations.literal: Now there is a guest without a host, there is a front without a rear—you ought to circulate proclamations through your command and, answering the imperial summons, campaign against him."
translations.idiomatic: Today the stars show a guest with no host, a van with no rear—issue orders through your army and march under the edict to crush him."

sentences.zh: 」約乃率眾向合肥。

translations.literal: Yue thereupon led his host toward Hefei.
translations.idiomatic: Zu Yue marched on Hefei.

sentences.zh: 俄而敦死眾敗，遂住壽陽。

translations.literal: Before long Dun died and his host was defeated, and he then stayed at Shouyang.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dun soon died and his army collapsed; Zu Yue ended up holding Shouyang.

sentences.zh: 洋又曰：「江淮之間當有軍事，譙城虛曠，宜還固守。

translations.literal: Yang also said, "Between the Yangzi and Huai there will be military affairs; Qiao city is empty and open—you ought to return and defend it firmly.
translations.idiomatic: Dai Yang added: "War is coming to the Jiang-Huai belt; Qiao stands empty—pull back and hold it fast."

sentences.zh: 不者，雍丘、沛皆非官有也。

translations.literal: If not, Yongqiu and Pei will both no longer be in official hands."
translations.idiomatic: Otherwise neither Yongqiu nor Pei will stay yours."

sentences.zh: 」約不從，豫土遂陷於賊。

translations.literal: Yue did not follow this, and the lands of Yu then fell into the hands of bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Zu Yue ignored him and lost the Yu region to the enemy.

sentences.zh: 春，約南行佃，遇大雷雨西南來，洋曰：「甲子西南天雷，其夏必失大將。

translations.literal: In spring Yue went south to farm the fields and met a great thunderstorm coming from the southwest; Yang said, "Jiazi with heaven's thunder in the southwest—this summer a great general is sure to be lost."
translations.idiomatic: That spring Zu Yue went south to camp and met a thunderstorm from the southwest. Dai Yang said a jia-zi thunderbolt from the southwest foretold the loss of a top commander that summer.

sentences.zh: 」至夏，汝南人反，執約兄子濟，送于石勒。

translations.literal: When summer came, the people of Runan rebelled, seized Yue's elder brother's son Ji, and delivered him to Shi Le.
translations.idiomatic: By summer Runan had risen, seized Zu Yue's nephew Ji, and handed him to Shi Le.

sentences.zh: 約府內地忽赤如丹，洋曰：「案《河圖徵》云：『地赤如丹血丸丸，當有下反上者。

translations.literal: Inside Yue's headquarters the ground suddenly became red as cinnabar; Yang said, "According to the Hetu zheng, 'When the earth is red as cinnabar like blood pellets, there will be one below who rebels against those above.
translations.idiomatic: The soil inside Zu Yue's yamen flushed red as lacquer. Dai Yang cited the River Chart augury: crimson earth like bloody pearls means subjects will turn on their lords.

sentences.zh: 』恐十月二十七日胡馬當來飲淮水。

translations.literal: I fear that on the twenty-seventh day of the tenth month Hu horses will come to drink from the Huai River."
translations.idiomatic: I fear barbarian horses will water in the Huai on the twenty-seventh of the tenth month."

sentences.zh: 」至時，石勒騎大至，攻城大戰。

translations.literal: When the time came, Shi Le's cavalry arrived in great numbers and besieged the city in great battle.
translations.idiomatic: On that day Shi Le's cavalry swarmed in and stormed the walls.

sentences.zh: 其日西風，兵火俱發，約大懼。

translations.literal: That day the wind blew from the west; weapons and fire both broke out; Yue was greatly frightened.
translations.idiomatic: A west wind rose; blades and flames mingled; Zu Yue panicked.

sentences.zh: 會風回，賊退。

translations.literal: Just then the wind shifted and the bandits withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Then the gale veered and the besiegers drew off.

sentences.zh: 時傳言勒遣騎向壽陽，約欲送其家還江東，洋曰：「必無此事。

translations.literal: At the time rumor said Le was sending cavalry toward Shouyang; Yue wished to send his family back east of the Yangzi; Yang said, "There is assuredly no such matter."
translations.idiomatic: Rumors claimed Shi Le aimed at Shouyang; Zu Yue meant to evacuate his kin across the river. Dai Yang said the tale was false.

sentences.zh: 」尋而傳言果妄。

translations.literal: Before long the rumor indeed proved false.
translations.idiomatic: The rumor soon collapsed.

sentences.zh: 咸和初，月暈左角，有赤白珥。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xianhe, the moon had a halo on its left horn with red and white ear-threads.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Xian-he era a lunar halo ringed the moon's left horn with red and white spikes.

sentences.zh: 約問洋，洋曰：「角為天門，開布陽道，官門當有大戰。

translations.literal: Yue asked Yang; Yang said, "The horn is Heaven's Gate; it opens out the yang road—there will be a great battle at the palace gates.
translations.idiomatic: Zu Yue asked its meaning. Dai Yang said the horn is Heaven's Gate opening the solar path—expect a major clash at the palace gates.

sentences.zh: 」俄而蘇峻遣使招約俱反，洋謂約曰：「蘇峻必敗，然其初起，兵鋒不可當，可外和內嚴，以待其變。

translations.literal: Before long Su Jun sent envoys to summon Yue to rebel together; Yang said to Yue, "Su Jun is sure to be defeated, yet at his first rise his army's edge cannot be withstood—you may outwardly conciliate while inwardly tightening guard, awaiting his transformation.
translations.idiomatic: Su Jun soon invited Zu Yue into revolt. Dai Yang warned that Su must fail yet his first rush would be unstoppable—feign peace, steel the defenses, and wait for his slide.

sentences.zh: 」約不從，遂與峻反。

translations.literal: Yue did not follow this, and therefore joined Jun in rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Zu Yue refused the counsel and joined Su Jun.

sentences.zh: 至三年五月，大風雷雨西北來，城內晦螟，洋謂約曰：「雷鳴人上，明使君當遠佞近直，愛下振貧。

translations.literal: When it reached the fifth month of the third year, a great wind and thunderstorm came from the northwest; inside the city it was dark as midnight; Yang said to Yue, "When thunder sounds above men, it means the enlightened lord should distance sycophants and draw near the upright, cherish subordinates and relieve the poor.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of year three a northwest storm plunged the city into utter darkness. Dai Yang said thunder rolling over men tells a governor to banish flatterers, embrace honest men, cherish troops, and succor the needy.

sentences.zh: 昔秦有此變，卒致亂亡。

translations.literal: Formerly Qin had this transformation and in the end encountered chaos and perish.
translations.idiomatic: Qin once saw the same sign and soon fell to chaos.

sentences.zh: 」約大怒，收洋系之。

translations.literal: Yue was greatly angered, seized Yang, and bound him.
translations.idiomatic: Zu Yue, enraged, had Dai Yang arrested and bound.

sentences.zh: 遣部將李概將兵到盧江，其眾盡散。

translations.literal: He sent his division commander Li Gai to lead troops to Lujiang, and his host entirely scattered.
translations.idiomatic: He dispatched Li Gai toward Lujiang; the column melted away.

sentences.zh: 約召洋出，問之曰：「吾還東何如留壽陽？

translations.literal: Yue summoned Yang out and questioned him, saying, "How is it if I return east versus staying at Shouyang?
translations.idiomatic: Zu Yue released Dai Yang and asked whether to retreat east or remain in Shouyang.

sentences.zh: 若留壽陽，何如入胡？

translations.literal: If I stay at Shouyang, how is it compared to entering among the Hu?
translations.idiomatic: If he stayed in Shouyang, how would that compare to throwing in with the barbarians?

sentences.zh: 」洋曰：「東入失半，入胡滅門，留壽陽尚可。

translations.literal: Yang said, "Going east you lose half; entering among the Hu exterminates the whole household; staying at Shouyang is still tolerable."
translations.idiomatic: Dai Yang replied: flight east costs half your following; submission to the Hu wipes out your line; holding Shouyang is the least ill choice.

sentences.zh: 」約欲東向曆陽，其眾不樂東下，皆叛約，劫約姊及嫂奔于石勒。

translations.literal: Yue wished to go east toward Liyang; his host was not pleased to go east and all rebelled against Yue, kidnapping Yue's elder sister and sister-in-law and fleeing to Shi Le.
translations.idiomatic: Zu Yue tried for Liyang; his men refused the eastern march, mutinied, and carried his sister and sister-in-law off to Shi Le.

sentences.zh: 約到曆陽，祖煥問洋曰：「君昔言平西在壽陽可得五年，果如君言。

translations.literal: When Yue reached Liyang, Zu Huan asked Yang, "Formerly you said the Pingxi commander could hold Shouyang for five years, and it indeed matched your words.
translations.idiomatic: At Liyang Zu Huan reminded Dai Yang: "You once said the Pingxi general could keep Shouyang five years, and you were right.

sentences.zh: 今在曆陽，可得幾時？

translations.literal: Now that he is at Liyang, how long can he have?
translations.idiomatic: Now that he is in Liyang, how long does he have?"

sentences.zh: 」洋曰：「得六月耳。

translations.literal: Yang said, "He obtains six months only."
translations.idiomatic: "Six months, no more," said Dai Yang.

sentences.zh: 」約問洋：「台下及此氣侯何如？

translations.literal: Yue asked Yang, "How are matters below the terraces and the qi signs here?
translations.idiomatic: Zu Yue pressed him about the capital and local omens.

sentences.zh: 」洋曰：「此當復有反者。

translations.literal: Yang said, "Here there will again be one who rebels.
translations.idiomatic: Dai Yang said another rising would strike this region.

sentences.zh: 台下來年三月當太平，江州當大喪。

translations.literal: Below the terraces next year's third month will be at peace; Jiang Province will have a great mourning.
translations.idiomatic: The capital will quiet down by the third month next year, but Jiangzhou will suffer a great bereavement.

sentences.zh: 後南方復有軍事，去此千里。

translations.literal: Afterward in the south there will again be military affairs a thousand li from here.
translations.idiomatic: Later fighting will flare again a thousand li to the south.

sentences.zh: 」尋而牽騰叛約，約率所親將家屬奔于石勒。

translations.literal: Before long Qian Teng rebelled against Yue; Yue led those close to him, taking family dependents, and fled to Shi Le.
translations.idiomatic: Qian Teng soon mutinied; Zu Yue fled with kinsmen into Shi Le's camp.

sentences.zh: 二月而天子反正，四月而溫嶠卒，郭默據湓口以叛。

translations.literal: In the second month the Son of Heaven returned to normal rule; in the fourth month Wen Jiao died; Guo Mo occupied Penkou in rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: The second month saw the emperor restored; the fourth brought Wen Jiao's death and Guo Mo's seizure of Penkou.

sentences.zh: 後勒誅約及親屬並盡，皆如洋言。

translations.literal: Later Le executed Yue and his kin to the last person—all as Yang had said.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Le later executed Zu Yue and his entire clan, just as Dai Yang foretold.

sentences.zh: 約既敗，洋往尋陽。

translations.literal: After Yue was defeated, Yang went to Xunyang.
translations.idiomatic: When Zu Yue fell, Dai Yang went to Xunyang.

sentences.zh: 時劉胤鎮尋陽，胤問洋曰：「我病當差不？

translations.literal: At the time Liu Yin garrisoned Xunyang; Yin asked Yang, "Will my illness get better?
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yin, then holding Xunyang, asked whether his illness would mend.

sentences.zh: 」洋曰：「不憂使君不差，憂使君今年有大厄。

translations.literal: Yang said, "I do not worry that the lord will not recover; I worry that the lord has a great calamity this year.
translations.idiomatic: Dai Yang said he did not fear the sickness lingering but feared a mortal stroke within the year.

sentences.zh: 使君年四十七，行年入庚寅。

translations.literal: The lord is forty-seven years of age; his annual cycle enters gengyin.
translations.idiomatic: You are forty-seven; your yearly star enters geng-yin.

sentences.zh: 《太公陰謀》曰：『六庚為白獸，在上為客星，在下為害氣。

translations.literal: The Taigong yinmou says, 'The six geng are the White Beast; above they are the guest star, below they are the baleful qi.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Duke's Secret Stratagem says the six geng days are the White Beast—above as guest stars, below as injurious vapor.

sentences.zh: 』年與命並，必凶當忌。

translations.literal: When the year and fate coincide, it is surely inauspicious and must be guarded against.
translations.idiomatic: When the year-star meets your fate, disaster follows—beware.

sentences.zh: 十二月二十二日庚寅勿見客。

translations.literal: On the twenty-second day of the twelfth month, gengyin, do not receive guests."
translations.idiomatic: On the twenty-second of the twelfth month, a geng-yin day, admit no visitors."

sentences.zh: 」胤曰：「我當解職，將君還野中治病。

translations.literal: Yin said, "I shall resign my post and take you back to the wilds to treat the illness.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yin answered that he would resign and take Dai Yang home to cure him.

sentences.zh: 」洋曰：「使君當作江州，不得解職。

translations.literal: Yang said, "The lord will hold Jiang Province; you cannot resign the post.
translations.idiomatic: Dai Yang replied, "You are destined to govern Jiangzhou—you cannot step down.

sentences.zh: 」胤曰：「溫公不復還邪？

translations.literal: Yin said, "Will Lord Wen not return?
translations.idiomatic: Will Wen Qiao not come back?"

sentences.zh: 」洋曰：「溫公雖還，使君故作江州。

translations.literal: Yang said, "Although Lord Wen returns, the lord will still hold Jiang Province.
translations.idiomatic: Even if Wen Qiao returns, you will still take Jiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 」俄如其言。

translations.literal: Before long it was as he said.
translations.idiomatic: It unfolded exactly so.

sentences.zh: 九月甲寅申時，回風從東來，入胤兒船中，西過，狀如匹練，長五六丈。

translations.literal: On jiayin in the ninth month at the shen double-hour, a whirlwind came from the east, entered the boat of Yin's son, passed westward, shaped like a bolt of plain silk five or six zhang long.
translations.idiomatic: On jia-yin of the ninth month at mid-afternoon a whirlwind from the east struck Liu Yin's son's boat, then swept west in a band five or six zhang like white silk.

sentences.zh: 洋曰：「風從咸池下來，攝提下去，咸池為刀兵，大殺為死喪。

translations.literal: Yang said, "The wind came down from the Xianchi pool, the Sheti handle going down; Xianchi is blades and weapons, the great killing is death and mourning.
translations.idiomatic: Dai Yang read it: wind dropped from the celestial Xianchi while Sheti sank—Xianchi means arms, the Great Kill means death.

sentences.zh: 到甲子日申時，府內大聚骨理之。

translations.literal: When it reaches jiazi day at the shen double-hour, inside the headquarters they will greatly gather bones and bury them.
translations.idiomatic: On the next jia-zi day at the shen hour the yamen will heap bones for burial.

sentences.zh: 胤問在何處，洋曰：「不出州府門也。

translations.literal: Yin asked where; Yang said, "It will not go outside the province headquarters gate."
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yin asked where; Dai Yang said within the governor's gate.

sentences.zh: 」胤架府東門。

translations.literal: Yin erected the eastern gate of the headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yin kept the compound's east gate open as the main entrance.

sentences.zh: 洋又曰：「東為天牢，牢下開門，憂天獄至。

translations.literal: Yang also said, "East is Heaven's Prison; below the prison the gate opens—worry that Heaven's Jail arrives.
translations.idiomatic: Dai Yang added: east is the celestial prison—open its gate and the jail star enters.

sentences.zh: 」十二月十七日，洋又曰：「臘近可閉門，以五十人備守，並以百人備東北寅上，以卻害氣。

translations.literal: On the seventeenth day of the twelfth month Yang again said, "La is near; you can close the gates, prepare fifty men on guard, and also station a hundred men northeast on the yin position above, to repel the baleful qi.
translations.idiomatic: On the seventeenth of the twelfth month he urged: with Laba near, seal the gates, post fifty defenders plus a hundred on the northeast yin corner to turn the baleful vapor.

sentences.zh: 」胤不從。

translations.literal: Yin did not follow this.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yin ignored him.

sentences.zh: 二十四日壬辰，胤遂為郭默所害。

translations.literal: On renchen the twenty-fourth day, Yin was then killed by Guo Mo.
translations.idiomatic: On ren-chen, the twenty-fourth, Guo Mo murdered Liu Yin.

sentences.zh: 南中郎將桓宣以洋為參軍，將隨宣往襄陽，太尉陶侃留之住武昌。

translations.literal: General of the Center Army Huan Xuan appointed Yang as aide and was about to take Yang with Xuan to Xiangyang, but Grand Commandant Tao Kan detained him to stay at Wuchang.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Xuan, South Center general, took Dai Yang as aide for a march to Xiangyang, but Tao Kan kept him in Wuchang.

sentences.zh: 時侃謀北伐，洋曰：「前年十一月熒惑守胃昴，至今年四月，積五百餘日。

translations.literal: At the time Kan planned a northern expedition; Yang said, "In the eleventh month of the year before last Mars guarded Mao and the Pleiades; until this year's fourth month it accumulated more than five hundred days.
translations.idiomatic: As Tao Kan planned a northern push, Dai Yang noted Mars had lingered in Mao and the Pleiades since last year's eleventh month—over five hundred days by the fourth month.

sentences.zh: 昴，趙之分野，石勒遂死。

translations.literal: Mao is the field division of Zhao; Shi Le thereupon died.
translations.idiomatic: Mao marks Zhao's astrological field—Shi Le died under that sign.

sentences.zh: 熒惑以七月退，從畢右順行入黃道，未及天關，以八月二十二日復逆行還鉤，繞畢向昴。

translations.literal: Mars in the seventh month retired, from Bi's right proceeding smoothly into the Yellow Road; before reaching the Celestial Pass, on the twenty-second day of the eighth month it again retrograded back to the Hook, circling Bi toward the Pleiades.
translations.idiomatic: Mars withdrew in the seventh month, sliding right of Bi into the ecliptic; before reaching the Celestial Gate it turned retrograde on the twenty-second of the eighth, looping the Hook and wrapping Bi toward the Pleiades.

sentences.zh: 昴畢為邊兵，主胡夷，故置天弓以射之。

translations.literal: The Pleiades and Bi are frontier troops, governing the Hu and Yi; therefore Heaven sets the Bow to shoot them.
translations.idiomatic: Bi and the Pleiades mean border war and barbarians—heaven strings the bow to shoot them.

sentences.zh: 熒惑逆行，司無德之國，石勒死是也。

translations.literal: Mars retrograding punishes states without virtue—Shi Le's death is a case of this.
translations.idiomatic: Retrograde Mars punishes virtueless realms—Shi Le's end fits the pattern.

sentences.zh: 勒之餘燼，以自殘害。

translations.literal: The remaining embers of Le thereby harm themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Le's leftover sparks will consume themselves.

sentences.zh: 今年官與太歲、太陰三合癸巳，癸為北方，北方當受災。

translations.literal: This year the official star joins Grand Year and Grand Yin in a triple conjunction at guisi; gui is the north; the north is sure to suffer disaster.
translations.idiomatic: This year the bureaucratic star, Grand Year, and Grand Yin meet in gui-si—gui is north, and the north will suffer.

sentences.zh: 歲鎮二星共合翼軫，從子及巳，徘徊六年。

translations.literal: The Year and Garrison stars together join Yi and Zhen, from zi to si, lingering six years.
translations.idiomatic: Year and Garrison stars conjoin in Yi and Zhen from zi through si, hovering six years.

sentences.zh: 荊楚之分，歲鎮所守，其下國昌，豈非功德之徵也！

translations.literal: In the division of Jing and Chu, what Year and Garrison guard—below them the state flourishes—is this not a sign of merit and virtue!
translations.idiomatic: They guard the Jing-Chu field—states beneath them prosper. Surely this marks your merit.

sentences.zh: 今年六月，鎮星前角亢。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of this year the Garrison Star moved ahead of Horn and Neck.
translations.idiomatic: This sixth month Garrison advanced before Horn and Neck.

sentences.zh: 角亢，鄭之分。

translations.literal: Horn and Neck are Zheng's division.
translations.idiomatic: Horn and Neck belong to Zheng's asterism.

sentences.zh: 歲星移入房，太白在心。

translations.literal: The Year Star moved into Chamber; the Great White was in Heart.
translations.idiomatic: The Year star entered Chamber while Venus sat in Heart.

sentences.zh: 心房，宋分。

translations.literal: Heart and Chamber are Song's division.
translations.idiomatic: Heart and Chamber mark Song's field.

sentences.zh: 順之者昌，逆之者亡。

translations.literal: Those who accord with it flourish; those who oppose it perish.
translations.idiomatic: Follow heaven's layout and thrive; resist it and perish.

sentences.zh: 石季龍若興兵東南，此其死會也。

translations.literal: If Shi Jilong raises troops toward the southeast, this will be the assembly of his death.
translations.idiomatic: Should Shi Hu march southeast, that campaign will be his death day.

sentences.zh: 官若應天伐刑，徑據宋鄭，則無敵矣。

translations.literal: If the lord, answering Heaven, punishes the punished, and goes straight to occupy Song and Zheng, then there will be none to match you.
translations.idiomatic: March in accord with heaven, strike the guilty, seize Song and Zheng, and none will stand against you.

sentences.zh: 若天與不取，反受其咎。

translations.literal: If Heaven grants and you do not take, you will on the contrary receive its blame.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven offers the opening—refuse it and you earn heaven's blame.

sentences.zh: 」侃志在中原，聞而大喜。

translations.literal: Kan's ambition was in the Central Plain; hearing this he was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Tao Kan's heart was set on the north; the reading delighted him.

sentences.zh: 會病篤，不果行。

translations.literal: Just then he was critically ill and in the end could not go.
translations.idiomatic: He fell mortally ill and never marched.

sentences.zh: 侃薨，征西將軍庾亮代鎮武昌，復引洋問氣侯。

translations.literal: When Kan died, General Who Conquers the West Yu Liang succeeded him in garrisoning Wuchang and again summoned Yang to ask about qi signs.
translations.idiomatic: After Tao Kan died, Yu Liang took the western command at Wuchang and again consulted Dai Yang on omens.

sentences.zh: 洋曰：「天有白氣，喪必東行，不過數年必應。

translations.literal: Yang said, "Heaven has white qi; mourning is sure to travel eastward; within no more than a few years it is sure to correspond.
translations.idiomatic: Dai Yang said white vapor in the sky meant mourning moving east within a few years.

sentences.zh: 」尋有大鹿向西城門，洋曰：「野獸向城，主人將去。

translations.literal: Before long a great deer went toward the west city gate; Yang said, "When wild beasts face the city, the master will depart.
translations.idiomatic: Soon a stag walked toward the west gate; wild beasts facing the walls mean the lord will leave.

sentences.zh: 」城東家夜半望見城內有數炬火，從城上出，如大車狀，白布幔覆，與火俱出城東北行，至江乃滅。

translations.literal: People east of the city at midnight looked and saw several torch-fires inside the city, coming out from atop the wall like great carts, covered with white cloth canopies; together with the fire they went out northeast of the city, reaching the river and then being extinguished.
translations.idiomatic: East-side households saw at midnight bundles of flame slide from the battlements like covered wagons, wrapped in white sheets, rolling northeast out of town until they vanished in the river.

sentences.zh: 洋聞而歎曰：「此與前白氣同。

translations.literal: When Yang heard this he sighed and said, "This is the same as the white qi of before."
translations.idiomatic: Hearing the tale, Dai Yang sighed: "That repeats the white-vapor omen we saw earlier."

sentences.zh: 」時亮欲西鎮石城，或問洋：「此西足當欲東不？

translations.literal: At the time Liang wished to garrison Shicheng to the west; someone asked Yang, "Is this 'west' enough, or does it intend to go east?
translations.idiomatic: Yu Liang planned to move west to garrison Shicheng. Someone asked Dai Yang whether "west" here meant a drift eastward instead.

sentences.zh: 」洋曰：「不當也。

translations.literal: Yang said, "It is not appropriate."
translations.idiomatic: Dai Yang said it would not serve.

sentences.zh: 」，洋言於亮曰：「武昌土地有山無林，政可圖始，不可居終。

translations.literal: Yang spoke to Liang, saying, "The land of Wuchang has mountains but no forests—it may be planned for a beginning, but cannot be dwelt in to the end."
translations.idiomatic: He told Yu Liang: "Wuchang is ridged but treeless—fine to start a venture, fatal to finish one there."

sentences.zh: 山作八字，數不及九。

translations.literal: The mountains form the character 'eight'; the reckoning does not reach nine.
translations.idiomatic: The hills trace the shape of the character ba; numerically they never reach nine—a place that cannot endure.

sentences.zh: 昔吳用壬寅來上；

translations.literal: Formerly Wu used renyin to come up to the capital;
translations.idiomatic: Eastern Wu rose on a ren-yin year and moved the court upstream;

sentences.zh: 創立宮城，至己酉，還下秣陵。

translations.literal: they founded the palace city, and by jiyou they returned down to Moling.
translations.idiomatic: they built the palace enclosure, then by ji-you had withdrawn downstream to Moling.

sentences.zh: 陶公亦涉八年。

translations.literal: Lord Tao likewise crossed eight years.
translations.idiomatic: Tao Kan's stay there lasted eight years as well.

sentences.zh: 土地盛衰有數，人心去就有期，不可移也。

translations.literal: The flourishing and decline of land has a number; the people's hearts' going and staying have a term—it cannot be shifted.
translations.idiomatic: Soil has its cycle of boom and bust, and popular allegiance its term—no edict can fix that.

sentences.zh: 公宜更擇吉處，武昌不可久住。

translations.literal: You ought to choose another auspicious place; Wuchang cannot be long dwelt in."
translations.idiomatic: Choose another seat of power; Wuchang must not be your long-term capital."

sentences.zh: 」五年，亮令毛寶屯邾城。

translations.literal: In the fifth year Liang ordered Mao Bao to encamp at Zhucheng.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year Yu Liang stationed Mao Bao at Zhu fortress.

sentences.zh: 九月，洋言於亮曰：「毛豫州今年受死問。

translations.literal: In the ninth month Yang spoke to Liang, saying, "Prefect Mao of Yu Province this year receives the inquiry of death.
translations.idiomatic: That ninth month Dai Yang warned Yu Liang: "Mao Bao, your Yuzhou governor, faces a death omen this year.

sentences.zh: 昨朝大霧晏風，當有怨賊報仇，攻圍諸侯，誠宜遠偵邏。

translations.literal: Yesterday morning there was great fog and a late wind; there ought to be resentful bandits taking revenge, besieging lords—you truly ought to send scouts far out.
translations.idiomatic: Yesterday's thick fog and sluggish wind mean vengeful raiders will ring a nobleman's walls—push your patrols deep into the country.

sentences.zh: 」寶問當在何時，答曰：「五十日內。

translations.literal: Bao asked when it would be; he answered, "Within fifty days."
translations.idiomatic: Mao Bao asked when; Dai Yang said within fifty days.

sentences.zh: 」其夕，又曰：「九月建戌，硃雀飛驚，征軍還歸，乘戴火光，天示有信，災發東房，葉落歸本，慮有後患。

translations.literal: That evening he again said, "The ninth month establishes xu; the Vermilion Bird flies in alarm; the expeditionary army returns home, riding on bearing fire light—Heaven shows trust; disaster issues from the eastern chamber; leaves fall and return to the root—I fear there will be later trouble.
translations.idiomatic: That night he added a hexagram reading: ninth month, xu month, the Vermilion Bird startled, armies wheeling home under livid fire—heaven vouches the sign; calamity rises in the east wing, like leaves seeking the root—expect a lingering blow.

sentences.zh: 」明日，又曰：「昨夜火殃，非國福，今年架屋，致使君病，可因燒屋，移家南渡，無嫌也。

translations.literal: The next day he again said, "Last night's fire calamity is not the state's blessing; this year you built houses and caused the lord to fall ill—you may burn the houses, move the household south across the river—there is nothing to blame.
translations.idiomatic: Next morning he blamed the new roofs for Yu Liang's illness: burn the structures, move the family south across the river without scruple.

sentences.zh: 」寶即遣兒婦還武昌。

translations.literal: Bao thereupon sent his son's wife back to Wuchang.
translations.idiomatic: Mao Bao immediately sent his daughter-in-law back to Wuchang.

sentences.zh: 尋傳賊當來攻城，洋曰：「十月丁亥夜半時得賊問，幹為君，支為臣，丁為征西府，亥為邾城，功曹為賊神，加子時十月水王木相，王相氣合，賊必來。

translations.literal: Before long rumor said bandits would come to attack the city; Yang said, "On dinghai of the tenth month, in the middle of the night, we obtain the bandits' inquiry: qian is lord, zhi is minister; ding is the Western Expedition headquarters, hai is Zhucheng; the merit clerk is the bandits' spirit; adding the zi double-hour, in the tenth month water is king and wood is minister; king and minister qi combine—the bandits are sure to come.
translations.idiomatic: Word spread of a siege. Dai Yang set a divination clock for ding-hai at midnight: stems mark lord and minister, ding stands for the western expedition yamen and hai for Zhu fort; with water ruling the tenth night hour and wood assisting, host and guest vapors merge—the raiders will come.

sentences.zh: 寅數七，子數九，賊高可九千人，下可七千人。

translations.literal: Yin's number is seven, zi's number is nine; the bandits at most can be nine thousand men, at least seven thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Yin counts seven and zi nine: expect between seven and nine thousand foemen.

sentences.zh: 從魁為貴人加丁，下克上，有空亡之事，不敢進武昌也。

translations.literal: Congkui is the noble man added to ding; below overcomes above; there is the matter of emptiness and void—they dare not advance on Wuchang.
translations.idiomatic: The deity Congkui sitting on ding shows subordinates overcoming superiors with hollow middle—too weak to push on to Wuchang.

sentences.zh: 」賊果陷邾城而去。

translations.literal: The bandits indeed took Zhucheng and departed.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy stormed Zhu fort and withdrew, as he said.

sentences.zh: 亮問洋曰：「故當不失石城否？

translations.literal: Liang asked Yang, "So in the end we will not lose Shicheng, will we?
translations.idiomatic: Yu Liang asked whether Shicheng would still hold.

sentences.zh: 」洋曰：「賊從安陸向石城，逆太白，當伐身，無所慮。

translations.literal: Yang said, "The bandits go from Anlu toward Shicheng, contrary to the Great White—they will harm themselves; there is nothing to worry about.
translations.idiomatic: Dai Yang said their march from Anlu toward Shicheng runs counter to Venus—they will wound themselves; have no fear.

sentences.zh: 」亮曰：「天何以利胡而病我？

translations.literal: Liang said, "Why does Heaven favor the Hu and afflict us?"
translations.idiomatic: Yu Liang cried, "Why does heaven help the barbarians and hurt us?"

sentences.zh: 」洋曰：「天符有吉凶，土地有盛衰，今年害氣三合己亥，己為天下，亥為戎胡，季龍亦當受死。

translations.literal: Yang said, "Heaven's tallies have auspiciousness and inauspiciousness; land has flourishing and decline; this year the baleful qi triple-conjoins at jihai—ji is All-under-Heaven, hai is the Rong and Hu; Jilong likewise ought to receive death.
translations.idiomatic: Dai Yang answered: omens cut both ways, and ground has its seasons; this year's malignant conjunction stacks on ji-hai—ji is the realm, hai the northern tribes—Shi Hu too should die.

sentences.zh: 今乃不憂賊，但憂公病耳。

translations.literal: Now you need not worry about the bandits, but only worry about the lord's illness.
translations.idiomatic: Worry not the enemy but your own sickness.

sentences.zh: 」亮曰：「何方救我疾？

translations.literal: Liang said, "From what direction may my illness be saved?
translations.idiomatic: Yu Liang asked where to turn for a cure.

sentences.zh: 」洋曰：「荊州受兵，江州受災，公可去此二州。

translations.literal: Yang said, "Jing Province receives weapons; Jiang Province receives disaster—you may leave these two provinces.
translations.idiomatic: Dai Yang said Jingzhou would see arms and Jiangzhou calamity—flee both regions.

sentences.zh: 」亮曰：「如此，當有解不」？

translations.literal: Liang said, "If it is thus, will there still be relief?
translations.idiomatic: Yu Liang asked whether any remedy remained.

sentences.zh: 」洋曰：「恨晚，猶差不也。

translations.literal: Yang said, "It is regrettably late, yet perhaps not entirely without improvement.
translations.idiomatic: Dai Yang answered: the hour is late, yet something may still be salvaged.

sentences.zh: 」亮竟不能解二州，遂至大困。

translations.literal: Liang in the end could not leave the two provinces, and thereupon came to great distress.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Liang could not abandon either province and fell into mortal crisis.

sentences.zh: 洋曰：「昔蘇峻時，公于白石祠中祈福，許賽其牛，至今未解，故為此鬼所考。

translations.literal: Yang said, "Formerly at the time of Su Jun, you prayed for blessing in the shrine at White Rock, vowing to repay it with an ox, and to this day you have not released the vow; therefore this ghost torments you.
translations.idiomatic: Dai Yang reminded him: during Su Jun's revolt Yu Liang had vowed an ox at the White Rock shrine and never redeemed it—angry spirits now pressed him.

sentences.zh: 」亮曰：「有之，君是神人也。

translations.literal: Liang said, "There is such a thing—you are a spiritlike man.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Liang confessed, "You read me like a god.

sentences.zh: 」或問洋曰：「庾公可得幾時？

translations.literal: Someone asked Yang, "How long can Lord Yu obtain?
translations.idiomatic: Another asked how long Yu Liang had left.

sentences.zh: 」洋曰：「見明年。

translations.literal: Yang said, "He will be seen until next year.
translations.idiomatic: Dai Yang said he would last into the next year—barely.

sentences.zh: 」時亮已不識人，咸以為妄，果至正月一日而薨。

translations.literal: At the time Liang already did not recognize people; all thought it wild talk, and indeed on the first day of the first month he passed away.
translations.idiomatic: By then Yu Liang no longer knew faces; they mocked the prophecy—yet he died on New Year's Day.

sentences.zh: 庾翼代亮，洋復為占侯。

translations.literal: Yu Yi succeeded Liang, and Yang again performed omen divination for him.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Yi replaced his brother and again retained Dai Yang for omens.

sentences.zh: 少時卒，年八十餘。

translations.literal: Before long he died, aged more than eighty.
translations.idiomatic: Dai Yang died soon after, aged over eighty.

sentences.zh: 所占驗者不可勝紀。

translations.literal: What he divined and verified cannot be fully recorded.
translations.idiomatic: His verified predictions are too many to count.

sentences.zh: 韓友

translations.literal: Han You.
translations.idiomatic: Han You.

sentences.zh: 韓友，字景先，廬江舒人也。

translations.literal: Han You, courtesy name Jingxian, was a native of Shu in Lujiang.
translations.idiomatic: Han You, courtesy name Jingxian, came from Shu county in Lujiang.

sentences.zh: 為書生，受《易》于會稽伍振，善占卜，能圖宅相塚，亦行京費厭勝之術。

translations.literal: He was a literatus student; he received the Changes from Wu Zhen of Kuaiji; he was good at divination, could chart dwellings and read tombs, and also practiced the Jing and Fei apotropaic arts.
translations.idiomatic: He studied the Book of Changes under Wu Zhen of Kuaiji, excelled at milfoil divination, geomancy for houses and graves, and the apotropaic methods of the Jing and Fei schools.

sentences.zh: 龍舒長鄧林婦病積年，垂死，醫巫皆息意。

translations.literal: The wife of Deng Lin, magistrate of Longshu, had been ill many years and was at the point of death; physicians and shamans had all abandoned hope.
translations.idiomatic: The wife of Longshu magistrate Deng Lin had lain near death for years while doctors and exorcists gave up.

sentences.zh: 友為筮之，使畫作野豬著臥處屏風上，一宿覺佳，於是遂差。

translations.literal: You performed milfoil divination for her, had her paint a wild boar on the screen at the head of her bed, and after one night she felt better, whereupon she then recovered.
translations.idiomatic: Han You divined for her, told her to paint a boar on her bedside screen, and after one comfortable night she mended.

sentences.zh: 舒縣廷掾王睦病死，已復魄。

translations.literal: Wang Mu, clerk of the county court of Shu county, died of illness, then revived.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Mu, a Shu county clerk, died of sickness and came back to life.

sentences.zh: 友為筮之，令以丹畫版作日月置床頭，又以豹皮馬鄣泥臥上，立愈。

translations.literal: You performed milfoil divination for him, ordered him to paint sun and moon with cinnabar on a board and place them at the head of the bed, and also to spread a mud-spattered leopard-skin horse screen over where he lay, and he immediately recovered.
translations.idiomatic: Han You had him paint red sun and moon on a board at his pillow and drape a mud-splashed leopard-hide horse blind over the couch—he healed at once.

sentences.zh: 劉世則女病魅積年，巫為攻禱，伐空塚故城間，得狸鼉數十，病猶不差。

translations.literal: Liu Shize's daughter had been possessed by a mei demon many years; shamans attacked it with prayer, felling empty tombs between old ramparts, and obtained several tens of otter-crocodiles, yet the illness still did not improve.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Shize's daughter endured a fox-spirit for years; shamans raided old tombs and dragged out dozens of otters and soft-shelled turtles, yet she stayed ill.

sentences.zh: 友筮之，命作布囊，依女發時，張囊著窗牖間，友閉戶作氣，若有所驅。

translations.literal: You divined by milfoil, ordered a cloth bag made, and when the girl's fit came, spread the bag at the window; You closed the door and made qi as if driving something.
translations.idiomatic: Han You cast yarrow, sewed a cloth sack, and when her seizure began hung it in the window while he shut the door and drove spirits with breath control.

sentences.zh: 斯須之間，見囊大脹如吹，因決敗之，女仍大發。

translations.literal: In a short while they saw the bag greatly swell as if blown, and therefore burst it open; the girl still had a great outbreak.
translations.idiomatic: The sack swelled as if inflated; he slit it and the girl convulsed worse.

sentences.zh: 友乃更作皮囊二枚，遝張之，施張如前，囊復脹滿。

translations.literal: You then made two leather bags, repeatedly spread them, deploying them as before; the bags again swelled full.
translations.idiomatic: He made two leather bags, hung them as before, and they ballooned again.

sentences.zh: 因急縛囊口，懸著樹二十許日，漸消，開視有二斤狐毛，女遂差。

translations.literal: Thereupon he urgently tied the bag mouth, hung it on a tree for about twenty days; it gradually shrank; opening and looking, there were two jin of fox fur, and the girl then recovered.
translations.idiomatic: He lashed the mouths shut and hung them on a tree twenty days until they deflated; inside were two jin of fox fur, and the girl recovered.

sentences.zh: 宣城邊洪以四月中就友卜家中安否，友曰：「卿家有兵殃，其禍甚重。

translations.literal: Bian Hong of Xuancheng in the fourth month went to You to divine whether his household was secure; You said, "Your household has a military calamity; the disaster is very heavy.
translations.idiomatic: Fourth month, Xuancheng's Bian Hong asked Han You if his home was safe. Han You said a military scourge loomed, very grave.

sentences.zh: 可伐七十束柴，積於庚地，至七月丁酉放火燒之，咎可消也。

translations.literal: You may cut seventy bundles of firewood, pile them on the geng ground, and on dingyou of the seventh month set fire and burn them—the blame can be dispelled.
translations.idiomatic: Stack seventy faggots on the geng sector and burn them on ding-you of the seventh month to lift the curse.

sentences.zh: 不爾，其凶難言。

translations.literal: If not, its inauspiciousness is hard to describe.
translations.idiomatic: Ignore the rite and the misfortune beggars description.

sentences.zh: 」洪即聚柴。

translations.literal: Hong thereupon gathered firewood.
translations.idiomatic: Bian Hong collected the wood.

sentences.zh: 至日，大風，不敢發火。

translations.literal: When the day came, there was a great wind, and he dared not set the fire.
translations.idiomatic: On the appointed day a gale rose and he feared to light it.

sentences.zh: 洪後為廣陽領校，遭母喪歸家，友來投之，時日已暮，出告從者，速裝束，吾當夜去。

translations.literal: Later Hong became Guangyang chief inspector; encountering his mother's mourning he returned home, and You came to lodge with him; the time was already dusk; he went out and told his followers, "Pack quickly; I must leave this night.
translations.idiomatic: Later Bian Hong served as Guangyang chief inspector. Mourning his mother, he returned home; Han You visited at dusk, then burst out to servants to pack—he must leave that night.

sentences.zh: 從者曰：「今日已暝，數十里草行，何急復去？

translations.literal: The followers said, "Today is already dark; several tens of li through the grass—why urgently leave again?
translations.idiomatic: They protested: night had fallen and the moor road was long—why flee again?

sentences.zh: 」友曰：「非汝所知也。

translations.literal: You said, "This is not what you can understand.
translations.idiomatic: Han You said they could not understand.

sentences.zh: 此間血覆地，寧可復住！

translations.literal: Here blood will cover the ground—how can one stay again!
translations.idiomatic: Blood would soak the ground—no one should stay.

sentences.zh: 」苦留之，不待食而去。

translations.literal: They bitterly urged him to stay; he did not wait for food and departed.
translations.idiomatic: They pressed him to dine; he refused and rode off.

sentences.zh: 其夜洪欻發狂，絞殺兩子，並殺婦，又斫父妾二人，皆被創，因出亡走。

translations.literal: That night Hong suddenly went mad, strangled two sons, and also killed his wife, and further hacked his father's two concubines, all wounded, then fled away.
translations.idiomatic: That night Bian Hong went mad, throttled two sons, slew his wife, hacked his father's two concubines, and bolted wounded from the house.

sentences.zh: 明日，其宗族往收殯亡者，尋索洪，數日，于宅前林中得之，已自經死。

translations.literal: The next day his lineage kin went to gather the dead for burial and searched for Hong; after several days they found him in the woods before the compound; he had already hanged himself.
translations.idiomatic: Next day kinsmen buried the dead and searched until they found him hanged in the grove before his gate.

sentences.zh: 宣城太守殷祐有病，友筮之，曰：「七月晦日，將有大鸜鳥來集廳事上，宜勤伺取，若獲者為善，不獲將成禍。

translations.literal: Yin You, governor of Xuancheng, was ill; You divined for him and said, "On the last day of the seventh month a great mynah bird will come and alight on the hall affairs; you ought diligently to watch and capture it—if you obtain it that is good; if you do not obtain it, a calamity will form.
translations.idiomatic: Xuancheng governor Yin You fell sick. Han You divined: on the seventh month's last day a giant mynah would land in the audience hall—catch it or disaster would follow.

sentences.zh: 」祐乃謹為其備。

translations.literal: You thereupon carefully made preparations for this.
translations.idiomatic: Yin You prepared meticulously.

sentences.zh: 至日，果有大鸜垂尾九尺，來集廳事上，掩捕得之，祐乃遷石頭督護，後為吳郡太守。

translations.literal: When the day came, there was indeed a great mynah with a tail nine chi long that came and alighted on the hall affairs; they covered and captured it and obtained it; You thereupon was promoted to protector at Stone Citadel, later becoming governor of Wu commandery.
translations.idiomatic: The bird appeared with a nine-chi tail; they netted it, Yin You was promoted Stone Citadel protector, then Wu commandery governor.

sentences.zh: 友卜占神效甚多，而消殃轉禍，無不皆驗。

translations.literal: You's divinations were very many in spiritlike efficacy, and in dispelling calamity and turning misfortune there was none that did not verify.
translations.idiomatic: Han You's readings were uncannily accurate, and every apotropaic rite he prescribed worked.

sentences.zh: 于寶問其故，友曰：「筮封用五行相生殺，如案方投藥治病，以冷熱相救。

translations.literal: Gan Bao asked him the reason; You said, "Milfoil hexagrams use the five phases' mutual production and killing; it is like according to formula casting medicine to treat illness, using cold and heat to rescue each other.
translations.idiomatic: Gan Bao asked why. Han You compared yarrow to prescribing hot or cold drugs by formula.

sentences.zh: 其差與不差，不可必也。

translations.literal: Whether it recovers or does not recover cannot be certain.
translations.idiomatic: Recovery, of course, is never guaranteed.

sentences.zh: 」友以舉賢良，元帝渡江，以為廣武將軍，永嘉末卒。

translations.literal: You, recommended as worthy and good, when Emperor Yuan crossed the Yangzi was appointed General Who Extends Might, and died at the end of Yongjia.
translations.idiomatic: Recommended worthy and excellent, he became General Who Extends Might after Emperor Yuan crossed the river and died at Yongjia's end.

sentences.zh: 淳于智

translations.literal: Chunyu Zhi.
translations.idiomatic: Chunyu Zhi.

sentences.zh: 淳于智，字叔平，濟北盧人也。

translations.literal: Chunyu Zhi, courtesy name Shuping, was a native of Lu in Jibei.
translations.idiomatic: Chunyu Zhi, courtesy name Shuping, was a man of Lu in Jibei.

sentences.zh: 有思義，能《易》筮，善厭勝之術。

translations.literal: He had reflective sense of duty; he could perform Changes divination by milfoil and was good at apotropaic arts.
translations.idiomatic: He was dutiful and thoughtful, divined from the Changes, and mastered apotropaic rites.

sentences.zh: 高平劉柔夜臥，鼠齧其左手中指，以問智。

translations.literal: Liu Rou of Gaoping lay sleeping at night; a rat gnawed his left hand middle finger; he asked Zhi.
translations.idiomatic: Gaoping's Liu Rou woke to a rat chewing his left middle finger and consulted Chunyu Zhi.

sentences.zh: 智曰：「是欲殺君而不能，當為君使其反死。

translations.literal: Zhi said, "It wishes to kill you but cannot; I shall for you make it instead die.
translations.idiomatic: Chunyu Zhi said the beast meant murder but lacked power—he would turn the bane back on the rat.

sentences.zh: 」乃以硃書手腕橫文後三寸作田字，辟方一寸二分，使露手以臥。

translations.literal: Thereupon with cinnabar he wrote on the transverse lines three cun behind the wrist a field character, one cun two fen square on a side, and had him expose the hand to sleep.
translations.idiomatic: He drew a cinnabar "field" character on the transverse crease three cun above the wrist, each side one cun two fen, and had Liu sleep with the mark bare.

sentences.zh: 明旦，有大鼠伏死手前。

translations.literal: At dawn there was a large rat lying dead before the hand.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn a huge rat lay dead before the marked hand.

sentences.zh: 譙人夏侯藻母病困，詣智卜，忽有一狐當門向之嗥。

translations.literal: Xia Zao of Qiao's mother was gravely ill; he went to Zhi to divine, when suddenly a fox stood at the gate howling toward him.
translations.idiomatic: Qiao man Xia Zao sought Chunyu Zhi for his dying mother; a fox stood howling at the gate.

sentences.zh: 藻怖愕，馳見智。

translations.literal: Zao was frightened and alarmed and galloped to see Zhi.
translations.idiomatic: Terror-struck, Xia Zao raced to Chunyu Zhi.

sentences.zh: 智曰：「其禍甚急，君速歸，在狐嗥處拊心啼哭，令家人驚怪，大小必出，一人不出，哭勿止，然後其禍可救也。
