translations.literal: Zhi said, "The calamity is very urgent; you should quickly return, at the place of the fox's howl beat your breast and weep aloud, causing the household to be startled and strange, and great and small must all come out—if one person does not come out, do not stop weeping; afterward the calamity can be saved.
translations.idiomatic: Chunyu Zhi said speed home, wail and beat your breast where the fox cried until every soul, high or low, rushes outdoors—if anyone stays inside, never stop keening—only then can the house be saved.

sentences.zh: 」藻還，如其言，母亦扶病而出。

translations.literal: Zao returned and acted as he said; his mother also supported her illness and came out.
translations.idiomatic: Xia Zao obeyed; even his sick mother let herself be helped outside.

sentences.zh: 家人既集，堂屋五間拉然而崩。

translations.literal: Once the household had assembled, the five-bay main hall suddenly collapsed with a crash.
translations.idiomatic: When the family had gathered, their five-bay hall crashed flat.

sentences.zh: 護軍張劭母病篤，智筮之，使西出市沐猴，系母臂，令傍人捶拍，恆使作聲，三日放去。

translations.literal: Zhang Shao the protector's mother was critically ill; Zhi divined for her, had him go west out to the market to buy a bathing monkey, tie it on the mother's arm, order those beside to pound and pat, constantly making it cry out, and on the third day release it.
translations.idiomatic: Protector Zhang Shao's mother lay dying. Chunyu Zhi sent him west to market for a macaque, bound it on her arm, had attendants pat it until it shrieked three days, then released it.

sentences.zh: 劭從之。

translations.literal: Shao followed this.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Shao obeyed.

sentences.zh: 其猴出門即為犬所咋死，母病遂差。

translations.literal: When the monkey went out the gate it was immediately bitten to death by a dog; his mother's illness thereupon improved.
translations.idiomatic: The monkey was killed by a dog at the door; the mother recovered.

sentences.zh: 上党鮑瑗家多喪病貧苦，或謂之曰：「淳于叔平神人也，君何不試就卜，知禍所在？

translations.literal: Bao Yuan of Shangdang had many deaths and illness in the family and was poor and bitter; someone said to him, "Chunyu Shuping is a spiritlike man—why do you not try going to him for divination, to know where the calamity lies?
translations.idiomatic: Shangdang's Bao Yuan suffered repeated deaths, sickness, and poverty. Friends urged him to consult "spirit-man" Chunyu Zhi.

sentences.zh: 」瑗性質直，不信卜筮，曰：「人生有命，豈卜筮所移！

translations.literal: Yuan's nature was honest and straightforward; he did not believe in milfoil divination, saying, "Human life has fate—how can milfoil divination shift it!
translations.idiomatic: Bao Yuan, blunt and skeptical, said fate ruled life—how could yarrow move it?

sentences.zh: 」會智來，應詹謂曰：「此君寒士，每多屯虞，君有通靈之思，可為一卦。

translations.literal: Just then Zhi came; Ying Zhan said to him, "This gentleman is a poor scholar, always having many setbacks; you have thoughts that penetrate the spirits—please cast one hexagram.
translations.idiomatic: Chunyu Zhi arrived; Ying Zhan begged a reading for the hard-luck scholar.

sentences.zh: 」智乃為卦，卦成，謂瑗曰：「君安宅失宜，故令君困。

translations.literal: Zhi thereupon cast a hexagram; when the hexagram was complete, he said to Yuan, "Your peaceful dwelling is out of accord; therefore it causes you to be distressed.
translations.idiomatic: Chunyu Zhi cast the lines and told Bao Yuan his house sat wrong, hence his troubles.

sentences.zh: 君舍東北有大桑樹，君徑至市，入門數十步，當有一人持荊馬鞭者，便就買以懸此樹，三年當暴得財。

translations.literal: Northeast of your house there is a great mulberry tree; you should go straight to the market, enter the gate several tens of paces, and there ought to be a person holding a thorn horsewhip—then go buy it and hang it on this tree; in three years you will suddenly obtain wealth.
translations.idiomatic: A giant mulberry stood northeast of the house—Bao must enter the market, walk a few dozen paces inside the gate, buy the thorn switch a vendor held, hang it on that tree, and in three years wealth would explode upon him.

sentences.zh: 」瑗承言詣市，果得馬鞭，懸之三年，浚井，得錢數十萬，銅鐵器復二十餘萬，於是致贍，疾者亦愈。

translations.literal: Yuan accepted the words and went to the market, and indeed obtained a horsewhip; he hung it three years, dredged the well, and obtained several hundred thousand cash, and bronze and iron vessels again more than two hundred thousand, whereupon he became well provided for, and the sick also recovered.
translations.idiomatic: He found the whip, hung it three years, cleaned his well, and pulled up hundreds of thousands in coin plus two hundred thousand more in bronze and iron, ending want and curing the household.

sentences.zh: 其消災轉禍，不可勝紀，而卜筮所占，千百皆中。

translations.literal: His dispelling disaster and turning misfortune cannot be fully recorded, and in what milfoil divination divined, a thousand or a hundred all hit.
translations.idiomatic: His turnings of ill luck are legion, and his yarrow casts hit time after time.

sentences.zh: 應詹少亦多病，智乃為符使詹佩之，誦其文，既而皆驗，莫能學也。

translations.literal: Ying Zhan in his youth also had many illnesses; Zhi then made a talisman for Zhan to wear, reciting its text, and afterward all verified; none could study it.
translations.idiomatic: Ying Zhan had been sickly as a boy; Chunyu Zhi gave him a talisman to wear and chant—every omen proved true, yet no one could copy the craft.

sentences.zh: 性深沈，常自言短命，曰：「辛亥歲天下有事，當有巫醫挾道術者死。

translations.literal: His nature was deep and still; he often said of himself that his life would be short, saying, "In the xinhai year there will be affairs in All-under-Heaven; there must be shamans and physicians who grasp Dao arts who will die.
translations.idiomatic: Brooding and reserved, he predicted a short life: in the xin-hai year the realm would convulse and spirit-doctors would die.

sentences.zh: 吾守《易》義以行之，猶當不應此乎！

translations.literal: I guard the meaning of the Changes to practice it—should I still not correspond to this!
translations.idiomatic: He asked whether keeping faith with the Changes could spare him—it could not.

sentences.zh: 」太康末，為司馬督，有寵于楊駿，故見殺。

translations.literal: At the end of Taikang he was a Sima supervisor, favored by Yang Jun, and therefore was killed.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Taikang he served as palace Sima inspector, favored by Yang Jun, and died in the purge.

sentences.zh: 步熊

translations.literal: Bu Xiong.
translations.idiomatic: Bu Xiong.

sentences.zh: 步熊，字叔羆，陽平發幹人也。

translations.literal: Bu Xiong, courtesy name Shupi, was a native of Fagan in Yangping.
translations.idiomatic: Bu Xiong, courtesy name Shupi, came from Fagan in Yangping.

sentences.zh: 少好卜筮數術，門徒甚盛。

translations.literal: In his youth he loved divination by milfoil and numerological arts; his disciples were very numerous.
translations.idiomatic: He loved yarrow and number-craft and drew a crowd of disciples.

sentences.zh: 熊學舍側有一人燒死，吏持熊諸生，謂為失火。

translations.literal: Beside Xiong's study hall someone burned to death; clerks seized Xiong's students, deeming that they had lost control of the fire.
translations.idiomatic: When a neighbor burned to death beside his school, clerks arrested Bu Xiong's pupils for careless fire.

sentences.zh: 熊曰：「已為卿卜得其人矣。

translations.literal: Xiong said, "I have already divined for you and obtained that person."
translations.idiomatic: Bu Xiong told the clerk, "I have already found your arsonist."

sentences.zh: 使從道南行，當有一人來問得火主未者，便縛之。

translations.literal: Send someone south along the road; there ought to be a person who comes asking whether the fire master has been found—then bind him.
translations.idiomatic: Send a man south along the track until someone asks whether the fire's owner has been caught—seize him.

sentences.zh: 」吏如熊言，果是耕人，自言草惡難耕，故燒之，忽風起延燒遠近，實不知草中有人。

translations.literal: The clerk acted as Xiong said; it was indeed a farmer, who said of himself that the grass was bad and hard to plow, therefore he burned it; suddenly wind rose and the fire spread far and near; in truth he did not know there was a person in the grass.
translations.idiomatic: The officer obeyed: a plowman admitted he had torched tough stubble without knowing a sleeper lay in the weeds; a gust had spread the blaze.

sentences.zh: 又鄰人兒遠行，或告已死，其父母號哭制服，熊為之卜，克日當還，如期果至。

translations.literal: Again a neighbor's son went on a distant journey; someone reported he had already died; his parents wailed and put on mourning garments; Xiong divined for them that on the determined day he ought to return, and at the appointed time he indeed arrived.
translations.idiomatic: When a neighbor's son was rumored dead abroad, Bu Xiong set a return date; the youth walked in on that very day.

sentences.zh: 趙王倫聞其名，召之。

translations.literal: Prince Zhao Lun heard his name and summoned him.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Sima Lun of Zhao summoned him.

sentences.zh: 熊謂諸生曰：「倫死不久，不足應也。

translations.literal: Xiong said to his students, "Lun will not die long from now—it is not worth responding."
translations.idiomatic: Bu Xiong told his disciples Sima Lun would soon perish—not worth serving.

sentences.zh: 」倫怒，遣兵圍之數重。

translations.literal: Lun was angry and dispatched troops to surround them in many layers.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Lun ringed the school with soldiers.

sentences.zh: 熊乃使諸生著其裘南走，倫兵悉赴捉之，熊密從北出，得脫。

translations.literal: Xiong then had the students put on his furs and run south; Lun's soldiers all rushed to seize them; Xiong secretly went out from the north and escaped.
translations.idiomatic: He dressed pupils in his own pelts to draw the chase south while he slipped out north.

sentences.zh: 後為成都王穎所辟，穎使熊射覆，物無所失。

translations.literal: Later he was recruited by Prince Chengdu Ying; Ying had Xiong shoot the covered vessel, and of objects there was none he missed.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Chengdu Sima Ying employed him; in the "cover the jar" divination game he never missed.

sentences.zh: 後穎奔關中，平昌公模鎮鄴，以熊穎黨，誅之。

translations.literal: Later Ying fled into the passes; Prince Pingchang Mo garrisoned Ye, and because Xiong was Ying's partisan, executed him.
translations.idiomatic: When Sima Ying fled to Guanzhong, Prince Pingchang Sima Mo held Ye and executed Bu Xiong as his partisan.

sentences.zh: 杜不愆

translations.literal: Du Buqian.
translations.idiomatic: Du Buqian.

sentences.zh: 杜不愆，廬江人也。

translations.literal: Du Buqian was a native of Lujiang.
translations.idiomatic: Du Buqian came from Lujiang.

sentences.zh: 少就外祖郭璞學《易》卜。

translations.literal: In his youth he studied the Changes and divination from his maternal grandfather Guo Pu.
translations.idiomatic: As a boy he learned the Book of Changes and milfoil from his grandfather Guo Pu.

sentences.zh: 屢有驗。

translations.literal: Repeatedly there were verifications.
translations.idiomatic: His readings repeatedly proved true.

sentences.zh: 高平郗超年二十餘，得重疾，試令筮之。

translations.literal: Xi Chao of Gaoping, aged more than twenty, contracted a grave illness; they tried ordering Buqian to divine by milfoil for him.
translations.idiomatic: Xi Chao of Gaoping, barely twenty, fell dangerously ill; his household had Du Buqian cast yarrow.

sentences.zh: 不愆曰：「案卦言之，卿所苦尋除。

translations.literal: Buqian said, "According to what the hexagram says, what you suffer from will soon be removed."
translations.idiomatic: Du Buqian said the hexagram promised relief.

sentences.zh: 然宜於東北三十里上宮姓家索其所養雄雉，籠盛置東簷下，卻後九日丙午日午時，必當有雌雉飛來與交，既而雙去。

translations.literal: Yet you should at thirty li to the northeast seek the caged cock raised by a family surnamed Shang on the heights, put it in a cage and place it under the eastern eaves; after nine days on bingwu day at the wu double-hour, a hen is sure to fly in and mate with it; afterward both will leave together.
translations.idiomatic: But he must fetch a penned rooster from the Shang family on the northeast hill thirty li away, set the cage under the east eaves, and on the ninth day at noon on a bing-wu day a hen would fly in, couple, and both depart.

sentences.zh: 若如此，不出二十日病都除，又是休應，年將八十，位極人臣。

translations.literal: If it is thus, within twenty days the illness will entirely be removed, and moreover it is a rest hexagram's response—you will reach nearly eighty years of age and rank as extreme as any minister of men.
translations.idiomatic: If so, within twenty days the sickness lifts and the omen adds long life—nearly eighty—and ministerial peak.

sentences.zh: 若但雌逝雄留者，病一周方差，年半八十，名位亦失。

translations.literal: If only the hen departs and the cock remains, the illness will improve after one week, the years half of eighty, and fame and position will likewise be lost.
translations.idiomatic: If the hen alone leaves, recovery takes a full week, life stops near forty, and rank is lost.

sentences.zh: 」超時正羸篤，慮命在旦夕，笑而答曰：「若保八十之半，便有餘矣。

translations.literal: At the time Chao was just emaciated and critical, worried that his life was at dawn or dusk; smiling he answered, "If it preserves half of eighty, there is surplus."
translations.idiomatic: Xi Chao, wasted and near death, laughed: half of eighty was plenty.

sentences.zh: 一周病差，何足為淹！

translations.literal: Illness improving after one week—what is sufficient to call delay!
translations.idiomatic: A week's illness—what delay is that?

sentences.zh: 」然未之信。

translations.literal: Yet he did not believe it.
translations.idiomatic: He still doubted.

sentences.zh: 或勸依其言，索雉果得。

translations.literal: Someone urged him to follow his words; seeking the cock he indeed obtained it.
translations.idiomatic: Friends pressed him to obey; he found the rooster.

sentences.zh: 至丙午日，超臥南軒之下觀之，至日晏，果有雌雉飛入籠，與雄雉交而去，雄雉不動。

translations.literal: When bingwu day came, Chao lay beneath the southern gallery observing; when the day grew late, there was indeed a hen that flew into the cage, mated with the cock, and departed; the cock did not move.
translations.idiomatic: At noon on bing-wu he watched from the south loggia: a hen flew into the cage, mounted the rooster, and flew off while the cock stayed.

sentences.zh: 超歎曰：「雖管郭之奇，何以尚此！

translations.literal: Chao sighed, saying, "Even the marvels of Guan and Guo—how could they surpass this!"
translations.idiomatic: Xi Chao marveled: even Guan Lu and Guo Pu never matched such precision.

sentences.zh: 」超病彌年乃起，至四十，卒于中書郎。

translations.literal: Chao's illness lasted a full year before he rose; when he reached forty he died as a secretary at the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he lingered a year before rising, died at forty as a Secretariat gentleman.

sentences.zh: 不愆後占筮轉疏，無復此類。

translations.literal: Buqian afterward in divination and milfoil became gradually more distant; there was no more of this kind.
translations.idiomatic: Later Du Buqian's art grew rougher; nothing again matched that feat.

sentences.zh: 後為桓嗣建威參軍。

translations.literal: Later he became aide to Huan Si's Army Who Establishes Might.
translations.idiomatic: He ended aide to Huan Si, Establishing Might general.

sentences.zh: 嚴卿

translations.literal: Yan Qing.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Qing.

sentences.zh: 嚴卿，會稽人也。

translations.literal: Yan Qing was a native of Kuaiji.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Qing came from Kuaiji.

sentences.zh: 善卜筮。

translations.literal: He was good at divination by milfoil.
translations.idiomatic: He excelled at yarrow divination.

sentences.zh: 鄉人魏序欲暫東行，荒年多抄盜，令卿筮之。

translations.literal: A townsman Wei Xu wished temporarily to travel east; in years of famine there were many bandits and robbers; he ordered Qing to divine it.
translations.idiomatic: Fellow villager Wei Xu planned an eastern journey in famine years rife with bandits and asked Yan Qing to read the omens.

sentences.zh: 卿筮曰：「君慎不可東行，必遭暴害之氣，而非劫也。

translations.literal: Qing divined and said, "You must be careful not to travel east; you are sure to encounter the qi of sudden violence, yet it will not be robbery."
translations.idiomatic: The oracle forbade the east road: violent air, not common brigands.

sentences.zh: 」序不之信。

translations.literal: Xu did not believe him.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Xu scoffed.

sentences.zh: 卿曰：「既必不停，宜以禳之，可索西郭外獨母家白雄狗系著船前。

translations.literal: Qing said, "Since you certainly will not stop, you ought to exorcise it: you may seek a white male dog from the lone mother west of the outer wall and tie it at the prow of the boat."
translations.idiomatic: If he must sail, hang a white male dog from the lone widow west of the wall on the boat's bow.

sentences.zh: 」求索止得駁狗，無白者。

translations.literal: He sought and obtained only a piebald dog; there was no white one.
translations.idiomatic: He could only find a spotted dog, none pure white.

sentences.zh: 卿曰：「駁者亦足，然猶恨其色不純，當餘小毒，正及六畜輩耳，無所復憂。

translations.literal: Qing said, "Piebald is also sufficient, yet I still regret that its color is not pure; there will remain a small poison, reaching only to the six domestic animals and the like; there is nothing further to worry about."
translations.idiomatic: Yan Qing said piebald would serve yet left a taint of venom—livestock would bear the brunt, not people.

sentences.zh: 」序行半路，狗忽然作聲甚急，有如人打之者。

translations.literal: When Xu had gone halfway on the road, the dog suddenly made sounds very urgent, as if someone were beating it.
translations.idiomatic: Mid-voyage the dog yelped as if flogged.

sentences.zh: 比視，已死，吐黑血鬥餘。

translations.literal: When they looked, it was already dead, vomiting more than a dou of black blood.
translations.idiomatic: It lay dead, heaving a dou of black blood.

sentences.zh: 其夕，序墅上白鵝數頭無故自死，而序家無恙。

translations.literal: That night several white geese on Xu's manor for no reason died of themselves, while Xu's household had no harm.
translations.idiomatic: That night his white geese dropped dead, yet the family stayed untouched.

sentences.zh: 隗炤

translations.literal: Wei Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Zhao.

sentences.zh: 隗炤，汝陰人也。

translations.literal: Wei Zhao was a native of Ruyin.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Zhao came from Ruyin.

sentences.zh: 善於《易》。

translations.literal: He was good at the Changes.
translations.idiomatic: He mastered the Book of Changes.

sentences.zh: 臨終，書版授其妻曰：「吾亡後當大荒窮，雖爾慎莫賣宅也。

translations.literal: Facing death, he wrote on a board and handed it to his wife, saying, "After my death there will be great famine and poverty; although it is so, be careful not to sell the house."
translations.idiomatic: Dying, he inscribed a board for his wife: after his death want would come—yet never sell the house.

sentences.zh: 卻後五年春，當有詔使來頓此亭，姓龔，此人負吾金，即以此版往責之，勿違言也。

translations.literal: After five years in spring, there will be an imperial envoy who stops at this post station, surnamed Gong; this person owes me gold—then take this board to go demand repayment of him; do not disobey my words.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth spring an edict-bearer surnamed Gong would lodge at their post—he owed Wei Zhao gold; she must present the board to collect—ignore the order at peril.

sentences.zh: 」炤亡後，其家大困乏，欲賣宅，憶夫言輒止。

translations.literal: After Zhao died, his household was greatly destitute; they wished to sell the house, but remembering her husband's words each time stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Poverty pressed them to sell, but his warning checked them each time.

sentences.zh: 期日，有龔使者止亭中，妻遂齎版往責之。

translations.literal: When the appointed day came, there was indeed an envoy Gong who stopped in the post station; the wife thereupon carried the board to go demand repayment of him.
translations.idiomatic: On schedule Envoy Gong arrived; she brought the tally to claim the debt.

sentences.zh: 使者執版惘然，不知所以。

translations.literal: The envoy held the board blankly, not knowing the reason.
translations.idiomatic: Gong stared at the board, baffled.

sentences.zh: 妻曰：「夫臨亡，手書版見命如此，不敢妄也。

translations.literal: The wife said, "When my husband faced death, he personally wrote on the board and showed the command thus; I dare not be reckless."
translations.idiomatic: She said her dying husband had written the instructions himself.

sentences.zh: 」使者沈吟良久而悟，謂曰：「賢夫何善？

translations.literal: The envoy pondered a long time and understood, saying to her, "In what was your worthy husband skilled?"
translations.idiomatic: After long thought Gong asked what arts her husband had.

sentences.zh: 」妻曰：「夫善於《易》，而未會為人卜也。

translations.literal: The wife said, "My husband was good at the Changes, yet never once divined for people."
translations.idiomatic: She said he knew the Changes but never took clients.

sentences.zh: 」使者曰：「噫，可知矣！

translations.literal: The envoy said, "Ah, it can be known!"
translations.idiomatic: Gong exclaimed that he understood.

sentences.zh: 」乃命取蓍筮之，卦成，撫掌而歎曰：「妙哉隗生！

translations.literal: He thereupon ordered them to bring milfoil and divine; when the hexagram was complete, he clapped his palm and sighed, saying, "Wonderful, Master Wei!"
translations.idiomatic: He cast yarrow himself and cried, "Brilliant Wei Zhao!"

sentences.zh: 含明隱跡，可謂鏡窮達而洞吉凶者也。

translations.literal: Holding brightness yet hiding his traces—he may be called one who mirrors poverty and success and thoroughly perceives auspiciousness and inauspiciousness.
translations.idiomatic: He hid brilliance yet mirrored every rise and fall of fortune.

sentences.zh: 」於是告炤妻曰：「吾不相負金也，賢夫自有金耳，知亡後當暫窮，故藏金以待太平，所以不告兒婦者，恐金盡而困無已也。

translations.literal: Thereupon he told Zhao's wife, "I do not owe your husband gold; your worthy husband himself had gold; knowing that after death there would be temporary poverty, therefore he hid gold to await peace; the reason he did not tell sons and daughters-in-law was fear that when the gold was exhausted distress would have no end."
translations.idiomatic: He told her Gong carried no debt: Wei Zhao had buried five hundred jin for the lean years, hiding it from children lest they spend the hoard and still starve.

sentences.zh: 知吾善《易》，故書版以寄意耳。

translations.literal: Knowing I am good at the Changes, therefore he wrote the board to entrust his meaning.
translations.idiomatic: He knew Gong understood the Changes, so the board was the cipher.

sentences.zh: 金有五百斤，盛以青甕，覆以銅柈，埋在堂屋東頭，去壁一丈，入地九尺。

translations.literal: The gold is five hundred jin, stored in green jars, covered with bronze platters, buried at the east end of the main hall, one zhang from the wall, nine chi into the earth.
translations.idiomatic: Five hundred jin lay in green jars under bronze lids, one zhang from the east hall wall, nine chi down.

sentences.zh: 」妻還掘之，皆如卜焉。

translations.literal: The wife returned and dug; all was as divined.
translations.idiomatic: She dug and found every coin as the yarrow said.

sentences.zh: 卜珝

translations.literal: Bu Xu.
translations.idiomatic: Bu Xu.

sentences.zh: 卜珝，字子玉，匈奴後部人也。

translations.literal: Bu Xu, courtesy name Ziyu, was a native of the Rear Division of the Xiongnu.
translations.idiomatic: Bu Xu, courtesy name Ziyu, belonged to the Xiongnu rear division.

sentences.zh: 少好讀《易》，郭璞見而歎曰：「吾所弗如也，柰何不免兵厄！

translations.literal: In his youth he loved reading the Changes; Guo Pu saw him and sighed, "What I cannot match—yet how can you avoid the calamity of weapons!"
translations.idiomatic: Guo Pu, seeing his mastery of the Changes, praised him yet foretold a violent end.

sentences.zh: 」珝曰：「然。

translations.literal: Xu said, "So it is."
translations.idiomatic: Bu Xu agreed.

sentences.zh: 吾大厄在四十一，位為卿將，當受禍耳。

translations.literal: My great calamity is at forty-one; my position will be minister and general; I shall receive disaster.
translations.idiomatic: His fate peaked at forty-one as minister-general in disaster.

sentences.zh: 不爾者，亦為猛獸所害。

translations.literal: If not that, I will likewise be harmed by a fierce beast.
translations.idiomatic: Otherwise a savage beast would kill him.

sentences.zh: 吾亦未見子之令終也。

translations.literal: I likewise have not yet seen your good end.
translations.idiomatic: Nor would Guo Pu enjoy a peaceful death, he added.

sentences.zh: 」璞曰：「吾禍在江南，甚營之，未見免兆。

translations.literal: Pu said, "My calamity is in Jiangnan; I greatly take precautions for it; I have not yet seen signs of escape."
translations.idiomatic: Guo Pu said his doom lay south of the Yangzi—he saw no escape.

sentences.zh: 雖然，在南猶可延期，住此不過時月。

translations.literal: Even so, in the south I can still prolong the term; dwelling here will not exceed months.
translations.idiomatic: Southward he might buy time; staying north gave only months.

sentences.zh: 」珝曰：「子勿為公吏，可以免諸。

translations.literal: Xu said, "You must not become a public clerk; then you can avoid the various."
translations.idiomatic: Bu Xu told him to shun official clerking to dodge fate.

sentences.zh: 」璞曰：「吾不能免公吏，猶子之不能免卿將也。

translations.literal: Pu said, "I cannot avoid being a public clerk, just as you cannot avoid being minister and general."
translations.idiomatic: Guo Pu answered that neither could flee the roles heaven chose.

sentences.zh: 」珝曰：「吾此雖當有帝王子，終不復奉二京矣。

translations.literal: Xu said, "Although here there ought to be an imperial prince, in the end I will not again serve the two capitals."
translations.idiomatic: Bu Xu predicted an imperial prince would rise yet he would never serve Luoyang or Chang'an again.

sentences.zh: 琅邪可奉，卿謹奉之，主晉祀者必此人也。

translations.literal: Langye can be served; you carefully serve him; the one who will uphold Jin's sacrifices is sure to be this man.
translations.idiomatic: Serve the house of Langye faithfully—the man who keeps the Jin altars will come from there.

sentences.zh: 」珝遂隱于龍門山。

translations.literal: Xu thereupon hid on Mount Longmen.
translations.idiomatic: Bu Xu withdrew to Mount Longmen.

sentences.zh: 劉元海僭號，徵為大司農、侍中，固以疾辭。

translations.literal: When Liu Yuanhai arrogated the title, he summoned him as Grand Minister of Agriculture and palace attendant; he firmly declined on grounds of illness.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yuan summoned him as grand minister of agriculture and palace attendant; illness was his excuse.

sentences.zh: 元海曰：「人各有心，卜珝不欲在吾朝，何異高祖四公哉！

translations.literal: Yuanhai said, "Each person has his own mind; Bu Xu not wishing to be in my court—how is it different from the Four Lords of the High Ancestor!"
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yuan likened his refusal to the recluses who snubbed Han Gaozu.

sentences.zh: 可遂其高志。

translations.literal: Let him follow his lofty intent.
translations.idiomatic: He let Bu Xu keep his lofty resolve.

sentences.zh: 」後復徵為光祿大夫，珝謂使者曰：「非吾死所也。

translations.literal: Later he was again summoned as Grand Master of Splendid Brightness; Xu said to the envoy, "It is not the place of my death."
translations.idiomatic: Later summons to grand master of splendid brightness drew his refusal: that office was not where he would die.

sentences.zh: 」及劉聰嗣偽位，徵為太常。

translations.literal: When Liu Cong succeeded to the false throne, he summoned him as Grand Master of Ceremonies.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Cong named him grand master of ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 時劉琨據并州，聰問何時可平，珝答曰：「并州陛下之分，今茲克之必矣。

translations.literal: At the time Liu Kun held Bing Province; Cong asked when it could be pacified; Xu answered, "Bing Province is Your Majesty's division; now this year taking it is sure."
translations.idiomatic: Liu Cong asked when Liu Kun's Bingzhou would fall. Bu Xu said it belonged to the barbarian house and would fall that year.

sentences.zh: 」聰戲曰：「朕欲勞先生一行可乎？

translations.literal: Cong jested, "I wish to trouble the master to go on one journey—may it be done?"
translations.idiomatic: Liu Cong teased whether Bu Xu would lead the campaign.

sentences.zh: 」珝曰：「臣所以來不及裝者，正為是行也。

translations.literal: Xu said, "The reason your servant came without finishing packing is precisely for this journey."
translations.idiomatic: Bu Xu said he had hurried north unfinished precisely to take that march.

sentences.zh: 」聰大悅，署珝使持節、平北將軍。

translations.literal: Cong was greatly pleased and appointed Xu bearer of credentials, General Who Pacifies the North.
translations.idiomatic: Delighted, Liu Cong made him credential-bearing general who pacifies the north.

sentences.zh: 將行，謂其妹曰：「此行也，死自吾分，後慎勿紛紜。

translations.literal: About to depart, he said to his younger sister, "In this journey, death is my lot; afterward be careful not to make confusion."
translations.idiomatic: Before leaving he told his sister the campaign meant his death and begged her not to stir strife afterward.

sentences.zh: 」及攻晉陽，為琨所敗，珝卒先奔，為其元帥所殺。

translations.literal: When they attacked Jinyang, they were defeated by Kun; Xu was the first to flee in rout and was killed by his commander-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: At Jinyang Liu Kun routed the host; Bu Xu ran first and his commander-in-chief executed him for it.

sentences.zh: 鮑靚

translations.literal: Bao Jing.
translations.idiomatic: Bao Jing.

sentences.zh: 鮑靚，字太玄，東海人也。

translations.literal: Bao Jing, courtesy name Taixuan, was a native of Donghai.
translations.idiomatic: Bao Jing, courtesy name Taixuan, came from Donghai.

sentences.zh: 年五歲，語父母云：「本是曲陽李家兒，九歲墜井死。

translations.literal: At age five he told his parents, saying, "Originally I was a son of the Li family of Quyang; at nine I fell into a well and died."
translations.idiomatic: At five he told his parents he had been a Li boy in Quyang who drowned in a well at nine.

sentences.zh: 」其父母尋訪得李氏，推問皆符驗。

translations.literal: His parents searched and found the Li family; pushing the inquiry, everything matched and verified.
translations.idiomatic: They traced the Li household and every detail matched.

sentences.zh: 靚學兼內外，明天文河洛書，稍遷南陽中部都尉，為南海太守。

translations.literal: Jing's learning embraced inner and outer; he understood astronomy and Hetu-Luo writings; he was gradually promoted to central commandant of Nanyang and became governor of Nanhai.
translations.idiomatic: He mastered Confucian and occult lore, astronomy, and River Chart texts, rose to Nanyang commandant, then Nanhai governor.

sentences.zh: 嘗行部入海，遇風，饑甚，取白石煮食之以自濟。

translations.literal: Once on a circuit he entered the sea, met wind, and was extremely hungry; he took white stones, boiled them, and ate them to save himself.
translations.idiomatic: Caught in a gale at sea, he boiled white stones to stay alive.

sentences.zh: 王機時為廣州刺史，入廁，忽見二人著烏衣，與機相捍，良久擒之，得二物似烏鴨。

translations.literal: Wang Ji at the time was governor of Guang Province; entering the privy, he suddenly saw two persons in black garments grappling with Ji; after a long time he seized them and obtained two things resembling crows.
translations.idiomatic: Guangzhou governor Wang Ji, in his privy, wrestled two black-clad figures into two crow-shaped things.

sentences.zh: 靚曰：「此物不祥。

translations.literal: Jing said, "These things are inauspicious."
translations.idiomatic: Bao Jing called them ill omens.

sentences.zh: 」機焚之，徑飛上天，機尋誅死。

translations.literal: Ji burned them; they flew straight up to heaven; before long Ji was executed and died.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ji burned them; they shot skyward; soon he was executed.

sentences.zh: 靚嘗見仙人陰君，授道訣，百餘歲卒。

translations.literal: Jing once met the transcendent Lord Yin, who handed him Dao formulas; he died aged more than a hundred.
translations.idiomatic: He met transcendent Yin Jun, received Dao formulas, and died past a hundred.

sentences.zh: 吳猛

translations.literal: Wu Meng.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Meng.

sentences.zh: 吳猛，豫章人也。

translations.literal: Wu Meng was a native of Yuzhang.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Meng came from Yuzhang.

sentences.zh: 少有孝行，夏日常手不驅蚊，懼其去己而噬親也。

translations.literal: In his youth he had filial conduct; in summer he commonly did not drive away mosquitoes with his hands, fearing that leaving himself they would bite his parents.
translations.idiomatic: In summer he let mosquitoes bite his own flesh lest they reach his parents.

sentences.zh: 年四十，邑人丁義始授其神方。

translations.literal: At forty a townsman Ding Yi first handed him spirit formulas.
translations.idiomatic: At forty Ding Yi of his town gave him spirit recipes.

sentences.zh: 因還豫章，江波甚急，猛不假舟楫，以白羽扇畫水而渡，觀者異之。

translations.literal: Returning to Yuzhang, the river waves were very swift; Meng did not borrow boat or oar, but with a white feather fan traced the water and crossed; observers marveled at him.
translations.idiomatic: Returning to Yuzhang he fanned the rapids with a white feather fan and walked the waves while crowds gaped.

sentences.zh: 庾亮為江州刺史，嘗遇疾，聞猛神異，乃迎之，問己疾何如。

translations.literal: Yu Liang was governor of Jiang Province; he once fell ill; hearing of Meng's spiritlike strangeness, he therefore welcomed him and asked how his illness was.
translations.idiomatic: Jiangzhou governor Yu Liang, ill, summoned the wonder-worker Wu Meng to ask his prognosis.

sentences.zh: 猛辭以算盡，請具棺服。

translations.literal: Meng declined on the ground that his reckoning was exhausted, and requested to prepare coffin garments.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Meng said his allotted span was spent and asked for shroud and coffin.

sentences.zh: 旬日而死，形狀如生。

translations.literal: Within ten days he died; his form was as if alive.
translations.idiomatic: Within ten days he was dead, yet looked as though he merely slept.

sentences.zh: 未及大斂，遂失其屍。

translations.literal: Before the great laying-in, his corpse then disappeared.
translations.idiomatic: Before the lying-in-state, the body vanished.

sentences.zh: 識者以為亮不祥之徵。

translations.literal: Those with insight deemed it an ill-omened sign for Liang.
translations.idiomatic: Knowledgable men took it for a dark portent for Yu Liang.

sentences.zh: 亮疾果不起。

translations.literal: Liang's illness indeed did not recover.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Liang's sickness proved fatal.

sentences.zh: 幸靈

translations.literal: Xing Ling.
translations.idiomatic: Xing Ling.

sentences.zh: 幸靈者，豫章建昌人也。

translations.literal: Xing Ling was a native of Jianchang in Yuzhang.
translations.idiomatic: Xing Ling came from Jianchang in Yuzhang commandery.

sentences.zh: 性少言，與小人群居，見侵辱而無慍色，邑裏號之癡，雖其父母兄弟亦以為癡也。

translations.literal: By nature he spoke little; he dwelt among common folk; when insulted he showed no angry look; the village called him a fool—even his parents and brothers thought him a fool.
translations.idiomatic: He was a man of few words who lived among laborers, bore insult without anger, and was dismissed by kin and neighbors alike as simple-minded.

sentences.zh: 嘗使守稻，群牛食之，靈見而不驅，待牛去乃往理其殘亂者。

translations.literal: Once they had him guard the rice; a herd of cattle ate it; Ling saw but did not drive them, waiting until the cattle left before going to put in order what was broken and disordered.
translations.idiomatic: Set to watch the paddies, he let cattle graze unmolested, then straightened the trampled stalks once they wandered off.

sentences.zh: 其父母見而怒之，靈曰：「夫萬物生天地之間，各欲得食。

translations.literal: His parents saw and were angry with him; Ling said, "The myriad things born between Heaven and Earth each wish to obtain food."
translations.idiomatic: His parents raged; he answered that every creature under heaven must eat.

sentences.zh: 牛方食，柰何驅之！

translations.literal: The cattle are just eating—how can I drive them!
translations.idiomatic: The oxen were feeding—why drive them away?

sentences.zh: 」其父愈怒曰：「即如汝言，復用理壞者何為？

translations.literal: His father was still more angry and said, "If it is just as you say, what is the use again of putting in order what is ruined?"
translations.idiomatic: His father snapped: if that were true, why bother straightening ruined grain?

sentences.zh: 」靈曰：「此稻又欲得終其性，牛自犯之，靈可以不收乎！」

translations.literal: Ling said, "This rice again wishes to fulfill its nature; the cattle themselves violated it—how can Ling not gather it in!"
translations.idiomatic: He replied that the crop too had its nature to fulfill; the beasts had wronged it, and he must restore what he could.

sentences.zh: 時順陽樊長賓為建昌令，發百姓作官船於建城山中，吏令人各作箸一雙。

translations.literal: At the time Fan Changbin of Shunyang was magistrate of Jianchang; he drafted the common people to build official boats in the mountains of Jiancheng; clerks ordered each person to make one pair of chopsticks.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Changbin of Shunyang, then Jianchang magistrate, levied labor to build government barges in Jiancheng hills and ordered every household to carve one pair of chopsticks.

sentences.zh: 靈作而未輸，或竊之焉。

translations.literal: Ling made them but had not yet delivered them; someone stole them.
translations.idiomatic: Xing Ling carved his pair but someone stole them before delivery.

sentences.zh: 俄而竊者心痛欲死，靈謂之曰：「爾得無竊我箸乎？

translations.literal: Before long the thief's heart hurt as if dying; Ling said to him, "Could it be that you stole my chopsticks?"
translations.idiomatic: Soon the thief doubled over with cardiac pain until Xing Ling asked if he had stolen the chopsticks.

sentences.zh: 」竊者不應。

translations.literal: The thief did not answer.
translations.idiomatic: The thief stayed silent.

sentences.zh: 有頃，愈急，靈曰：「若爾不以情告我者，今真死矣。

translations.literal: After a moment it grew worse; Ling said, "If you do not tell me the truth, now you will truly die."
translations.idiomatic: As the pain sharpened, Xing Ling warned that only a confession would lift the curse.

sentences.zh: 」竊者急遽，乃首出之。

translations.literal: The thief, urgent and hasty, then confessed it.
translations.idiomatic: The thief confessed in panic.

sentences.zh: 靈於是飲之以水，病即立愈。

translations.literal: Ling thereupon gave him to drink water, and the illness immediately improved.
translations.idiomatic: Xing Ling gave him water and the fit vanished.

sentences.zh: 行人由此敬畏之。

translations.literal: Travelers from this revered him.
translations.idiomatic: Wayfarers spread word of his power and learned to fear him.

sentences.zh: 船成，當下，吏以二百人引一艘，不能動，方請益人。

translations.literal: When the boats were finished and were to be launched downstream, clerks used two hundred men to pull one vessel and could not move it; they were about to request more men.
translations.idiomatic: Two hundred men could not budge a finished hull downstream; the overseers meant to call for more hands.

sentences.zh: 靈曰：「此以過足，但部分未至耳。

translations.literal: Ling said, "This force is already more than enough; only the disposition has not yet arrived."
translations.idiomatic: Xing Ling said the haulers were ample—the formation was wrong.

sentences.zh: 靈請自牽之。

translations.literal: Ling requested to pull it himself.
translations.idiomatic: He asked to take the lines himself.

sentences.zh: 」乃手執箸，惟用百人，而船去如流。

translations.literal: Thereupon he personally held the chopsticks, using only a hundred men, and the boat went like flowing water.
translations.idiomatic: Gripping his chopsticks, he used just a hundred men and the hull slid like a current.

sentences.zh: 眾大驚怪，咸稱其神，於是知名。

translations.literal: The crowd was greatly astonished and strange; all called him spiritlike; from this he became known.
translations.idiomatic: The crowd cried miracle and his fame spread.

sentences.zh: 有龔仲儒女病積年，氣息財屬，靈使以水含之，已而強起，應時大愈。

translations.literal: There was the daughter of Gong Zhongru who had been ill many years, her breath just continuous; Ling had her hold water in the mouth; afterward she forcibly rose and at the proper time greatly recovered.
translations.idiomatic: Gong Zhongru's daughter had lain at death's door for years; he had her rinse with water, then she sat up and healed.

sentences.zh: 又呂猗母皇氏得痿痹病，十有餘年，靈療之，去皇氏數尺而坐，冥目寂然，有頃，顧謂猗曰：「扶夫人令起。

translations.literal: Again Lu Yi's mother Lady Huang contracted atrophy-paralysis illness for more than ten years; Ling treated her, sitting several chi from Lady Huang, eyes closed in stillness; after a moment he looked back and told Yi, "Support the lady and order her to rise."
translations.idiomatic: Lu Yi's mother Huang had been paralyzed a decade; Xing Ling sat in trance yards away, then told Yi to raise her.

sentences.zh: 」猗曰：「老人得病累年，奈何可倉卒起邪？

translations.literal: Yi said, "The old woman has been ill many years—how can she suddenly rise?"
translations.idiomatic: Lu Yi protested that an aged invalid could not simply stand.

sentences.zh: 」靈曰：「但試扶起。

translations.literal: Ling said, "Only try supporting her to rise."
translations.idiomatic: Xing Ling insisted they try.

sentences.zh: 」於是兩人夾扶以立。

translations.literal: Thereupon two people supported her on the sides to stand.
translations.idiomatic: Two servants propped her upright.

sentences.zh: 少選，靈又令去扶，即能自行，由此遂愈。

translations.literal: After a short while Ling again ordered them to remove the support, and she was able to walk by herself; from this she then recovered.
translations.idiomatic: Moments later he bade them let go; she walked unaided and thereafter recovered.

sentences.zh: 於是百姓奔趣，水陸輻輳，從之如雲。

translations.literal: Thereupon commoners rushed to him; by water and land they converged like spokes to a hub; those who followed him were like clouds.
translations.idiomatic: Commoners flocked from every road and river until his following swelled like clouds.

sentences.zh: 皇氏自以病久，懼有發動，靈乃留水一器令食之，每取水，輒以新水補處，二十餘年水清如新，塵垢不能加焉。

translations.literal: Lady Huang, because the illness had been long, feared there might be a relapse; Ling then left one vessel of water and ordered her to eat from it; each time she drew water he always replenished the place with fresh water; for more than twenty years the water was clear as new; dust and filth could not adhere to it.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing relapse, she kept his water jar—each draught she refilled, and for twenty years the water stayed pure as when he charmed it.

sentences.zh: 時高悝家有鬼怪，言語訶叱，投擲內外，不見人形，或器物自行，再三發火，巫祝厭劾而不能絕。

translations.literal: At the time Gao Kui's household had a ghost that spoke and scolded, threw things inside and outside, showed no human form; sometimes utensils moved themselves; repeatedly fire broke out; shamans exorcised but could not stop it.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Kui's house was plagued by a poltergeist—voices, flying objects, self-moving tools, recurrent fires—shamans failed to quell it.

sentences.zh: 適值靈，乃要之。

translations.literal: It happened to meet Ling, and they therefore invited him.
translations.idiomatic: They met Xing Ling and pressed him to help.

sentences.zh: 靈於陌頭望其屋，謂悝曰：「此君之家邪？

translations.literal: Ling at the end of the lane looked at the house and said to Kui, "Is this your lord's home?"
translations.idiomatic: From the lane mouth he asked Gao Kui if that was his roof.

sentences.zh: 」悝曰：「是也。

translations.literal: Kui said, "It is so."
translations.idiomatic: Kui confirmed it.

sentences.zh: 」靈曰：「知之足矣。

translations.literal: Ling said, "Knowing is enough."
translations.idiomatic: Xing Ling said knowing sufficed.

sentences.zh: 」悝固請之，靈不得已，至門，見符索甚多，謂悝曰：「當以正止邪，而以邪救邪，惡得已乎！

translations.literal: Kui firmly requested him; Ling, having no choice, reached the gate, saw very many talisman cords, and said to Kui, "One ought to use the straight to stop the deviant, yet you use the deviant to save the deviant—how can it be stopped!"
translations.idiomatic: Pressed to enter, he saw talismans plastered everywhere and scolded Kui for fighting wrong with wrong.

sentences.zh: 」並使焚之，惟據軒小坐而去，其夕鬼怪即絕。

translations.literal: He had them all burned, only leaned on the railing for a short sit and departed; that night the ghost then ceased.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered the charms burned, lingered briefly on the porch, and that night the haunting ended.

sentences.zh: 靈所救愈多此類，然不取報謝。

translations.literal: What Ling saved and healed was mostly of this kind, yet he did not take repayment or thanks.
translations.idiomatic: He cured countless folk yet took no fee.

sentences.zh: 行不騎乘，長不娶妻，性至恭，見人即先拜，言輒自名。

translations.literal: In travel he did not ride mounts; grown up he did not take a wife; his nature was extremely deferential—seeing people he first bowed and in speech always gave his own name.
translations.idiomatic: He walked everywhere, never married, bowed first to every passerby, and always named himself in speech.

sentences.zh: 凡草木之夭傷于山林者，必起理之，器物之傾覆于途路者，必舉正之。

translations.literal: Whenever plants or trees had early harm in mountain forests, he was sure to rise and put them in order; whenever utensils had overturned on roads, he was sure to lift and right them.
translations.idiomatic: He straightened broken saplings in the hills and righted overturned jars on the road.

sentences.zh: 周旋江州間，謂其士人曰：「天地之於人物，一也，咸欲不失其情性，奈何制服人以為奴婢乎！

translations.literal: Moving about between Jiang Province he said to its gentlemen, "Heaven and Earth's relation to people and things is one; all wish not to lose their genuine nature—why bind people and make them slaves and maids!"
translations.idiomatic: He told Jiangzhou gentry that heaven treats all beings alike—why turn men into bondservants?

sentences.zh: 諸君若欲享多福以保性命，可悉免遣之。

translations.literal: If you gentlemen wish to enjoy abundant blessing and preserve life, you may all release and send them away.
translations.idiomatic: Release your slaves, he urged, if they sought fortune and long life.

sentences.zh: 」十餘年間，賴其術以濟者極多。

translations.literal: Within more than ten years those who relied on his art to be saved were extremely many.
translations.idiomatic: For a decade multitudes owed him their lives.

sentences.zh: 後乃娶妻，畜車以奴婢，受貨賂致遺，於是其術稍衰，所療得失相半焉。

translations.literal: Later he then took a wife, kept carriages with slave girls, received goods bribes and sent gifts, and thereupon his arts gradually declined; what he treated had gain and loss half and half.
translations.idiomatic: Later he wed, kept carriage and concubines, took fees, and his cures hit or miss.

sentences.zh: 佛圖澄

translations.literal: Fotucheng.
translations.idiomatic: Fotucheng.

sentences.zh: 佛圖澄，天竺人也。

translations.literal: Fotucheng was a native of Tianzhu.
translations.idiomatic: Fotucheng came from India.

sentences.zh: 本姓帛氏。

translations.literal: His original surname was the Bo clan.
translations.idiomatic: His clan had originally been Bo.

sentences.zh: 少學道，妙通玄術。

translations.literal: In his youth he studied the Way and wonderfully penetrated arcane arts.
translations.idiomatic: Youthful Dao study gave him mastery of occult technique.

sentences.zh: ，來適洛陽，自雲百有餘歲，常服氣自養，能積日不食。

translations.literal: Coming to Luoyang, he said of himself that he was more than a hundred years old; he constantly ingested qi to nurture himself and could go many days without eating.
translations.idiomatic: He reached Luoyang claiming a century of age, nourished himself on breath, and fasted for days on end.

sentences.zh: 善誦神咒，能役使鬼神。

translations.literal: He was good at reciting spirit spells and could command ghosts and spirits.
translations.idiomatic: He chanted dharanis and commanded ghosts and gods.

sentences.zh: 腹旁有一孔，常以絮塞之，每夜讀書，則拔絮，孔中出光，照於一室。

translations.literal: Beside his belly there was one hole; he constantly plugged it with floss; each night when reading books he then pulled out the floss; from the hole light emerged, illuminating one room.
translations.idiomatic: A hole in his flank, corked with cotton, blazed forth lamplight each night he read.

sentences.zh: 又嘗齋時，平旦至流水側，從腹旁孔中引出五藏六府洗之，訖，還內腹中。

translations.literal: Again, once during fast days, at dawn he went to the side of running water, drew out the five zang and six fu from the hole beside his belly, washed them, finished, and returned them inside the belly.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn on a fast day he drew organs from the aperture, rinsed them in running water, and tucked them back.

sentences.zh: 又能聽鈴音以言吉凶，莫不懸驗。

translations.literal: Again he could listen to bell sounds and speak of auspiciousness and inauspiciousness; none failed to verify in advance.
translations.idiomatic: Temple bells told him fortune, and every omen proved true.

sentences.zh: 及洛中寇亂，乃潛草野以觀變。

translations.literal: When banditry and chaos struck Luoyang, he then hid in the wild grass to observe the changes.
translations.idiomatic: Luoyang's turmoil drove him to lie low in the weeds and watch events.

sentences.zh: 石勒屯兵葛陂，專行殺戮，沙門遇害者其眾。

translations.literal: Shi Le stationed troops at Gebei and exclusively carried out slaughter; very many shramanas encountered harm.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Le camped at Gebei in slaughter; monks died in droves.

sentences.zh: 澄投勒大將軍郭黑略家，黑略每從勒征伐，輒豫克勝負，勒疑而問曰：「孤不覺卿有出眾智謀，而每知軍行吉凶何也？

translations.literal: Cheng threw himself on the house of Le's great general Guo Heilie; Heilie each time followed Le on campaigns and always beforehand knew victory and defeat; Le doubted and asked, "I do not perceive that you have outstanding wisdom and stratagem—yet how is it you always know the army's march auspicious or inauspicious?"
translations.idiomatic: Fotucheng sheltered with general Guo Heilie, whose uncanny forecasts of battle Shi Le credited until he demanded an explanation.

sentences.zh: 」黑略曰：「將軍天挺神武，幽靈所助，有一沙門智術非常，雲將軍當略有區夏，己應為師。

translations.literal: Heilie said, "The general is heaven-endowed divine martial; dark spirits aid him; there is one shramana whose wisdom and arts are extraordinary; he says the general ought to seize the Xia regions and I ought to be his teacher."
translations.idiomatic: Heilie said a monk of rare power prophesied Shi Le's conquest of the heartland and named himself the general's teacher.

sentences.zh: 臣前後所白，皆其言也。

translations.literal: What your servant has reported before and after is all his words.
translations.idiomatic: Every counsel Heilie had offered came from the monk.

sentences.zh: 」勒召澄，試以道術。

translations.literal: Le summoned Cheng and tested him with Dao arts.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Le summoned Fotucheng to test his powers.

sentences.zh: 澄即取缽盛水，燒香咒之，須臾缽中生青蓮花，光色曜日，勒由此信之。

translations.literal: Cheng immediately took a bowl, filled it with water, burned incense and chanted over it; in a moment in the bowl a green lotus flower was born, its light dazzling the sun; Le from this believed him.
translations.idiomatic: Fotucheng conjured a blazing green lotus in a water bowl, and Shi Le believed.

sentences.zh: 勒自葛陂還河北，過枋頭，枋頭人夜欲斫營，澄謂黑略曰：「須臾賊至，可令公知。

translations.literal: When Le returned from Gebei to Hebei, passing Fangtou, the people of Fangtou at night wished to raid the camp; Cheng told Heilie, "In a moment bandits will arrive—you may let the duke know."
translations.idiomatic: Marching past Fangtou, Fotucheng warned Guo Heilie of a night raid so Shi Le could ready the camp.

sentences.zh: 」果如其言，有備，故不敗。

translations.literal: It indeed happened as he said; there was preparation, therefore they were not defeated.
translations.idiomatic: The raid came as foretold but met prepared defenses.

sentences.zh: 勒欲試澄，夜冠胄衣甲，執刀而坐，遣人告澄云：「夜來不知大將軍何所在。

translations.literal: Le wished to test Cheng; at night he donned helmet and armor, grasped a knife and sat, sent a person to tell Cheng, saying, "In the night we do not know where the great general is."
translations.idiomatic: Shi Le donned armor one night and sent a messenger pretending not to find him—a test of the monk.

sentences.zh: 」使人始至，未及有言，澄逆問曰：「平居無寇，何故夜嚴？

translations.literal: When the messenger had just arrived, before there were words, Cheng preemptively asked, "In ordinary times without bandits, why strictness at night?"
translations.idiomatic: Fotucheng intercepted the envoy: "No raiders threaten—why the midnight alert?"

sentences.zh: 」勒益信之。

translations.literal: Le still more believed him.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Le's faith deepened.

sentences.zh: 勒後因忿，欲害諸道士，並欲苦澄。

translations.literal: Later Le because of anger wished to harm the various Daoists and also wished to torment Cheng.
translations.idiomatic: Later, in a rage, Shi Le meant to kill Daoist priests and torture Fotucheng.

sentences.zh: 澄乃潛避至黑略舍，語弟子曰：「若將軍信至，問吾所在者，報雲不知所之。

translations.literal: Cheng then secretly fled to Heilie's quarters, telling his disciples, "If the general's messenger arrives and asks where I am, report saying you do not know where he has gone."
translations.idiomatic: Fotucheng hid with Guo Heilie and told disciples to feign ignorance of his whereabouts.

sentences.zh: 」既而勒使至，覓澄不得。

translations.literal: Before long Le's messenger arrived and could not find Cheng.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Le's runners found no trace of him.

sentences.zh: 使還報勒，勒驚曰：「吾有惡意向澄，澄舍我去矣。

translations.literal: The messenger returned and reported to Le; Le startled said, "I had an evil intent toward Cheng; Cheng has abandoned me and left."
translations.idiomatic: Shi Le panicked, fearing his ill will had driven the monk away.

sentences.zh: 」通夜不寢，思欲見澄。

translations.literal: Through the night he did not sleep, thinking he wished to see Cheng.
translations.idiomatic: He lay sleepless, longing to see him.

sentences.zh: 澄知勒意悔，明旦造勒。

translations.literal: Cheng knew Le's mind repented; at dawn he visited Le.
translations.idiomatic: Sensing remorse, Fotucheng appeared at dawn.

sentences.zh: 勒曰：「昨夜何行？

translations.literal: Le said, "Where did you go last night?"
translations.idiomatic: Shi Le asked where he had been the night before.

sentences.zh: 」澄曰：「公有怒心，昨故權避公。

translations.literal: Cheng said, "Your lordship had an angry mind; yesterday I therefore temporarily avoided your lordship."
translations.idiomatic: Fotucheng said he had dodged the duke's wrath.

sentences.zh: 今改意，是以敢來。

translations.literal: Now your mind has changed; therefore I dare to come.
translations.idiomatic: Now that the temper had passed, he dared return.

sentences.zh: 勒大笑曰：「道人謬矣。」

translations.literal: Le laughed greatly and said, "The Daoist is mistaken."
translations.idiomatic: Shi Le laughed and called him a sly monk.

sentences.zh: 襄國城塹水源在城西北五里，其水源暴竭，勒問澄何以致水。

translations.literal: The moat water source of Xiangguo city lay five li northwest of the city; its water source suddenly dried up; Le asked Cheng how to bring water.
translations.idiomatic: Xiangguo's moat ran dry; Shi Le asked Fotucheng to restore it.

sentences.zh: 澄曰：「今當敕龍取水。

translations.literal: Cheng said, "Now we ought to command the dragon to fetch water."
translations.idiomatic: Fotucheng said he would bid a dragon to refill the spring.

sentences.zh: 」乃與弟子法首等數人至故泉源上，坐繩床，燒安息香，咒願數百言。

translations.literal: Thereupon with disciples such as Fashou, several persons, he went to the old spring source, sat on a rope bed, burned benzoin incense, and chanted vows several hundred words.
translations.idiomatic: He and disciples like Fashou sat rope beds at the dry head, burned frankincense, and chanted hundreds of lines.

sentences.zh: 如此三日，水泫然微流，有一小龍長五六寸許，隨水而來，諸道士競往觀之。

translations.literal: Thus for three days the water trickled in a thin flow; there was one small dragon about five or six cun long that came with the water; the various Daoists vied to go observe it.
translations.idiomatic: After three days a trickle began; a six-inch dragon rode the flow while Daoists crowded to watch.

sentences.zh: 有頃，水大至，隍塹皆滿。

translations.literal: After a moment the water arrived in great volume; moat and ditch were all full.
translations.idiomatic: Soon torrents filled ditch and moat.

sentences.zh: 鮮卑段末波攻勒，眾甚盛。

translations.literal: The Xianbei Duan Mobo attacked Le; his host was very large.
translations.idiomatic: Xianbei chieftain Duan Mobo besieged Shi Le with a mighty host.

sentences.zh: 勒懼，問澄。

translations.literal: Le was afraid and questioned Cheng.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Le, afraid, consulted Fotucheng.

sentences.zh: 澄曰：「昨日寺鈴鳴雲，明旦食時，當擒段末波。

translations.literal: Cheng said, "Yesterday the monastery bell sounded saying, at the meal hour tomorrow morning, you will seize Duan Mobo."
translations.idiomatic: Fotucheng said the stupa bell had promised Duan Mobo's capture by breakfast next day.

sentences.zh: 」勒登城望末波軍，不見前後，失色曰：「末波如此，豈可獲乎！

translations.literal: Le ascended the city and gazed at Mobo's army, not seeing front or rear, changed color and said, "Mobo like this—how can he be captured!"
translations.idiomatic: From the wall Shi Le saw endless ranks and despaired of taking Mobo.

sentences.zh: 」更遣夔安問澄。

translations.literal: He again sent Kui An to ask Cheng.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Kui An back to the monk.

sentences.zh: 澄曰：「已獲末波矣。

translations.literal: Cheng said, "Mobo has already been captured."
translations.idiomatic: Fotucheng said Mobo was already taken.

sentences.zh: 」時城北伏兵出，遇末波，執之。

translations.literal: At the time ambush troops north of the city came out, encountered Mobo, and seized him.
translations.idiomatic: Northern ambushers sprang forth and seized Duan Mobo.

sentences.zh: 澄勸勒宥末波，遣還本國，勒從之，卒獲其用。

translations.literal: Cheng urged Le to spare Mobo and send him back to his native state; Le followed this and in the end obtained his service.
translations.idiomatic: Fotucheng urged mercy; Shi Le released Mobo and later profited from his loyalty.

sentences.zh: 劉曜遣從弟岳攻勒，勒遣石季龍距之。

translations.literal: Liu Yao sent his cousin Yue to attack Le; Le sent Shi Jilong to resist him.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yao sent cousin Liu Yue against Shi Le, who answered with Shi Hu.

sentences.zh: 嶽敗，退保石梁塢，季龍堅柵守之。

translations.literal: Yue was defeated, withdrew and guarded Stone Beam Redoubt; Jilong firmly palisaded and guarded it.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yue retreated to Shiliang stockade; Shi Hu locked palisades around him.

sentences.zh: 澄在襄國，忽歎曰：「劉嶽可憫！

translations.literal: Cheng in Xiangguo suddenly sighed, saying, "Liu Yue is pitiable!"
translations.idiomatic: From Xiangguo Fotucheng cried that Liu Yue was doomed.

sentences.zh: 」弟子法祚問其故，澄曰「昨日亥時，嶽已敗被執。

translations.literal: The disciple Fazuo asked the reason; Cheng said, "Yesterday at the hai double-hour Yue had already been defeated and captured."
translations.idiomatic: Disciple Fazuo asked why; Fotucheng said Liu Yue had fallen at the previous day's hai hour.

sentences.zh: 」果如所言。

translations.literal: It indeed happened as he said.
translations.idiomatic: News proved him right.

sentences.zh: 及曜自攻洛陽，勒將救之，其群下咸諫以為不可。

translations.literal: When Yao personally attacked Luoyang, Le was about to rescue it; all his subordinates together remonstrated deeming it impossible.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Yao besieged Luoyang, Shi Le meant to march; every minister called it folly.

sentences.zh: 勒以訪澄，澄曰：「相輪鈴音云：'秀支替戾岡，僕穀劬禿當。

translations.literal: Le consulted Cheng; Cheng said, "The sound of the stupa-wheel bell says: 'Xiuzhi tiligang, pugu qutu dang."
translations.idiomatic: Fotucheng cited the stupa bell's Jie-language line: 'Xiuzhi tiligang, pugu qutu dang.'

sentences.zh: 」此羯語也，秀支，軍也。

translations.literal: This is Jie language; xiuzhi means army.
translations.idiomatic: That tongue was Jie: xiuzhi meant 'army.'

sentences.zh: 替戾岡，出也。

translations.literal: Tiligang means go out.
translations.idiomatic: Tiligang meant 'march forth.'

sentences.zh: 僕谷，劉曜胡位也。

translations.literal: Pugu is Liu Yao's Hu title.
translations.idiomatic: Pugu was the Jie title for Liu Yao.

sentences.zh: 劬禿當，捉也。

translations.literal: Qutu dang means seize.
translations.idiomatic: Qutu dang meant 'capture.'

sentences.zh: 此言軍出捉得曜也。

translations.literal: This says the army goes out and seizes and obtains Yao.
translations.idiomatic: The verse meant the host would march out and take Liu Yao alive.

sentences.zh: 」又令一童子潔齋七日，取麻油合胭脂，躬自研於掌中，舉手示童子，粲然有輝。

translations.literal: Again he ordered one boy, purifying fast for seven days, to take sesame oil mixed with rouge; he personally ground it in his palm, raised his hand to show the boy, and there was a brilliant gleam.
translations.idiomatic: He had a lad fast seven days, then rubbed sesame oil and rouge in his palm until it flashed blindingly for the boy to see.

sentences.zh: 童子驚曰：「有軍馬甚眾，見一人長大白晳，以硃絲縛其肘。

translations.literal: The boy startled said, "There are very many army horses; I see one man, tall, white and bright, with cinnabar silk binding his elbow."
translations.idiomatic: The boy cried that he saw hosts of cavalry and a tall pale man with red cord wound round his arm.

sentences.zh: 」澄曰：「此即曜也。

translations.literal: Cheng said, "This is indeed Yao."
translations.idiomatic: Fotucheng said that man was Liu Yao.

sentences.zh: 」勒其悅，遂赴洛距曜，生擒之。

translations.literal: Le was greatly pleased; thereupon he went to Luoyang to resist Yao and seized him alive.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Le rejoiced, marched to Luoyang, and took Liu Yao prisoner.

sentences.zh: 勒僭稱趙天王，行皇帝事，敬澄彌篤。

translations.literal: Le arrogated the title King of Zhao and carried out emperor's affairs; he revered Cheng still more deeply.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Le styled himself Zhao heaven-king and ruled as emperor while honoring Fotucheng ever more deeply.

sentences.zh: 時石蔥將叛，澄誡勒曰：「今年蔥中有蟲，食必害人，可令百姓無食蔥也。

translations.literal: At the time Shi Cong was about to rebel; Cheng warned Le, saying, "This year in scallions there are worms; eating them is sure to harm people—you may order the common people not to eat scallions."
translations.idiomatic: When Shi Cong plotted revolt, Fotucheng warned that worm-ridden scallions would poison anyone who ate them.

sentences.zh: 」勒班告境內，慎無食蔥。

translations.literal: Le issued an order proclaiming within the borders to be careful not to eat scallions.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Le banned scallions across the realm.

sentences.zh: 俄而石蔥果走。

translations.literal: Before long Shi Cong indeed fled.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Cong soon fled as foretold.

sentences.zh: 勒益重之，事必諮而後行，號曰大和尚。

translations.literal: Le still more esteemed him; for affairs he was sure to consult him before acting; he styled him Great Monk.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Le deferred on every policy and titled him Great Monk.

sentences.zh: 勒愛子斌暴病死，將殯，勒歎曰：「朕聞虢太子死，扁鵲能生之，今可得效乎？

translations.literal: Le's beloved son Bin died suddenly of illness; about to encoffin him, Le sighed, "I have heard that when the crown prince of Guo died, Bian Que could revive him—may we now obtain that effect?"
translations.idiomatic: Shi Le's favorite Shi Bin died young; the king wondered if Fotucheng could repeat Bian Que's revival of Guo's heir.

sentences.zh: 」乃令告澄。

translations.literal: Thereupon he ordered Cheng to be told.
translations.idiomatic: He summoned Fotucheng.

sentences.zh: 澄取楊枝沾水，灑而咒之。

translations.literal: Cheng took a willow branch, dipped it in water, sprinkled and chanted over him.
translations.idiomatic: The monk sprinkled Bin with willow water and chanted.

sentences.zh: 就執斌手曰：「可起矣！

translations.literal: He grasped Bin's hand and said, "You may rise!"
translations.idiomatic: He seized the boy's hand and commanded him to rise.

sentences.zh: 」因此遂蘇，有頃，平復。

translations.literal: From this he then revived; after a moment he was calm and recovered.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Bin stirred, then fully recovered.

sentences.zh: 自是勒諸子多在澄寺中養之。

translations.literal: From this Le's various sons were mostly reared in Cheng's monastery.
translations.idiomatic: After that Shi Le boarded his sons in Fotucheng's cloister.

sentences.zh: 勒死之年，天靜無風，而塔上一鈴獨鳴，澄謂眾曰：「鈴音雲，國有大喪，不出今年矣。

translations.literal: In the year Le died, heaven was still without wind, yet one bell on the pagoda alone rang; Cheng told the crowd, "The bell's sound says the state has a great mourning—not beyond this year."
translations.idiomatic: The year Shi Le would die, a windless day rang a single stupa bell; Fotucheng told the assembly the realm would mourn before year's end.

sentences.zh: 」既而勒果死。

translations.literal: Before long Le indeed died.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Le died on cue.

sentences.zh: 及季龍僭位，遷都於鄴，傾心事澄，有重於勒。

translations.literal: When Jilong arrogated the throne, he moved the capital to Ye; he poured his heart into Cheng, weightier than with Le.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Hu moved the court to Ye and honored Fotucheng more than Shi Le had.

sentences.zh: 下書衣澄以綾錦，乘以雕輦，朝會之日，引之升殿，常侍以下悉助舉輿，太子諸公扶翼而上，主者唱大和尚，眾坐皆起，以彰其尊。

translations.literal: He issued edicts to clothe Cheng in damask and brocade, to mount him on a carved palanquin; on court audience days he led him up the hall—regular attendants and below all helped lift the carriage, while the heir and princes supported him on the sides; the master of ceremonies announced Great Monk, and all seated rose—to display his honor.
translations.idiomatic: He draped the monk in silk, gave him a carved litter, and made the whole court hoist him to the throne dais while criers hailed Great Monk and every seat rose.

sentences.zh: 又使司空李農旦夕親問，其太子諸公五日一朝，尊敬莫與為比。

translations.literal: Again he had Minister of Works Li Nong morning and evening inquire in person; his heir and princes attended audience every five days—none matched that reverence.
translations.idiomatic: Minister Li Nong tended him daily; princes waited on him every five days—unmatched homage.

sentences.zh: 支道林在京師，聞澄與諸石遊，乃曰：「澄公其以季龍為海鷗鳥也。

translations.literal: Zhi Daolin in the capital, hearing that Cheng associated with the various Shi, then said, "Lord Cheng surely takes Jilong for a sea gull bird."
translations.idiomatic: Zhi Dun in the capital sneered that Fotucheng treated Shi Hu like the tame gulls of the parable—unafraid of the butcher's heart.

sentences.zh: 百姓因澄故多奉佛，皆營造寺廟，相競出家，真偽混淆，多生愆過。

translations.literal: Because of Cheng the commoners for the most part took up Buddhism, all building temples and competing to leave home—true and false mixed, and very many faults arose.
translations.idiomatic: Masses aped the monk, built shrines, and tonsured until true faith mingled with fraud and scandal multiplied.

sentences.zh: 季龍下書料簡，其著作郎王度奏曰：「佛，外國之神，非諸華所應祠奉。

translations.literal: Jilong issued an edict to examine them; his editorial director Wang Du memorialized, saying, "Buddha is a god of foreign lands—not what the various Hua ought to worship and serve."
translations.idiomatic: Shi Hu ordered a purge; Wang Du argued Buddha was a foreign god unfit for Chinese worship.

sentences.zh: 漢代初傳其道，惟聽西域人得立寺都邑，以奉其神，漢人皆不出家。

translations.literal: In Han when the Way first spread, only Western Region persons were allowed to erect temples in the capital to serve their god; Han people all did not leave home.
translations.idiomatic: Han law had let only westerners build urban temples while native Chinese stayed lay.

sentences.zh: 魏承漢制，亦循前軌。

translations.literal: Wei inherited Han's system and likewise followed the former track.
translations.idiomatic: Wei continued the same rule.

sentences.zh: 今可斷趙人悉不聽詣寺燒香禮拜，以遵典禮，其百辟卿士下逮眾隸，例皆禁之，其有犯者，與淫祀同罪。

translations.literal: Now we may cut off Zhao people entirely from hearing them go to temples to burn incense and bow in worship, to follow canonical ritual—from the hundred ministers and grandees down to the mass of bondservants, by rule all forbid it; those who violate it share the crime of licentious sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Du urged banning all Zhao subjects from temples on pain of illicit-cult statutes, high to low.

sentences.zh: 其趙人為沙門者，還服百姓。

translations.literal: Those among Zhao people who became shramanas should return to commoner dress.
translations.idiomatic: Chinese monks must laicize.

sentences.zh: 」朝士多同度所奏。

translations.literal: Court gentlemen mostly agreed with what Du memorialized.
translations.idiomatic: Most courtiers backed Wang Du.

sentences.zh: 季龍以澄故，下書曰：「朕出自邊戎，忝君諸夏，至於饗祀，應從本俗。

translations.literal: Jilong because of Cheng issued an edict saying, "I come from the border Rong; I disgrace myself as lord of the various Xia—as to offerings and sacrifice, I ought to follow my native customs."
translations.idiomatic: Shi Hu cited Fotucheng and proclaimed his barbarian origin: rites should follow tribal ways.

sentences.zh: 佛是戎神，所應兼奉，其夷趙百姓有樂事佛者，特聽之。」

translations.literal: Buddha is a Rong god; one ought jointly to serve him; among barbarian and Zhao commoners those who delight in serving Buddha are specially permitted.
translations.idiomatic: He declared Buddha a tribal deity whom Zhao might freely worship.

sentences.zh: 澄時止鄴城寺中，弟子遍于郡國。

translations.literal: Cheng at the time stopped in Ye city's monastery; his disciples spread through commanderies and states.
translations.idiomatic: Fotucheng lived at Ye's great cloister with disciples in every province.

sentences.zh: 嘗遣弟子法常北至襄國，弟子法佐從襄國還，相遇于梁基城下，對車夜談，言及和尚，比旦各去。

translations.literal: Once he sent disciple Fachang north to Xiangguo; disciple Fazuo returned from Xiangguo; they met beneath Liangji city, spoke through the night in facing carts of their master, and at dawn each departed.
translations.idiomatic: Disciples Fachang and Fazuo met at Liangji, talked in their carts till dawn about their teacher, then parted.

sentences.zh: 佐始入，澄逆笑曰：「昨夜爾與法常交車共說汝師邪？

translations.literal: When Zuo had just entered, Cheng preemptively laughed and said, "Last night you and Fachang crossed carts together speaking of your teacher, did you not?"
translations.idiomatic: Fotucheng greeted Fazuo with a laugh about his midnight cart talk with Fachang.

sentences.zh: 」佐愕然愧懺。

translations.literal: Zuo was startled and ashamed.
translations.idiomatic: Fazuo flushed with shame.

sentences.zh: 於是國人每相語：「莫起噁心，和尚知汝。

translations.literal: Thereupon people of the state each told one another, "Do not raise an evil mind—the monk knows you."
translations.idiomatic: Folk warned one another: the monk read every wicked thought.

sentences.zh: 」及澄之所在，無敢向其方面涕唾者。

translations.literal: Wherever Cheng was, none dared toward his direction spit or weep.
translations.idiomatic: None spat toward Fotucheng's quarter.

sentences.zh: 季龍太子邃有二字，在襄國，澄語邃曰：「小阿彌比當得疾，可往看之。

translations.literal: Jilong's heir Shi Sui had two sons in Xiangguo; Cheng told Sui, "Little Amita will presently fall ill—you may go look at him."
translations.idiomatic: Fotucheng told crown prince Shi Sui that his son Little Maitreya would sicken.

sentences.zh: 」邃即馳信往視，果已得疾。

translations.literal: Sui immediately sent a fast messenger to look, and indeed he had already fallen ill.
translations.idiomatic: Sui's courier found the boy already ill.

sentences.zh: 太醫殷騰及外國道士自言能療之。

translations.literal: Grand Physician Yin Teng and foreign Daoists claimed they could cure it.
translations.idiomatic: Court physician Yin Teng and foreign priests boasted a cure.

sentences.zh: 澄告弟子法牙曰：「正使聖人復出，不愈此疾，況此等乎！

translations.literal: Cheng told his disciple Faya, "Even if sages returned, they could not cure this illness—how much less these!"
translations.idiomatic: Fotucheng told Faya that neither sages nor charlatans could save the child.

sentences.zh: 」後三日果死。

translations.literal: After three days he indeed died.
translations.idiomatic: The boy died in three days.

sentences.zh: 邃將圖為逆，謂內豎曰：「和尚神通，儻發吾謀。

translations.literal: Sui was about to plot rebellion; he told the inner attendants, "The monk's spirit penetration—if he divulges my plan."
translations.idiomatic: Shi Sui schemed regicide and feared the monk would expose him.

sentences.zh: 明日來者，當先除之。

translations.literal: Whoever comes tomorrow, we ought first to eliminate him.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered tomorrow's visitors killed first.

sentences.zh: 」澄月望將入覲季龍，謂弟子僧慧曰：「昨夜天神呼我曰：'明日若入，還勿過人。

translations.literal: Cheng on the fifteenth of the month was about to enter audience with Jilong; he told his disciple Seng Hui, "Last night a spirit called me saying: 'If you enter tomorrow, on the return do not pass others.'"
translations.idiomatic: On the fifteenth Fotucheng told Seng Hui a god had warned him not to visit others after court.

sentences.zh: 」我儻有所過，汝當止我。

translations.literal: If I perhaps pass someone, you ought to stop me.
translations.idiomatic: If he detoured to anyone, Hui must stop him.

sentences.zh: 」澄常入，必過邃。

translations.literal: Cheng on entering always passed Sui.
translations.idiomatic: Fotucheng always called on Shi Sui after audience.

sentences.zh: 邃知澄入，要侯甚苦。

translations.literal: Sui knew Cheng would enter and waited bitterly hard.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Sui lay in wait.

sentences.zh: 澄將上南台，僧慧引衣，澄曰：「事不得止。

translations.literal: Cheng was about to ascend the south terrace; Seng Hui pulled his robe; Cheng said, "The affair cannot be stopped."
translations.idiomatic: Seng Hui tugged his sleeve on the south terrace stair; Fotucheng said the meeting could not be avoided.

sentences.zh: 」坐未安便起，邃固留不住，所謀遂差。

translations.literal: He had not sat in peace when he rose; Sui firmly could not detain him—what was plotted then missed.
translations.idiomatic: He rose before sitting long; Shi Sui could not hold him and the plot misfired.

sentences.zh: 還寺，歎曰：「太子作亂，其形將成，欲言難言，欲忍難忍。

translations.literal: Returning to the monastery, he sighed, "The heir is about to rebel; its form is about to complete—I wish to speak yet it is hard to speak; I wish to endure yet it is hard to endure."
translations.idiomatic: Back at the cloister he groaned that the heir's revolt was ripening yet speech was impossible.

sentences.zh: 」乃因事從容箴季龍，季龍終不能解。

translations.literal: Thereupon on an occasion he leisurely admonished Jilong; Jilong in the end could not understand.
translations.idiomatic: He hinted to Shi Hu, who grasped nothing.

sentences.zh: 俄而事發，方悟澄言。

translations.literal: Before long the affair broke out, and only then did he understand Cheng's words.
translations.idiomatic: When the coup erupted, Shi Hu recalled the warning.

sentences.zh: 後郭黑略將兵征長安北山羌，墮羌伏中。

translations.literal: Later Guo Heilie led troops to campaign against the Qiang of Chang'an's northern mountains and fell into Qiang ambush.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Heilie marched against northern Qiang and walked into an ambush.

sentences.zh: 時澄在堂上坐，慘然改容曰：「郭公今有厄。

translations.literal: At the time Cheng was sitting in the hall, changed color mournfully and said, "Lord Guo now has a calamity."
translations.idiomatic: Seated in the Dharma hall Fotucheng blanched: Guo Heilie faced doom.

sentences.zh: 」乃唱云：「眾僧祝願。

translations.literal: Thereupon he intoned, "All monks pray blessing."
translations.idiomatic: He called the sangha to chant blessings.

sentences.zh: 」澄又自祝願。

translations.literal: Cheng again personally prayed blessing.
translations.idiomatic: He added his own prayer.

sentences.zh: 須臾，更曰：若東南出者活，余向者則困。

translations.literal: After a moment he again said, "If they go out to the southeast they live; those who go toward the remainder are trapped."
translations.idiomatic: Moments later he said flight southeast meant life; other routes meant death.

sentences.zh: 」復更祝願。

translations.literal: Again he changed the prayer.
translations.idiomatic: He chanted again.

sentences.zh: 有頃，曰：「脫矣。

translations.literal: After a moment he said, "Escaped."
translations.idiomatic: Then he said, "He has broken free."

sentences.zh: 」後月餘，黑略還，自說墜羌圍中，東南走，馬乏，正遇帳下人，推馬與之曰：「公乘此馬，小人乘公馬，濟與不濟，命也。

translations.literal: After more than a month Heilie returned, saying of himself that he had fallen into Qiang's surround, fled southeast, his horses were exhausted, just then met a man of his tent staff who pushed a horse to him and said, "Your lordship ride this horse; your servant rides your lordship's horse—whether we ford or not is fate."
translations.idiomatic: A month later Guo Heilie returned, telling how he broke out southeast, swapped mounts with an orderly, and escaped by fate.

sentences.zh: 」略得其馬，故獲免。

translations.literal: Heilie obtained that horse and therefore was spared.
translations.idiomatic: That spare horse saved him.

sentences.zh: 推檢時日，正是澄祝願時也。

translations.literal: Checking the times and days, it was exactly when Cheng prayed blessing.
translations.idiomatic: The timestamps matched Fotucheng's chant.

sentences.zh: 時天旱，季龍遣其太子詣臨漳西滏口祈雨，久而不降，乃令澄自行，即有白龍二頭降於祠所，其日大雨方數千里。

translations.literal: At the time heaven was drought; Jilong sent his heir to Fuyin's west at the river mouth to pray for rain; long it did not descend; he then ordered Cheng himself to go, and immediately there were two white dragons that descended at the shrine place; that day great rain fell over several thousand square li.
translations.idiomatic: During drought Shi Hu's heir prayed at Fuyin in vain until Fotucheng went; twin white dragons descended and rain soaked a thousand li.

sentences.zh: 澄嘗遣弟子向西域市香，既行，澄告余弟子曰：「掌中見買香弟子在某處被劫垂死。

translations.literal: Cheng once sent disciples west to the Western Regions to buy incense; after they had gone, Cheng told the remaining disciples, "In my palm I see the incense-buying disciples at such-and-such a place being robbed and on the point of death."
translations.idiomatic: He sent men west for incense, then told others he saw them ambushed and dying.

sentences.zh: 」因燒香祝願，遙救護之。

translations.literal: Thereupon he burned incense, prayed blessing, and from afar protected and saved them.
translations.idiomatic: He burned incense and rescued them at a distance.

sentences.zh: 弟子後還，雲某月某日某處為賊所劫，垂當見殺，忽聞香氣，賊無故自驚曰：「救兵已至。

translations.literal: The disciples later returned, saying on such-and-such a month and day at such-and-such a place they were robbed by bandits and were about to be killed, when suddenly they smelled incense; the bandits without cause startled themselves and said, "Relief troops have already arrived."
translations.idiomatic: They returned reporting how bandits were about to kill them when incense filled the air and robbers fled shouting that relief had come.

sentences.zh: 」棄之而走。

translations.literal: They abandoned them and ran.
translations.idiomatic: The brigands dropped them and bolted.

sentences.zh: 黃河中舊不生黿，時有得者，以獻季龍。

translations.literal: In the Yellow River formerly softshell turtles did not grow; at the time when one was obtained, it was presented to Jilong.
translations.idiomatic: Yellow River turtles were rare; someone presented one to Shi Hu.

sentences.zh: 澄見而之曰：「桓溫入河，其不久乎！

translations.literal: Cheng saw it and said to him, "Huan Wen enters the river—will it not be before long!"
translations.idiomatic: Fotucheng said the turtle meant Huan Wen would soon cross the Yellow River.

sentences.zh: 」溫字元子，後果如其言也。

translations.literal: Wen's courtesy name was Yuanzi; afterward it indeed happened as he said.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Wen's courtesy name was Yuanzi; the prophecy came true.

sentences.zh: 季龍嘗晝寢，夢見群羊負魚從東北來，寤以訪澄。

translations.literal: Jilong once napped by day and dreamed a flock of sheep bearing fish came from the northeast; awake he consulted Cheng.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Hu dreamed sheep carrying fish from the northeast and asked Fotucheng.

sentences.zh: 澄曰：「不祥也，鮮卑其有中原乎！

translations.literal: Cheng said, "It is inauspicious; the Xianbei are about to have the Central Plain!"
translations.idiomatic: Fotucheng read it as Xianbei seizing the heartland.

sentences.zh: 」後亦皆驗。

translations.literal: Later all also verified.
translations.idiomatic: Later events proved him right.

sentences.zh: 澄嘗與季龍升中台，澄忽驚曰：「變，變，幽州當火災。

translations.literal: Cheng once ascended the middle terrace with Jilong; Cheng suddenly startled and said, "Change, change—Youzhou is about to have a fire disaster."
translations.idiomatic: On the middle terrace he cried that Youzhou would burn.

sentences.zh: 」乃取酒噀之，久而笑曰：「救已得矣。

translations.literal: Thereupon he took wine and sprayed it; after a long while he laughed and said, "The rescue has already been obtained."
translations.idiomatic: He sprayed wine and laughed that the fire was quenched.

sentences.zh: 」季龍遣驗幽州，雲爾日火從四門起，西南有黑雲來，驟雨滅之，雨亦頗有酒氣。

translations.literal: Jilong sent men to verify Youzhou; they said that day fire rose from the four gates, black clouds came from the southwest, sudden rain extinguished it, and the rain also had quite a smell of wine.
translations.idiomatic: Inspectors reported four-gate fires doused by a southwest black cloud and a rain that smelled of wine.

sentences.zh: 石宣將殺石韜，宣先到寺與澄同坐，浮屠一鈴獨鳴，澄謂曰：「解鈴音乎？

translations.literal: Shi Xuan was about to kill Shi Tao; Xuan first arrived at the monastery and sat with Cheng; one pagoda bell alone rang; Cheng said to him, "Do you understand the bell's sound?"
translations.idiomatic: Before murdering Shi Tao, Shi Xuan sat with Fotucheng while one bell tolled; the monk asked if he grasped its message.

sentences.zh: 鈴雲鬍子洛度。

translations.literal: The bell says 'beard rah-rodo.'
translations.idiomatic: The bell tolled a Jie phrase foretelling blood.

sentences.zh: 」宣變色曰：「是何言歟？

translations.literal: Xuan changed color and said, "What sort of talk is this!"
