translations.idiomatic: Shi Xuan snarled at the riddle.

sentences.zh: 」澄謬曰：「老胡為道，不能山居無言，重茵美服，豈非洛度乎！

translations.literal: Cheng pretended, saying, "Old Hu for the Way cannot dwell in the mountains without speech; layered mats and fine clothes—are they not rah-rodo!"
translations.idiomatic: Fotucheng feigned senile chatter about silks and cushions.

sentences.zh: 」石韜後至，澄孰視良久。

translations.literal: When Shi Tao afterward arrived, Cheng stared long.
translations.idiomatic: When Shi Tao entered, Fotucheng stared.

sentences.zh: 韜懼而問澄，澄曰：「怪公血臭，故相視耳。

translations.literal: Tao was afraid and questioned Cheng; Cheng said, "I marveled that your lordship's blood stank; therefore I looked."
translations.idiomatic: Shi Tao flinched; Fotucheng said he smelled blood.

sentences.zh: 」季龍夢龍飛西南，自天而落，旦而問澄，澄曰：「禍將作矣，宜父子慈和，深以慎之。

translations.literal: Jilong dreamed a dragon flew southwest, falling from heaven; at dawn he asked Cheng; Cheng said, "Disaster is about to happen; you ought to be father and sons kindly harmonious and deeply be careful of it."
translations.idiomatic: Shi Hu dreamed a dragon fall from the sky; Fotucheng urged father-son harmony before disaster.

sentences.zh: 」季龍引澄入東閣，與其後杜氏問訊之。

translations.literal: Jilong led Cheng into the eastern chamber and with his empress Du questioned him.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Hu brought him to Empress Du in the east closet.

sentences.zh: 澄曰：「脅下有賊，不出十日，自浮圖以西，此殿以東，當有血流，慎勿東也。

translations.literal: Cheng said, "Beneath the ribs there is a thief; within ten days, west of this pagoda and east of this hall, there ought to be flowing blood—be careful not to go east."
translations.idiomatic: He warned of a killer under the ribs, blood west of the stupa and east of the hall, and forbade eastward movement.

sentences.zh: 」杜後曰：「和尚耄邪！

translations.literal: Empress Du said, "Monk, are you senile!"
translations.idiomatic: Empress Du called him a dotard.

sentences.zh: 何處有賊？

translations.literal: Where is there a thief?
translations.idiomatic: Where was any assassin?

sentences.zh: 」澄即易語云：「六情所受，皆悉是賊。

translations.literal: Cheng immediately shifted language, saying, "What the six emotions receive—all are thieves."
translations.idiomatic: Fotucheng retreated to metaphor: every passion is a thief.

sentences.zh: 老自應耄，但使少者不昏即好耳。

translations.literal: I myself ought to be senile, but if it makes the young not reckless that is well.
translations.idiomatic: He claimed old folly—if the young stayed sober, well enough.

sentences.zh: 」遂便寓言，不復彰的。

translations.literal: Thereupon he spoke in allegory and no longer made it explicit.
translations.idiomatic: He spoke in parables and dropped plain speech.

sentences.zh: 後二日，宣果遣人害韜於佛寺中，欲因季龍臨喪殺之。

translations.literal: After two days Xuan indeed sent men to harm Tao inside a Buddha temple, wishing to take advantage of Jilong's coming to mourning to kill him.
translations.idiomatic: Two days later Shi Xuan had Shi Tao murdered in a temple, planning to kill Shi Hu at the funeral.

sentences.zh: 季龍以澄先誡，故獲免。

translations.literal: Jilong because Cheng had forewarned therefore was spared.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Hu survived thanks to Fotucheng's warning.

sentences.zh: 及宣被收，澄諫季龍曰：「皆陛下之子也，何為重禍邪！

translations.literal: When Xuan was seized, Cheng remonstrated Jilong, saying, "They are all Your Majesty's sons—why double the calamity!"
translations.idiomatic: When Shi Xuan was arrested, Fotucheng begged Shi Hu not to multiply the blood curse—all were his sons.

sentences.zh: 陛下若含怒加慈者，尚有六十餘歲。

translations.literal: If Your Majesty will contain wrath and add kindness, you still have more than sixty years.
translations.idiomatic: Mercy would buy Shi Hu sixty more years of life.

sentences.zh: 如必誅之，宣當為彗星下掃鄴宮。

translations.literal: If you are sure to execute him, Xuan will become a broom comet sweeping down on the Ye palace.
translations.idiomatic: Execute him and a comet would scour the Ye palace—meaning ruin.

sentences.zh: 」季龍不從。

translations.literal: Jilong did not follow this.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Hu refused the plea.

sentences.zh: 後月餘，有一妖馬，髦尾皆有燒狀，入中陽門，出顯陽門，東首東宮，皆不得入，走向東北，俄爾不見。

translations.literal: After more than a month there was one demon horse whose mane and tail both had burnt marks; it entered Zhongyang Gate, went out Xianyang Gate, tried east to the Eastern Palace but could not enter, ran toward the northeast, and before long disappeared.
translations.idiomatic: A month later a spectral horse with scorched mane and tail galloped through the gates, failed to enter the heir's east palace, fled northeast, and vanished.

sentences.zh: 澄聞而歎曰：「災其及矣！

translations.literal: When Cheng heard he sighed and said, "The calamity will reach us!"
translations.idiomatic: Hearing the omen, Fotucheng sighed that disaster was closing in.

sentences.zh: 」季龍大享群臣于太武前殿，澄吟曰：「殿乎，殿乎！

translations.literal: Jilong greatly feasted his ministers at the Taiwu front hall; Cheng chanted, "Hall, oh hall!"
translations.idiomatic: At a great feast in Taiwu hall Fotucheng chanted a riddle about the hall.

sentences.zh: 棘子成林，將壞人衣。

translations.literal: Thorns will grow into a forest; they will tear men's clothes.
translations.idiomatic: Thorn scrub would sprout to shred men's robes—he foretold Ran Min.

sentences.zh: 」季龍令發殿石下視之，有棘生焉。

translations.literal: Jilong ordered them to dig beneath the hall stones and look; there were thorns growing.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Hu had workers lift the foundation stones and found brambles sprouting below.

sentences.zh: 冉閔小字棘奴。

translations.literal: Ran Min's childhood name was Thorn Slave.
translations.idiomatic: Ran Min's pet name had been Thorn-slave.

sentences.zh: 季龍造太武殿初成，圖畫自古賢聖、忠臣、孝子、烈士、貞女，皆變為胡狀，旬餘，頭悉縮入肩中，惟冠䯰仿佛微出，季龍大惡之，秘而不言也。

translations.literal: When Jilong built the Taiwu hall and it was first completed, the paintings of ancient worthies, sages, loyal ministers, filial sons, martyrs, and chaste women all changed into Hu appearance; after more than ten days their heads all shrank into their shoulders; only caps and hairpins faintly protruded; Jilong greatly hated it and kept it secret without speaking.
translations.idiomatic: New Taiwu hall murals of Chinese paragons morphed into barbarian faces, heads sinking into shoulders—Shi Hu hid the horror.

sentences.zh: 澄對之流涕，乃自啟塋墓於鄴西紫陌，還寺，獨語曰：「得三年乎？

translations.literal: Cheng wept facing it, then personally opened a tomb mound west of Ye on Purple Lane; returning to the monastery he spoke alone, saying, "Can I obtain three years?"
translations.idiomatic: Fotucheng wept, opened his own grave west of Ye, and muttered whether he had three years left.

sentences.zh: 」自答：「不得。

translations.literal: He himself answered, "Cannot."
translations.idiomatic: He answered himself: no.

sentences.zh: 」又曰：「得二年、一年、百日、一月乎？

translations.literal: Again he said, "Can I obtain two years, one year, one hundred days, one month?"
translations.idiomatic: He asked again for two years, one year, hundred days, a month.

sentences.zh: 」自答：「不得。

translations.literal: He himself answered, "Cannot."
translations.idiomatic: Again: no.

sentences.zh: 」遂無復言。

translations.literal: Thereupon he had no more words.
translations.idiomatic: Then he fell silent.

sentences.zh: 謂弟子法祚曰：「戊申歲禍亂漸萌，己酉石氏當滅。

translations.literal: He told his disciple Fazuo, "In the wushen year misfortune and chaos gradually sprout; in jiyou the Shi clan will be destroyed."
translations.idiomatic: He told Fazuo that wu-shen would see chaos and ji-you the end of the house of Shi.

sentences.zh: 吾及其未亂，先從化矣。

translations.literal: I will precede transformation before they yet are in chaos.
translations.idiomatic: He would depart before the storm.

sentences.zh: 」卒于鄴宮寺。

translations.literal: He died in Ye's palace monastery.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the palace monastery at Ye.

sentences.zh: 後有沙門從雍州來，稱見澄西入關，季龍掘而視之，惟有一石無屍。

translations.literal: Later there was a shramana who came from Yong Province saying he saw Cheng enter the passes westward; Jilong dug and looked, and there was only one stone, no corpse.
translations.idiomatic: A monk from Yongzhou claimed Fotucheng went west; Shi Hu opened the tomb and found only a stone.

sentences.zh: 季龍惡之曰：「石者，朕也，葬我而去，吾將死矣。

translations.literal: Jilong hated it and said, "Stone is I; burying me and leaving— I am about to die."
translations.idiomatic: Shi Hu read stone as himself and knew his death neared.

sentences.zh: 」因而遇疾。

translations.literal: From this he encountered illness.
translations.idiomatic: He fell ill.

sentences.zh: 明年，季龍死，遂大亂。

translations.literal: The next year Jilong died, and thereupon great chaos.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Hu died the next year and the realm collapsed.

sentences.zh: 麻襦

translations.literal: Ma Ru.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Ru.

sentences.zh: 麻襦者，不知何許人也，莫得其姓名。

translations.literal: Ma Ru—none knew what place he was from; none could obtain his name.
translations.idiomatic: No one knew Ma Ru's origin or true name.

sentences.zh: 石季龍時，在魏縣市中乞丐，恆著麻襦布裳，故時人謂之麻襦。

translations.literal: At the time of Shi Jilong he begged in Weixian market, always wearing hemp trousers and cloth skirt; therefore people of the time called him Ma Ru.
translations.idiomatic: Under Shi Hu he begged in Weixian in hemp breeches—hence the name Hemp-cloth.

sentences.zh: 言語卓越，狀如狂者，乞得米穀不食，輒散置大路，雲飴天馬。

translations.literal: His speech was transcendent; his bearing like a madman's; the rice and grain he begged he did not eat but always scattered them on the great road, saying he fed Heaven's horses.
translations.idiomatic: He raved like a madman, scattered alms rice on the road, calling it fodder for heaven's horses.

sentences.zh: 趙興太守籍狀收送詣季龍。

translations.literal: The governor of Zhao Xing, Ji Zhuang, seized him on register and sent him to Jilong.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Xing governor Ji Zhuang arrested and sent him to Shi Hu.

sentences.zh: 先是，佛圖澄謂季龍曰：「國東二百里某月日當送一非常人，勿殺之也。

translations.literal: Before this Fotucheng had told Jilong, "East of the state two hundred li on such-and-such a month and day they will deliver one extraordinary man—do not kill him."
translations.idiomatic: Fotucheng had warned Shi Hu not to kill a strange man coming from the east.

sentences.zh: 」如期果至。

translations.literal: At the appointed time he indeed arrived.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Ru arrived on schedule.

sentences.zh: 季龍與共語，了無異言，惟道：「陛下當終一柱殿下。

translations.literal: Jilong spoke with him; there was completely no strange speech—he only said, "Your Majesty will end beneath one pillar's hall."
translations.idiomatic: Shi Hu found him taciturn except for the line about dying under a single-pillar hall.

sentences.zh: 」季龍不解，送以詣澄。

translations.literal: Jilong did not understand and sent him to Cheng.
translations.idiomatic: Puzzled, Shi Hu sent him to Fotucheng.

sentences.zh: 麻襦謂澄曰：「昔在光和中會，奄至今日。

translations.literal: Ma Ru said to Cheng, "Formerly at the Guanghe middle meeting, suddenly we have reached today."
translations.idiomatic: Ma Ru told Fotucheng they had met since the Guanghe conclave ages ago.

sentences.zh: 酉戎受玄命，絕曆終有期。

translations.literal: You Rong received the dark mandate; severed reckoning ends with a term.
translations.idiomatic: The western tribes took the mystic mandate; the broken calendar ends on schedule.

sentences.zh: 金離消于壞，邊荒不能遵，驅除靈期跡，莫已已之懿。

translations.literal: Metal departs in ruin; the border wastes cannot be followed; driving off the spirit term's traces—there is no end to such excellence.
translations.idiomatic: Metal fate melts in collapse; the frontiers cannot hold; spirit tracks must be swept away—endless virtue.

sentences.zh: 裔苗葉繁，其來方積。

translations.literal: Offspring shoots, leaves luxuriant—the coming is just accumulating.
translations.idiomatic: Sprouts and leaves multiply—the reckoning piles up.

sentences.zh: 休期於何期，永以歎之。

translations.literal: When is the rest term—forever I sigh for it.
translations.idiomatic: When will the pause come—only endless sighs.

sentences.zh: 」澄曰：「天回運極，否將不支，九木水為難，無可以術寧。

translations.literal: Cheng said, "Heaven's cycle reaches the limit; decline will not hold up; nine trees and water make difficulty—nothing by art can bring peace."
translations.idiomatic: Fotucheng answered in matching verse: the cosmic wheel nears its stop; decline cannot be propped; wood and water spell peril—no rite can calm it.

sentences.zh: 玄哲雖存世，莫能基必莫能基必頹。

translations.literal: Dark wisdom though it dwells in the world cannot found the base, surely cannot found the base—ruin.
translations.idiomatic: Even hidden sages cannot shore the foundation—it must fall.

sentences.zh: 久游閻浮利，擾擾多此患。

translations.literal: Long roaming Jambudvipa—tumult has much of this suffering.
translations.idiomatic: Long wandering this world brings such vexation.

sentences.zh: 行登陵雲宇，會于虛遊間。

translations.literal: Walking I will ascend the cloud tower; meet in empty roaming between.
translations.idiomatic: Soon we mount the cloud terraces and meet in the void.

sentences.zh: 」其所言人莫能曉。

translations.literal: What he spoke none of the people could understand.
translations.idiomatic: None understood their exchange.

sentences.zh: 季龍遣驛馬送還本縣，既出城，請步，云：「我當有所過，君至合口橋見待。

translations.literal: Jilong sent post horses to escort him back to his native county; after leaving the city he requested to walk, saying, "I must have a stop; you wait for me at Hegkou Bridge."
translations.idiomatic: Shi Hu sent him home by post; outside the walls he insisted on walking and told the escort to wait at Hegkou bridge.

sentences.zh: 」使人如言而馳，至橋，麻襦已先至。

translations.literal: The messenger galloped as he said; when he reached the bridge, Ma Ru was already there first.
translations.idiomatic: The rider galloped ahead yet Ma Ru was waiting on the bridge.

sentences.zh: 後慕容俊投季龍屍于漳水，倚橋柱不流，時人以為「一柱殿下」即謂此也。

translations.literal: Later Murong Jun threw Jilong's corpse into the Zhang River; it leaned against a bridge pillar and would not float; people of the time thought 'beneath one pillar's hall' meant this.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Jun cast Shi Hu's corpse in the Zhang where it lodged against a pier—folk said that fulfilled the one-pillar hall prophecy.

sentences.zh: 及元帝嗣位江左，亦以為「天馬」之應云。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yuan succeeded on the Jiangzuo, they also took it as a response of 'Heaven's horses.'
translations.idiomatic: Eastern Jin courtiers also linked the tale to the heaven-horse omen.

sentences.zh: 單道開

translations.literal: Shan Daokai.
translations.idiomatic: Shan Daokai.

sentences.zh: 單道開，敦煌人也。

translations.literal: Shan Daokai was a native of Dunhuang.
translations.idiomatic: Shan Daokai came from Dunhuang.

sentences.zh: 常衣粗褐，或贈以繒服，皆不著，不畏寒暑，晝夜不臥。

translations.literal: He constantly wore coarse hemp; if someone gifted him silk clothes he did not put them on; he did not fear cold or heat; day and night he did not lie down.
translations.idiomatic: He shunned silk gifts, braved heat and cold, and never slept.

sentences.zh: 恆服細石子，一吞數枚，日一服，或多或少。

translations.literal: He constantly swallowed fine pebbles, several pieces at one swallow, one dose a day, sometimes more sometimes less.
translations.idiomatic: He daily swallowed a handful of fine pebbles.

sentences.zh: 好山居，而山樹諸神見異形試之，初無懼色。

translations.literal: He loved dwelling in mountains; yet mountain tree gods showed strange forms to test him; at first he had no frightened look.
translations.idiomatic: Mountain spirits tested him with visions; he never flinched.

sentences.zh: 石季龍時，從西平來，一日行七百里，其一沙彌年十四，行亦及之。

translations.literal: At the time of Shi Jilong he came from Xiping, traveling seven hundred li in one day; one of his novices, fourteen years old, in walking also kept up.
translations.idiomatic: He walked seven hundred li from Xiping in a day with a fourteen-year-old novice at his heels.

sentences.zh: 至秦州，表送到鄴，季龍令佛圖澄與語，不能屈也。

translations.literal: Reaching Qin Province, he was memorialized and sent to Ye; Jilong ordered Fotucheng to speak with him and could not humble him.
translations.idiomatic: Qinzhou forwarded him to Ye where Fotucheng could not best him in debate.

sentences.zh: 初止鄴城西沙門法綝祠中，後徙臨漳昭德寺。

translations.literal: At first he stopped in the western city of Ye in the shramana Fachin's shrine; later he moved to Linzhang's Zhaode Monastery.
translations.idiomatic: He first lodged at monk Fachin's west-city shrine, then moved to Zhaode Monastery in Linzhang.

sentences.zh: 于房內造重閣，高八九尺，于上編管為禪室，常坐其中。

translations.literal: Inside his room he built a double loft eight or nine chi high; on top he wove rushes for a meditation chamber and constantly sat within it.
translations.idiomatic: He wove a meditation loft eight or nine chi high in his cell.

sentences.zh: 季龍資給甚厚，道開皆以施人。

translations.literal: Jilong supplied him very generously; Daokai all gave it to others.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Hu showered gifts; Shan Daokai gave them all away.

sentences.zh: 人或來諮問者，道開都不答。

translations.literal: If people came to consult and question him, Daokai entirely did not answer.
translations.idiomatic: He answered no questions.

sentences.zh: 日服鎮守藥數丸，大如梧子，藥有松蜜姜桂伏苓之氣，時復飲荼蘇一二升而已。

translations.literal: Daily he swallowed several pellets of tranquilizing medicine as large as wu-tong seeds; the medicine had the qi of pine honey, ginger, cinnamon, and poria; from time to time he again drank one or two sheng of tea broth only.
translations.idiomatic: He lived on walnut-sized pills scented with pine honey, ginger, cinnamon, and poria, plus an occasional liter or two of herb tea.

sentences.zh: 自雲能療目疾，就療者頗驗。

translations.literal: He said of himself that he could cure eye diseases; those who sought treatment were largely verified.
translations.idiomatic: He claimed to heal eyes and often succeeded.

sentences.zh: 視其行動，狀若有神。

translations.literal: Watching his movements, his bearing seemed as if he had spirit.
translations.idiomatic: His movements seemed superhuman.

sentences.zh: 佛圖澄曰：「此道士觀國興衰，若去者，當有大亂。

translations.literal: Fotucheng said, "This Daoist observes the state's rise and decline; if he leaves, there will be great chaos."
translations.idiomatic: Fotucheng said the hermit read the dynasty's fate and that his flight would mean chaos.

sentences.zh: 」及季龍末，道開南渡許昌，尋而鄴中大亂。

translations.literal: At the end of Jilong, Daokai crossed south to Xuchang; before long great chaos struck Ye.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Shi Hu's reign Shan Daokai fled south to Xuchang; Ye soon erupted.

sentences.zh: 至京師，後至南海，入羅浮山，獨處茅茨，蕭然物外。

translations.literal: He reached the capital, later reached Nanhai, entered Mount Luofu, dwelt alone in a thatched hut, detached beyond things.
translations.idiomatic: He passed through the capital to Nanhai and lived alone in a Luofu hut.

sentences.zh: 年百餘歲，卒於山舍，敕弟子以屍置石穴中，弟子乃移入石室。

translations.literal: At more than a hundred years of age he died in a mountain hut; he ordered disciples to place the corpse in a stone grotto; disciples then moved it into a stone chamber.
translations.idiomatic: He died past a hundred in a mountain cell, ordering disciples to lay him in a stone cave—they moved him to a stone room.

sentences.zh: 陳郡袁宏為南海太守，與弟穎叔及沙門支法防共登羅浮山，至石室口，見道開形骸如生，香火瓦器猶存。

translations.literal: Yuan Hong of Chen commandery was governor of Nanhai; with his brother Yingshu and shramana Zhi Fafang together they ascended Mount Luofu; reaching the stone chamber mouth they saw Daokai's skeleton as if alive; incense ash and pottery vessels still remained.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Hong, his brother, and monk Zhi Fafang climbed Luofu and found Shan Daokai's body intact in the cave with incense pots still there.

sentences.zh: 宏曰：「法師業行殊群，正當如蟬蛻耳。

translations.literal: Hong said, "The dharma master's karma and conduct surpass the crowd—this is rightly like a cicada's sloughing."
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Hong said the master's merit outshone the world—his corpse was a cicada shell.

sentences.zh: 」乃為之贊雲。

translations.literal: Thereupon he composed a eulogy for him.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Hong wrote his elegy.

sentences.zh: 黃泓

translations.literal: Huang Hong.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Hong.

sentences.zh: 黃泓，字始長，魏郡斥丘人也。

translations.literal: Huang Hong, courtesy name Shizhang, was a native of Chiqiu in Wei commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Hong, courtesy name Shizhang, came from Chiqiu in Wei commandery.

sentences.zh: 父沈，善天文秘術。

translations.literal: His father Shen was good at astronomy and secret arts.
translations.idiomatic: His father Huang Shen mastered astronomy and occult arts.

sentences.zh: 泓從父受業，精妙逾深，兼博覽經史，尤明《禮》《易》。

translations.literal: Hong received his father's teaching; his subtlety exceeded deeper; he also broadly read the classics and histories, especially understanding the Rites and Changes.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Hong surpassed his father in star lore and knew the canon, especially Rites and Changes.

sentences.zh: 性忠勤，非禮不動。

translations.literal: His nature was loyal and diligent; he did not move contrary to ritual.
translations.idiomatic: He was dutiful and never acted against propriety.

sentences.zh: 永嘉之亂，與渤海高瞻避地幽州，說瞻曰：「王浚昏暴，終必無成，宜思去就以圖久安。

translations.literal: At the Yongjia turmoil he with Bohai's Gao Zhan took refuge in You Province; he persuaded Zhan, saying, "Wang Jun is benighted and violent; in the end he will surely accomplish nothing—you ought to think of leaving or staying to plan long peace."
translations.idiomatic: During Yongjia's chaos he fled to Youzhou with Gao Zhan and urged him to abandon the tyrant Wang Jun.

sentences.zh: 慕容廆法政修明，虛懷引納，且讖言真人出東北，儻或是乎？

translations.literal: Murong Hui's laws and government are cultivated and clear; he empties his bosom to draw men in; moreover prophetic words say the true man issues from the northeast—perhaps this is it?
translations.idiomatic: Murong Hui ruled justly and omens named a true king in the northeast—perhaps Murong was he?

sentences.zh: 宜相與歸之，同建事業。

translations.literal: We ought together to go to him and jointly establish enterprise.
translations.idiomatic: They should join Murong Hui and build a future together.

sentences.zh: 」瞻不從。

translations.literal: Zhan did not follow this.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Zhan refused.

sentences.zh: 泓乃率宗族歸廆，廆待以客禮，引為參軍，軍國之務動輒訪之。

translations.literal: Hong thereupon led his lineage kin to go to Hui; Hui treated him with guest ritual, drew him in as aide, and for army and state affairs always consulted him.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Hong led his clan to Murong Hui, who made him military adviser on every weighty matter.

sentences.zh: 泓指說成敗，事皆如言。

translations.literal: Hong pointed out and explained success and failure; affairs all matched his words.
translations.idiomatic: His forecasts of rise and fall proved true.

sentences.zh: 廆常曰：「黃參軍，孤之仲翔也。

translations.literal: Hui often said, "Aide Huang is my Zhongxiang."
translations.idiomatic: Murong Hui called him his Zhongxiang.

sentences.zh: 」及皝嗣位，遷左常侍，領史官，甚重之。

translations.literal: When Murong Huang succeeded the throne, he promoted Hong to left regular attendant, concurrently astrologer, and greatly esteemed him.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Huang raised Huang Hong to left attendant-in-ordinary and chief astrologer, deeply trusted.

sentences.zh: 石季龍攻皝，皝將走遼東，泓曰：「賊有敗氣，無可憂也，不過二日，必當奔潰。

translations.literal: When Shi Jilong attacked Murong Huang, Murong Huang was about to flee to Liaodong; Hong said, "The bandits have the qi of defeat—nothing to worry about; within two days they are sure to flee in rout."
translations.idiomatic: As Shi Hu struck Murong Huang, the king planned flight to Liaodong; Huang Hong read rout-qi within two days.

sentences.zh: 宜嚴勒士馬，為追擊之備。

translations.literal: You ought strictly to ready knights and horses and make preparations to pursue and strike.
translations.idiomatic: He urged Murong Huang to ready a pursuit.

sentences.zh: 」皝曰：「今寇盛如此，卿言必走，孤未敢信。

translations.literal: Murong Huang said, "Now the raiders are this strong—your saying they are sure to flee—I dare not yet believe."
translations.idiomatic: Murong Huang doubted: the foe looked too strong.

sentences.zh: 」泓曰：「殿下言盛者，人事耳，臣言必走者，天時也，胡足為疑！

translations.literal: Hong said, "What Your Highness calls strong is human affairs; what your servant calls sure to flee is heaven's season—how is it worth doubting!"
translations.idiomatic: Huang Hong replied that strength was mere human show while heaven decreed rout—no room for doubt.

sentences.zh: 」及期，季龍果退，皝益奇之。

translations.literal: When the term came, Jilong indeed withdrew; Murong Huang still more marveled at him.
translations.idiomatic: Within two days Shi Hu retreated as predicted.

sentences.zh: 及慕容俊即王位，遷從事中郎，儁聞冉閔亂，將圖中原，訪之於泓，泓勸行，儁從之。

translations.literal: When Murong Jun assumed the royal title, Hong was promoted to adjutant; Jun heard of Ran Min's turmoil and was about to plan the Central Plain; he consulted Hong on it; Hong urged going; Jun followed this.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Jun, hearing Ran Min's chaos, asked Huang Hong, who urged a central-plain campaign—Jun agreed.

sentences.zh: 及僭號，署為進謀將軍、太史令、關內侯，尋加奉車都尉、西海太守、領太史令、開陽亭侯，又封平舒縣五等伯，常從左右，諮決大事，靈台令許敦害其寵，諂事慕容評，設異議以毀之，及以泓為太史靈台諸署統，加給事中。

translations.literal: When he arrogated the title, he appointed Hong Forward Planning General, grand astrologer, marquis within the passes; before long adding chariot commandant, West Sea governor, concurrent grand astrologer, marquis of Kaiyang village, again enfeoffing him as fifth-rank baron of Pingshu county; he constantly followed left and right, consulting and deciding great affairs; Spirit Terrace Director Xu Dun envied his favor, flattered Murong Ping, set contrary opinions to slander him, until Hong was made supervisor of all Grand Astrologer and Spirit Terrace offices, concurrently palace attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Jun heaped titles on him—forward-planning general, grand astrologer, marquis, chariot commandant, West Sea governor—while Xu Dun slandered him and Ping reassigned him to head every astrological office plus palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 泓待敦彌厚，不以毀己易心。

translations.literal: Hong treated Dun still more generously and did not change his mind because Dun slandered him.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Hong treated Xu Dun generously despite the slander.

sentences.zh: 慕容暐敗，以老歸家，歎曰：「燕必中興，其在吳王，恨吾年過不見耳。

translations.literal: When Murong Wei was defeated, he returned home old and sighed, saying, "Yan is sure to have a restoration; it lies with the Prince of Wu—I regret my years are past and I will not see it."
translations.idiomatic: After Murong Wei's fall he retired, predicting Yan's revival under the Prince of Wu—too old to see it.

sentences.zh: 」年九十七卒。

translations.literal: He died at ninety-seven.
translations.idiomatic: He died at ninety-seven.

sentences.zh: 卒後三年，偽吳王慕容垂興焉。

translations.literal: Three years after his death the false Prince of Wu Murong Chui rose.
translations.idiomatic: Three years later Murong Chui, the "Wu" prince, rose as he foretold.

sentences.zh: 索紞

translations.literal: Suo Dan.
translations.idiomatic: Suo Dan.

sentences.zh: 索紞，字叔徹，敦煌人也。

translations.literal: Suo Dan, courtesy name Shuche, was a native of Dunhuang.
translations.idiomatic: Suo Dan, courtesy name Shuche, came from Dunhuang.

sentences.zh: 少游京師，受業太學，博綜經籍，遂為通儒。

translations.literal: In his youth he traveled to the capital, received instruction at the Imperial Academy, broadly mastered the classics, and thereby became a comprehensive scholar.
translations.idiomatic: He studied at the capital academy and became a broad scholar.

sentences.zh: 明陰陽天文，善術數占侯。

translations.literal: He understood yin-yang and astronomy; he was good at numerology and omen divination.
translations.idiomatic: He knew yin-yang, astronomy, and number divination.

sentences.zh: 司徒辟，除郎中，知中國將亂，避世而歸。

translations.literal: The minister summoned him and appointed him gentleman; knowing the Middle Kingdom would be in chaos, he avoided the age and returned.
translations.idiomatic: The minister named him gentleman; foreseeing chaos, he went home.

sentences.zh: 鄉人從紞占問吉凶，門中如市，紞曰：「攻乎異端，戒在害己；

translations.literal: Townspeople followed Dan to divine and ask auspiciousness and inauspiciousness; at the gate it was like a market; Dan said, "Assaulting those heterodox paths—warning lies in harming oneself;"
translations.idiomatic: Neighbors mobbed his gate for fortunes until he quoted the Analects: attacking heterodoxy harms oneself.

sentences.zh: 無為多事，多事多患。

translations.literal: Doing nothing is many affairs—many affairs, many troubles.
translations.idiomatic: More business meant more trouble—best stay quiet.

sentences.zh: 」遂詭言虛說，無驗乃止。

translations.literal: Thereupon he spoke deceptively and emptily; when there was no verification they then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: He gave absurd answers until seekers quit.

sentences.zh: 惟以占夢為無悔吝，乃不逆問者。

translations.literal: Only in interpreting dreams he had no regret or stinginess—then he did not refuse questioners.
translations.idiomatic: Dream interpretation alone he took seriously and never refused.

sentences.zh: 孝廉令狐策夢立冰上，與冰下人語。

translations.literal: The filially recommended Linghu Ce dreamed standing on ice speaking with a man beneath the ice.
translations.idiomatic: Recommended scholar Linghu Ce dreamed he stood on ice talking to someone under the ice.

sentences.zh: 紞曰：「冰上為陽，冰下為陰，陰陽事也。

translations.literal: Dan said, "Above the ice is yang; beneath the ice is yin—yin-yang affairs."
translations.idiomatic: Suo Dan said ice above was yang, below yin—a yin-yang matter.

sentences.zh: 士如歸妻，迨冰未泮，婚姻事也。

translations.literal: The gentleman as if taking a wife, while the ice has not yet melted—marriage affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He cited the Book of Songs: taking a wife while frost still holds—marriage.

sentences.zh: 君在冰上與冰下人語，為陽語陰，媒介事也。

translations.literal: Your lordship on the ice speaks with the man beneath the ice—yang speaks to yin—a go-between affair.
translations.idiomatic: Standing on yang ice speaking to yin below meant matchmaking.

sentences.zh: 君當為人作媒，冰泮而婚成。

translations.literal: You ought to act as go-between for people; when the ice melts the marriage is accomplished.
translations.idiomatic: He would broker a wedding once the ice broke.

sentences.zh: 」策曰：「老夫耄矣，不為媒也。

translations.literal: Ce said, "This old man is senile; I will not act as go-between."
translations.idiomatic: Linghu Ce said he was too old to mediate matches.

sentences.zh: 」會太守田豹因策為子求鄉人張公徵女，仲春而成婚焉。

translations.literal: Just then prefect Tian Bao, through Ce, sought for his son the daughter of townsman Zhang Gongzheng; in mid-spring the marriage was completed.
translations.idiomatic: Prefect Tian Bao soon had Ce broker his son's betrothal to Zhang Gongzheng's daughter—the wedding came that mid-spring.

sentences.zh: 郡主簿張宅夢走馬上山，還繞舍三周，但見松柏，不知門處。

translations.literal: The commandery chief clerk Zhang Zhai dreamed a horse ran up a mountain, returned and circled the house three circuits, but saw only pines and cypresses and did not know where the gate was.
translations.idiomatic: Chief clerk Zhang Zhai dreamed a horse climb a hill, circle his house thrice, yet saw only pines with no gate in sight.

sentences.zh: 紞曰：「馬屬離，離為火。

translations.literal: Dan said, "Horse belongs to li; li is fire."
translations.idiomatic: Suo Dan said horses signified the Li trigram—fire.

sentences.zh: 火，禍也。

translations.literal: Fire means calamity.
translations.idiomatic: Fire meant disaster.

sentences.zh: 人上山，為凶字。

translations.literal: Man on a mountain forms the character for 'inauspicious.'
translations.idiomatic: A man on a mountain formed the graph for 'ominous.'

sentences.zh: 但見松伯，墓門象也。

translations.literal: Only seeing pines and cypresses is the image of a tomb gate.
translations.idiomatic: Pines and cypresses hinted at a cemetery gate.

sentences.zh: 不知門處，為無門也。

translations.literal: Not knowing where the gate is means there is no gate.
translations.idiomatic: No visible gate meant no escape.

sentences.zh: 三周，三期也。

translations.literal: Three circuits mean three periods.
translations.idiomatic: Three rounds meant three years.

sentences.zh: 後三年必有大禍。

translations.literal: After three years there is sure to be a great calamity.
translations.idiomatic: A great disaster would strike within three years.

sentences.zh: 」宅果以謀反伏誅。

translations.literal: Zhai indeed because plotting rebellion was executed.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zhai was executed for treason three years later.

sentences.zh: 索充初夢天上有二棺落充前，紞曰：「棺者，職也，當有京師貴人舉君。

translations.literal: Suo Chong at first dreamed two coffins in the sky fell before Chong; Dan said, "Coffin means office; there ought to be a noble man of the capital who recommends your lord."
translations.idiomatic: Suo Chong dreamed sky-coffins; Suo Dan read coffins as office—a capital patron would recommend him.

sentences.zh: 二官者，頻再遷。

translations.literal: Two offices mean frequent double promotion.
translations.idiomatic: Two coffins meant two swift promotions.

sentences.zh: 」俄而司徒王戎書屬太守使舉充，太守先署充功曹而舉孝廉。

translations.literal: Before long Minister of Education Wang Rong wrote instructing the prefect to recommend Chong; the prefect first signed Chong as merit clerk and then recommended him filially incorrupt.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Rong soon had the prefect recommend Suo Chong, first as merit clerk, then as filially incorrupt.

sentences.zh: 充後夢見一虜，脫上衣來詣充。

translations.literal: Later Chong dreamed one captive, removing his upper garment, came to Chong.
translations.idiomatic: Suo Chong later dreamed a barbarian strip his jacket and approach him.

sentences.zh: 紞曰：「虜去上中，下半男字，夷狄陰類，君婦當生男。

translations.literal: Dan said, "Captive without the upper middle leaves the lower half as the character 'male'; barbarians are yin in kind—your lordship's wife ought to bear a boy."
translations.idiomatic: Suo Dan parsed the graph: captive minus top yields 'male'—his wife would bear a son.

sentences.zh: 」終如其言。

translations.literal: In the end it happened as he said.
translations.idiomatic: It proved true.

sentences.zh: 宋桷夢內中有一人著赤衣，桷手把兩杖，極打之。

translations.literal: Song Jue dreamed inside the house there was one person in red clothes; Jue in his hand grasped two staffs and beat him extremely.
translations.idiomatic: Song Jue dreamed a red figure inside his house whom he beat with twin rods.

sentences.zh: 紞曰：「內中有人，肉字也。

translations.literal: Dan said, "Inside the house there is a person—the character 'flesh.'"
translations.idiomatic: Suo Dan said a man indoors formed the graph rou 'flesh.'

sentences.zh: 肉色，赤也。

translations.literal: Flesh color is red.
translations.idiomatic: Flesh-colored meant red.

sentences.zh: 兩杖，箸象也。

translations.literal: Two staffs are the image of chopsticks.
translations.idiomatic: Twin sticks stood for chopsticks.

sentences.zh: 極打之，飽肉食也。

translations.literal: Beating them extremely means eating meat to satiety.
translations.idiomatic: Beating fiercely meant feasting on meat.

sentences.zh: 」俄而亦驗焉。

translations.literal: Before long it likewise verified.
translations.idiomatic: The dream soon came true.

sentences.zh: 黃平問紞曰：「我昨夜夢舍中馬舞，數十人向馬拍手，此何祥也？

translations.literal: Huang Ping asked Dan, saying, "Last night I dreamed horses dancing in my house, several tens of people clapping toward the horses—what is this auspicious sign?"
translations.idiomatic: Huang Ping dreamed horses dancing at home while a crowd clapped.

sentences.zh: 」紞曰：「馬者，火也，舞為火起。

translations.literal: Dan said, "Horse is fire; dancing is fire rising."
translations.idiomatic: Horses meant fire; dancing meant flames rising.

sentences.zh: 向馬拍手，救火人也。

translations.literal: Clapping toward the horses are the people who put out the fire.
translations.idiomatic: Clapping toward the horses meant firefighting.

sentences.zh: 」平未歸而火作。

translations.literal: Before Ping returned, fire broke out.
translations.idiomatic: Fire broke out before Huang Ping got home.

sentences.zh: 索綏夢東有二角書詣綏，大角朽敗，小角有題韋囊角佩，一在前，一在後。

translations.literal: Suo Sui dreamed in the east there were two horned documents that came to Sui; the great horn was rotten, the small horn had an inscription on a leather bag at the horn pendant—one in front, one behind.
translations.idiomatic: Suo Sui dreamed two horned edicts from the east—one rotted, one inscribed, one before, one aft.

sentences.zh: 紞曰：「大角朽敗，腐棺木。

translations.literal: Dan said, "The great horn rotten means rotten coffin wood."
translations.idiomatic: The crumbling great horn meant a decaying coffin.

sentences.zh: 小角有題，題所詣。

translations.literal: The small horn having an inscription means the place it addresses.
translations.idiomatic: The marked small horn showed the message's target.

sentences.zh: 一在前，前紞凶也。

translations.literal: One in front—'before' is Suo's inauspicious.
translations.idiomatic: The front slip foretold Suo Dan's ill omen approaching.

sentences.zh: 一在後，後背也。

translations.literal: One behind—'behind' is the back.
translations.idiomatic: The rear slip pointed to someone's back—kin behind him.

sentences.zh: 當有凶背之問。

translations.literal: There ought to be a calamity question concerning a back.
translations.idiomatic: A bereavement message would come from the east.

sentences.zh: 」時綏父在東，居三日而凶問至。

translations.literal: At the time Sui's father was in the east; within three days the calamity question arrived.
translations.idiomatic: Suo Sui's father lay eastward; within three days news of his death arrived.

sentences.zh: 郡功曹張邈嘗奉使詣州，夜夢狼啖一腳。

translations.literal: The commandery merit clerk Zhang Miao once was sent on mission to the province; at night he dreamed a wolf gnawed one foot.
translations.idiomatic: Merit clerk Zhang Miao dreamed a wolf chewed his foot on a mission.

sentences.zh: 紞曰：「腳肉被啖，為卻字。

translations.literal: Dan said, "Foot flesh being gnawed forms the character 'retreat.'"
translations.idiomatic: Gnawed foot-flesh formed the graph for 'withdraw.'

sentences.zh: 」會東虜反，遂不行。

translations.literal: Just then eastern barbarians rebelled; therefore he did not go.
translations.idiomatic: Eastern rebels rose and the journey was canceled.

sentences.zh: 凡所占莫不驗。

translations.literal: In general what he divined had none that did not verify.
translations.idiomatic: Every divination Suo Dan gave proved true.

sentences.zh: 太守陰澹從求占書，紞曰：「昔入太學，因一父老為主人，其人無所不知，又匿姓名，有似隱者，紞因從父老問占夢之術，希申鄙藝，審測而說，實無書也。

translations.literal: Prefect Yin Dan sought divination books from him; Dan said, "Formerly I entered the Imperial Academy and, through one old man as host, that person knew everything and also hid his name, somewhat like a recluse; I therefore asked the old man the art of dream divination, hoping to extend my mean skill—examining and measuring then explaining—truly there are no books."
translations.idiomatic: Prefect Yin Dan asked for manuals; Suo Dan said he had learned dream lore from a nameless elder at the academy—no written text existed.

sentences.zh: 」澹命為西閣祭酒，紞辭曰：「少無山林之操，遊學京師，交結時賢，會中國不靖，欲養志終年。

translations.literal: Yin Dan ordered him to be libationer of the west gallery; Suo Dan declined, saying, "In youth I had no bent for mountain forests; I studied in the capital and befriended the worthies of the time; meeting the Middle Kingdom's unrest I wished to nurture my intent to the year's end."
translations.idiomatic: Yin Dan named him west-gallery libationer; Suo Dan refused, citing no reclusive bent and wishing to ride out the turmoil quietly.

sentences.zh: 老亦至矣，不求聞達。

translations.literal: Old age also has arrived; I do not seek fame and advancement.
translations.idiomatic: He was old and sought no office.

sentences.zh: 又少不習勤，老無吏幹，濛汜之年，弗敢聞命。

translations.literal: Moreover in youth I did not practice diligence; in old age I lack clerkly capacity—in the Mengsi years I dare not hear the command.
translations.idiomatic: He pleaded age and no talent for administration.

sentences.zh: 」澹以束帛禮之，月致羊酒。

translations.literal: Dan with bundles of silk saluted him and monthly sent sheep and wine.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Dan honored him with silk, mutton, and wine each month.

sentences.zh: 年七十五，卒於家。

translations.literal: At seventy-five he died at home.
translations.idiomatic: He died at home aged seventy-five.

sentences.zh: 孟欽

translations.literal: Meng Qin.
translations.idiomatic: Meng Qin.

sentences.zh: 孟欽，洛陽人也。

translations.literal: Meng Qin was a native of Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Meng Qin came from Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 有左慈、劉根之術，百姓惑而赴之。

translations.literal: He had the arts of Zuo Ci and Liu Gen; the common people were deluded and rushed to him.
translations.idiomatic: He wielded arts like Zuo Ci and Liu Gen and drew credulous crowds.

sentences.zh: 苻堅召詣長安，惡其惑眾，命苻融誅之。

translations.literal: Fu Jian summoned him to Chang'an, hated his deluding the masses, and ordered Fu Rong to execute him.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Jian summoned him to Chang'an, then ordered Fu Rong to kill him for misleading the people.

sentences.zh: 俄而欽至，融留之，遂大宴郡僚，酒酣，目左右收欽。

translations.literal: Before long Qin arrived; Rong detained him and thereupon greatly feasted commandery aides; when wine was deep he signaled attendants to seize Qin.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Rong feasted him, then at a signal moved to arrest him.

sentences.zh: 欽化為旋風，飛出第外。

translations.literal: Qin transformed into a whirlwind and flew out beyond the compound.
translations.idiomatic: Meng Qin became a whirlwind and blew out of the hall.

sentences.zh: 頃之，有告在城東者，融遣騎追之，垂及，忽然已遠，或有兵眾距戰，或前有溪澗，騎不得過，遂不知所在。

translations.literal: In a moment someone reported him in the city's east; Rong sent cavalry in pursuit; they almost caught up when suddenly he was already far; sometimes there were troops resisting battle, sometimes before them were streams and gullies the horses could not cross; in the end his whereabouts were unknown.
translations.idiomatic: Pursuers nearly caught him but met phantom armies and uncrossable streams until he vanished.

sentences.zh: 堅未，復見於青州。

translations.literal: Late in Jian's reign he was again seen in Qing Province.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Fu Jian's reign he reappeared in Qingzhou.

sentences.zh: 苻朗尋之，入於海島。

translations.literal: Fu Lang searched for him; he entered a sea island.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Lang tracked him to a sea isle.

sentences.zh: 王嘉

translations.literal: Wang Jia.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jia.

sentences.zh: 王嘉，字子年，隴西安陽人也。

translations.literal: Wang Jia, courtesy name Zinian, was a native of Anyang in Longxi.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jia, courtesy name Zinian, came from Anyang in Longxi.

sentences.zh: 輕舉止，醜形貌，外若不足，而聰睿內明。

translations.literal: He was light in bearing and ugly in form; outwardly as if insufficient, yet bright and keen within.
translations.idiomatic: He seemed a buffoon but was inwardly brilliant.

sentences.zh: 滑稽好語笑，不食五穀，不衣美麗，清虛服氣，不與世人交遊。

translations.literal: Witty, fond of speech and laughter, he ate not the five grains, wore not fine beauty, cleared his void and ingested qi, and did not mingle with people of the age.
translations.idiomatic: He jested, shunned grain and silk, fed on qi, and shunned society.

sentences.zh: 隱于東陽穀，鑿崖穴居，弟子受業者數百人，亦皆穴處。

translations.literal: He hid in Dongyang Valley, chiseled a cliff and dwelt in a cave; disciples who received his teaching were several hundred persons, and they too dwelt in caves.
translations.idiomatic: He and hundreds of pupils lived in cliff caves in Dongyang valley.

sentences.zh: 石季龍之末，棄其徒眾，至長安，潛隱於終南山，結庵廬而止。

translations.literal: At the end of Shi Jilong's time he abandoned his crowd of disciples, went to Chang'an, and secretly hid on Mount Zhongnan, tying a hut and stopping.
translations.idiomatic: Late under Shi Hu he abandoned followers, hid on Zhongnan near Chang'an, and built a hut.

sentences.zh: 門人聞而復隨之，乃遷於倒獸山。

translations.literal: Disciples heard and again followed him; he then moved to Mount Daoshou.
translations.idiomatic: Pupils found him so he moved to Mount Daoshou.

sentences.zh: 苻堅累徵不起，公侯已下咸躬往參詣，好尚之士無不師宗之。

translations.literal: Fu Jian repeatedly summoned him but he would not rise; dukes and marquises down all personally went to visit; gentlemen of fond bent all took him as teacher and ancestor.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Jian's summons failed; nobles visited in person and scholars revered him.

sentences.zh: 問其當世事者，皆隨問而對。

translations.literal: When asked about affairs of the present age, he all answered following the question.
translations.idiomatic: He answered every question about current events.

sentences.zh: 好為譬喻，狀如戲調；

translations.literal: He liked to make analogies; his manner was like jesting banter;
translations.idiomatic: He spoke in riddling jest;

sentences.zh: 言未然之事，辭如讖記，當時鮮能曉之，事過皆驗。

translations.literal: speaking of things not yet happened, his words were like prophecy records; at the time few could understand them; after events passed all verified.
translations.idiomatic: his future tense lines read like cryptic verse—few understood until they came true.

sentences.zh: 堅將南征，遣使者問之。

translations.literal: When Jian was about to campaign south, he dispatched an envoy to ask him.
translations.idiomatic: Before Fu Jian's southern campaign he sent an envoy to Wang Jia.

sentences.zh: 嘉曰：「金剛火強。

translations.literal: Jia said, "Vajra, fire strong."
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jia answered: "Metal hard, fire strong"—a warning.

sentences.zh: 」乃乘使者馬，正衣冠，徐徐東行數百步，而策馬馳反，脫衣服，棄冠履而歸，下馬踞床，一無所言。

translations.literal: Thereupon he mounted the envoy's horse, straightened cap and robes, slowly went east several hundred paces, then whipped the horse to gallop back, cast off clothes, threw away cap and shoes and returned, dismounted and squatted on the bed, saying nothing at all.
translations.idiomatic: He borrowed the envoy's horse, rode east slowly, galloped back stripping clothes and shoes, then sat mute on a couch.

sentences.zh: 使者還告，堅不語，復遣問之，曰：「吾世祚云何？

translations.literal: The envoy returned and reported; Jian did not speak; again he sent to ask, saying, "How is my dynastic fortune?"
translations.idiomatic: Fu Jian sent again to ask how long his line would last.

sentences.zh: 」嘉曰：「未央。

translations.literal: Jia said, "Not yet ended."
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jia said "Weiyang"—literally "not yet end."

sentences.zh: 」咸以為吉。

translations.literal: All thought it auspicious.
translations.idiomatic: Courtiers mistook it for good news.

sentences.zh: 明年癸未，敗於淮南，所謂未年而有殃也。

translations.literal: The next year guiwei, he was defeated at Huainan—this is what is meant by the wei year yet having calamity.
translations.idiomatic: Next year gui-wei he lost at Fei River—the wordplay meant disaster in the wei year, not endless blessing.

sentences.zh: 人侯之者，至心則見之，不至心則隱形不見。

translations.literal: Those who waited on him, if utmost in heart then saw him; if not utmost in heart then he hid form and was not seen.
translations.idiomatic: Earnest visitors saw him; half-hearted seekers found him invisible.

sentences.zh: 衣服在架，履杖猶存，或欲取其衣者，終不及，企而取之，衣架逾高，而屋亦不大，覆杖諸物亦如之。

translations.literal: Clothes on the rack, shoes and staff still there—if someone wished to take his clothes, in the end they could not reach; standing on tiptoe to take them, the clothes rack grew higher yet the house was not large; covering staff and other objects was likewise.
translations.idiomatic: His robe and staff on a rack eluded grasp—stretching for them raised the rack while the hut stayed small.

sentences.zh: 姚萇之入長安，禮嘉如苻堅故事，逼以自隨，每事諮之。

translations.literal: When Yao Chang entered Chang'an, he treated Jia like Fu Jian's precedent, forcing him to follow himself, consulting him on each affair.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Chang honored him as Fu Jian had and kept him for counsel.

sentences.zh: 萇既與苻登相持，問嘉曰：「吾得殺苻登定天下不？

translations.literal: After Chang was locked with Fu Deng in stalemate, he asked Jia, "Can I kill Fu Deng and settle All-under-Heaven?"
translations.idiomatic: Yao Chang asked if he could kill Fu Deng and unify the realm.

sentences.zh: 」嘉曰：「略得之。

translations.literal: Jia said, "Lue obtains it."
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jia said "lue de zhi"—roughly "you will get it."

sentences.zh: 」萇怒曰：「得當云得，何略之有！

translations.literal: Chang angrily said, "If you obtain, say obtain—what is this 'lue'!"
translations.idiomatic: Yao Chang raged at the hedge word lue.

sentences.zh: 」遂斬之。

translations.literal: Thereupon he executed him.
translations.idiomatic: He had Wang Jia beheaded.

sentences.zh: 先此，釋道安謂嘉曰：「世故方殷，可以行矣。

translations.literal: Before this, Shi Daoan had said to Jia, "The world's troubles are just now thick—you may go."
translations.idiomatic: Earlier monk Daoan had told him to flee the mounting troubles.

sentences.zh: 」嘉答曰：「卿其先行，吾負債未果去。

translations.literal: Jia answered, "You ought to go first; I have a debt unpaid and cannot yet leave."
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jia answered that Daoan should leave first—he still owed a karmic debt.

sentences.zh: 」俄而道安亡，至是而嘉戮死，所謂「負債」者也。

translations.literal: Before long Daoan died; when it came to this Jia was executed—this is what is called 'debt.'
translations.idiomatic: Daoan died soon after; Wang Jia's execution fulfilled the "debt" riddle.

sentences.zh: 苻登聞嘉死，設壇哭之，贈太師，諡曰文。

translations.literal: When Fu Deng heard Jia had died, he set up an altar and wept for him, posthumously gifting Grand Preceptor with posthumous name Wen.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Deng mourned Wang Jia as Grand Preceptor Wen.

sentences.zh: 及萇死，萇子興字子略方殺登，「略得」之謂也。

translations.literal: When Chang died, Chang's son Xing, courtesy name Zilue, thereupon killed Deng—this is what 'lue de' meant.
translations.idiomatic: When Yao Chang died, his son Yao Xing—style Zilue—killed Fu Deng, fulfilling the "lue de" wordplay.

sentences.zh: 嘉之死日，人有隴上見之。

translations.literal: On the day Jia died, someone saw him on the Long uplands.
translations.idiomatic: The day he died, witnesses saw him alive on the Long plateau.

sentences.zh: 其所造《牽三歌讖》，事過皆驗，累世猶傳之。

translations.literal: What he composed, the Qiansange Prophecies, after events passed all verified; for generations they were still transmitted.
translations.idiomatic: His Qiansange prophecy verses all came true and circulated for generations.

sentences.zh: 又著《拾遺錄》十卷，其記事多詭怪，今行於世。

translations.literal: Again he wrote the Shiyi lu in ten scrolls; its records are mostly uncanny and strange; now it circulates in the world.
translations.idiomatic: His ten-scroll Records of Gathered Remains of odd events still circulates.

sentences.zh: 僧涉

translations.literal: Seng She.
translations.idiomatic: Seng She.

sentences.zh: 僧涉者，西域人也，不知何姓。

translations.literal: Seng She was a man of the Western Regions; none knew his surname.
translations.idiomatic: Monk She came from the west; his surname was unknown.

sentences.zh: 少為沙門，苻堅時入長安。

translations.literal: In youth he became a shramana; in Fu Jian's time he entered Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: He tonsured young and reached Chang'an under Fu Jian.

sentences.zh: 虛靜服氣，不食五穀，日能行五百里，言未然之事，驗若指掌。

translations.literal: Empty and still, ingesting qi, he ate not the five grains, could travel five hundred li in a day, and spoke of things not yet happened as clear as pointing at a palm.
translations.idiomatic: He fasted on qi, walked five hundred li a day, and foretold the future with clarity.

sentences.zh: 能以秘祝下神龍，每旱，堅常使之咒龍請雨。

translations.literal: He could by secret invocations bring down divine dragons; whenever there was drought, Jian constantly had him curse dragons to request rain.
translations.idiomatic: Secret spells drew dragons into bowls whenever drought struck.

sentences.zh: 俄而龍下缽中，天輒大雨，堅及群臣親就缽觀之。

translations.literal: Before long a dragon came down into the bowl; heaven then sent great rain; Jian and his ministers personally approached the bowl to observe it.
translations.idiomatic: Dragons entered his bowl and rain followed while Fu Jian and courtiers watched.

sentences.zh: 卒于長安。

translations.literal: He died in Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 後大旱移時，苻堅歎曰：「涉公若在，豈憂此乎！」

translations.literal: Later after long drought Fu Jian sighed, "If Lord She were still here, how would I worry about this!"
translations.idiomatic: Years later Fu Jian sighed in drought that only Monk She could have saved them.

sentences.zh: 郭黁

translations.literal: Guo Wu.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Wu.

sentences.zh: 郭黁，西平人也。

translations.literal: Guo Wu was a native of Xiping.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Wu came from Xiping.

sentences.zh: 少明《老》《易》，仕郡主簿。

translations.literal: In his youth he understood the Laozi and Changes; he served as commandery chief clerk.
translations.idiomatic: He mastered Laozi and Changes and served as chief clerk.

sentences.zh: 張天錫末年，苻氏每有西伐之問，太守趙凝使黁筮之，黁曰：「若郡內二月十五日失囚者，東軍當至，涼祚必終。

translations.literal: In the last years of Zhang Tiansui, whenever the Fu clan had word of a western campaign, Prefect Zhao Ning had Wu divine by milfoil; Wu said, "If on the fifteenth day of the second month the commandery loses a prisoner, the eastern army will arrive and Liang's mandate will surely end."
translations.idiomatic: As Former Liang neared fall, Zhao Ning had Guo Wu cast yarrow: if a prisoner escaped on the second month's fifteenth, eastern troops would end Liang.

sentences.zh: 」凝乃申約屬縣。

translations.literal: Ning thereupon issued orders binding all subordinate counties.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Ning alerted every county.

sentences.zh: 至十五日，鮮卑折掘送馬於凝，凝怒其非駿，幽之內廄，鮮卑懼而夜遁。

translations.literal: When the fifteenth day came, Xianbei of Zhejue presented horses to Ning; Ning was angry they were not thoroughbreds and imprisoned them in the inner stable; the Xianbei feared and fled by night.
translations.idiomatic: On the day Xianbei herders delivered horses Zhao Ning jailed them for poor stock and they broke out by night.

sentences.zh: 凝以告黁，黁曰：「是也。

translations.literal: Ning reported to Wu; Wu said, "It is so."
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Ning told Guo Wu, who said the omen fit.

sentences.zh: 國家將亡，不可復振。」

translations.literal: The state is about to perish; it cannot be revived."
translations.idiomatic: The state would fall beyond saving."

sentences.zh: 苻堅末，當陽門震，刺史梁熙問黁曰：「其祥安在？

translations.literal: At the end of Fu Jian's reign the Dangyang Gate quaked; Inspector Liang Xi asked Wu, "Where lies its portent?"
translations.idiomatic: When Dangyang gate shook under Fu Jian, Liang Xi asked the meaning.

sentences.zh: 」黁曰：「為四夷之事也。

translations.literal: Wu said, "It is a matter of the four barbarians."
translations.idiomatic: Guo Wu said it foretold barbarian affairs.

sentences.zh: 當有外國二王來朝主上，一當反國，一死此城。

translations.literal: There ought to be two foreign kings who come to court to the lord; one ought to return to his state, one die in this city.
translations.idiomatic: Two foreign kings would visit; one would return home, one die in the city.

sentences.zh: 」歲餘而鄯善及前部王朝於苻堅，西歸，鄯善王死于姑臧。

translations.literal: After more than a year Shanshan and the king of the Front Department courted Fu Jian, went west homeward, and the king of Shanshan died at Guzang.
translations.idiomatic: A year later Shanshan and Front-Department kings paid court; Shanshan's king died at Guzang on the way west.

sentences.zh: 呂光之王河西也，西海太守王楨叛，黁勸光襲之。

translations.literal: When Lu Guang became king west of the River, West Sea governor Wang Zhen rebelled; Wu urged Guang to strike him.
translations.idiomatic: When Lu Guang held Hexi, rebel Wang Zhen drew Guo Wu's advice to attack.

sentences.zh: 光之左丞呂寶曰：「千里襲人，自昔所難，況王者之師天下所聞，何可僥倖以邀成功！

translations.literal: Guang's left aide Lu Bao said, "A thousand-li raid on others has from old been hard—how much more a royal host famed through the realm—how can you hazard luck to beg success!"
translations.idiomatic: Lu Bao warned that a thousand-li strike on a famous army was folly.

sentences.zh: 黁不可從，誤人大事。

translations.literal: Wu must not be followed—it will ruin the great affair.
translations.idiomatic: He said Guo Wu must not be heeded.

sentences.zh: 」黁曰：「若其不捷，黁自伏鈇鉞之誅。

translations.literal: Wu said, "If it is not victorious, Wu himself will submit to axe and halberd execution."
translations.idiomatic: Guo Wu vowed to face execution if the raid failed.

sentences.zh: 如其克也，左丞為無謀矣。

translations.literal: If it conquers, the left aide will have been without strategy.
translations.idiomatic: If it won, Lu Bao would look a fool.

sentences.zh: 」光從而克之。

translations.literal: Guang followed him and conquered.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Guang attacked and won.

sentences.zh: 光比之京管，常參帷幄密謀。

translations.literal: Guang compared him to Guan Zhong; he constantly joined curtain stratagems.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Guang likened him to Guan Zhong and kept him in secret council.

sentences.zh: 光將伐乞伏乾歸，黁諫曰：「今太白未出，不宜行師，往必無功，終當覆敗。

translations.literal: When Guang was about to campaign against Qifu GanGui, Wu remonstrated, saying, "Now the Great White has not yet risen; it is not fitting to move the army; if you go you will surely accomplish nothing and in the end will overturn in defeat."
translations.idiomatic: Guo Wu warned against marching before Venus rose—failure awaited.

sentences.zh: 」太史令賈曜以為必有秦隴之地。

translations.literal: Grand Astrologer Jia Yao held that he was sure to obtain Qin-Long lands.
translations.idiomatic: Grand astrologer Jia Yao predicted victory in Qin and Long.

sentences.zh: 及克金城，光使曜詰黁，黁密謂光曰：「昨有流星東墮，當有伏屍死將，雖得此城，憂在不守。

translations.literal: When they took Jincheng, Guang sent Yao to question Wu; Wu secretly told Guang, "Yesterday there was a shooting star falling east—there ought to be corpses strewn and a general dead; although you obtain this city, the worry lies in not holding it."
translations.idiomatic: After taking Jincheng Guo Wu whispered that a fallen meteor meant dead generals and a city hard to hold.

sentences.zh: 正月上旬，河冰將解，若不早渡，恐有大變。

translations.literal: In the first ten days of the first month the river ice will break; if you do not ford early, I fear a great change.
translations.idiomatic: River ice would break in early first month—cross soon or face disaster.

sentences.zh: 」後二日而敗問至，光引軍渡河訖，冰泮。

translations.literal: After two days defeat news arrived; Guang led the army to finish fording the river; the ice melted.
translations.idiomatic: Two days later defeat news came; Lu Guang finished crossing as the ice broke.

sentences.zh: 時人服其神驗。

translations.literal: People of the time admired his spiritlike verification.
translations.idiomatic: Contemporaries marveled at his accuracy.

sentences.zh: 光以黁為散騎常侍、太常。

translations.literal: Guang appointed Wu cadet attendant in regular service and grand master of ceremonies.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Guang named him supernumerary attendant and grand master of ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 黁後以光年老，知其將敗，遂與光僕射王祥起兵作亂。

translations.literal: Wu later because Guang was old knew he would be defeated; thereupon with Guang's steward Wang Xiang he raised troops in rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing Lu Guang aged and doomed, Guo Wu rebelled with steward Wang Xiang.

sentences.zh: 百姓聞黁起兵，咸以聖人起事，事無不成，故相率從之如不及。

translations.literal: When the commoners heard Wu raised troops, all thought a sage had begun an affair and nothing would fail; therefore they followed him in haste as if they could not catch up.
translations.idiomatic: The people thought a sage led a sure revolt and flocked to him.

sentences.zh: 黁以為代呂者王，乃推王乞基為主。

translations.literal: Wu thought 'the one who replaces Lu is Wang' and therefore pushed Wang Qiji to be leader.
translations.idiomatic: He read the prophecy "Wang replaces Lu" and raised Wang Qiji as figurehead.

sentences.zh: 後呂隆降姚興，興以王尚為涼州刺史，終如黁言。

translations.literal: Later Lu Long surrendered to Yao Xing; Xing appointed Wang Shang governor of Liang Province—ultimately as Wu had said.
translations.idiomatic: When Lu Long yielded to Yao Xing, Wang Shang became Liangzhou governor—fulfilling Guo Wu's line.

sentences.zh: 黁之與光相持也，逃人稱呂統病死，黁曰：「未也，光、統之命盡在一時。

translations.literal: When Wu and Guang were locked in stalemate, a fugitive said Lu Tong had died of illness; Wu said, "Not yet; Guang's and Tong's fates end at the same moment."
translations.idiomatic: Rumors said Lu Tong had died; Guo Wu said Lu Guang would die with him.

sentences.zh: 」黁後統死三日而光死。

translations.literal: Later Tong died three days and Guang died.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Tong died; three days later Lu Guang died.

sentences.zh: 黁嘗曰：「涼州謙光殿后當有索頭鮮卑居之。

translations.literal: Wu once said, "Behind Liangzhou's Modest Light Hall there will be Tuoba Xianbei dwelling."
translations.idiomatic: He predicted Tuoba Xianbei would hold the hall behind Liangzhou's Qian-Guang palace.

sentences.zh: 」終於禿髮傉檀、沮渠蒙遜迭據姑臧。

translations.literal: In the end Tufa Rutan and Juqu Mengxun alternately held Guzang.
translations.idiomatic: Tufa Rutan and Juqu Mengxun later seized Guzang in turn.

sentences.zh: 黁性褊酷，不為士庶所附。

translations.literal: Wu by nature was narrow and cruel and was not attached to by gentry and commoners.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Wu was harsh and won little loyalty.

sentences.zh: 戰敗，奔乞伏乾歸。

translations.literal: Defeated in battle, he fled to Qifu GanGui.
translations.idiomatic: He fled to Qifu GanGui after defeat.

sentences.zh: 乾歸敗，入姚興。

translations.literal: When GanGui was defeated, he entered Yao Xing.
translations.idiomatic: After GanGui fell he joined Yao Xing.

sentences.zh: 黁以滅姚者晉，遂將妻子南奔，為追兵所殺也。

translations.literal: Wu thought 'what destroys Yao is Jin' and thereupon led wife and children south in flight and was killed by pursuing troops.
translations.idiomatic: Believing Jin would destroy Yao, he fled south with family and died under pursuit.

sentences.zh: 鳩摩羅什

translations.literal: Kumarajiva.
translations.idiomatic: Kumarajiva.

sentences.zh: 鳩摩羅什，天竺人也。

translations.literal: Kumarajiva was a native of Tianzhu.
translations.idiomatic: Kumarajiva came from India.

sentences.zh: 世為國相。

translations.literal: For generations his family were state ministers.
translations.idiomatic: His clan had long served as chief ministers.

sentences.zh: 父鳩摩羅炎，聰懿有大節，將嗣相位，乃辭避出家，東渡蔥嶺。

translations.literal: His father Kumarayana was intelligent and virtuous with great integrity; about to inherit the minister's post, he declined and avoided it, left home, and crossed the Cong Ridge eastward.
translations.idiomatic: His father Kumarayana renounced succession as minister, took orders, and crossed the Pamirs east.

sentences.zh: 龜茲王聞其名，郊迎之，請為國師。

translations.literal: The king of Kucha heard his fame, met him in the suburbs, and requested him as national teacher.
translations.idiomatic: Kucha's king welcomed him as national preceptor.

sentences.zh: 王有妹，年二十，才悟明敏，諸國交娉，並不許，及見炎，心欲當之，王乃逼以妻焉。

translations.literal: The king had a younger sister, twenty years old, talented and bright; the various states sought her in marriage and she did not consent to any; when she saw Yan, in her heart she wished to match him; the king then forced her to be his wife.
translations.idiomatic: The princess, wooed by many realms, chose Kumarayana; the king compelled their marriage.

sentences.zh: 既而羅什在胎，其母慧解倍常。

translations.literal: Thereupon while Kumarajiva was in the womb his mother's wisdom doubled the norm.
translations.idiomatic: His mother grew doubly wise while carrying him.

sentences.zh: 及年七歲，母遂與俱出家。

translations.literal: When he reached seven years, his mother then with him left home.
translations.idiomatic: At seven mother and son both ordained.

sentences.zh: 羅什從師受經，日誦千偈，偈有三十二字，凡三萬二千言，義亦自通。

translations.literal: Kumarajiva received sutras from teachers, daily reciting a thousand gathas; each gatha had thirty-two graphs, in all thirty-two thousand graphs, and the meaning likewise penetrated of itself.
translations.idiomatic: He memorized a thousand thirty-two-character gathas daily—thirty-two thousand graphs—and grasped their sense.

sentences.zh: 年十二，其母攜到沙勒，國王甚重之，遂停沙勒一年。

translations.literal: At twelve his mother brought him to Shule; the king of the state greatly esteemed him, and he therefore stayed in Shule one year.
translations.idiomatic: At twelve he visited Shule and stayed a year, honored by the king.

sentences.zh: 博覽五明諸論及陰陽星算，莫不必盡，妙達吉凶，言若符契。

translations.literal: He broadly read the treatises of the five sciences and yin-yang and star reckoning; there was none he did not exhaust; he wonderfully penetrated auspicious and inauspicious, and his words matched tally.
translations.idiomatic: He mastered the five sciences, astrology, and omens with uncanny accuracy.

sentences.zh: 為性率達，不拘小檢，修行者頗共疑之。

translations.literal: By nature he was frank and open, not bound by petty scruple; practitioners largely doubted him together.
translations.idiomatic: His easy manner drew suspicion from ascetics.

sentences.zh: 然羅什自得於心，未嘗介意，專以大乘為化，諸學者皆共師焉。

translations.literal: Yet Kumarajiva was self-content in mind and never minded; he devoted himself to converting with the Great Vehicle, and all students together took him as teacher.
translations.idiomatic: He ignored critics and taught Mahayana to universal acclaim.

sentences.zh: 年二十，龜茲王迎之還國，廣說諸經，四遠學徒莫之能抗。

translations.literal: At twenty the king of Kucha welcomed him back to the state and broadly expounded the sutras; students from the four quarters could not rival him.
translations.idiomatic: At twenty Kucha recalled him to preach; none could match his learning.

sentences.zh: 有頃，羅什母辭龜茲王往天竺，留羅什住，謂之曰：「方等深教，不可思議，傳之東土，惟爾之力。

translations.literal: Before long Kumarajiva's mother took leave of the king of Kucha to go to Tianzhu, leaving Kumarajiva behind, telling him, "The profound teachings of the Great Equalities are beyond thought; to transmit them to the eastern lands is only through your strength."
translations.idiomatic: His mother left for India, charging him to carry the Mahayana east.

sentences.zh: 但於汝無利，其可如何？

translations.literal: Yet for you there is no benefit—what can be done?
translations.idiomatic: She warned the task would not profit him personally.

sentences.zh: 」什曰：「必使大化流傳，雖苦而無恨。

translations.literal: He said, "If it must make the great teaching flow and spread, though suffering there is no regret."
translations.idiomatic: He vowed to spread the dharma despite hardship.

sentences.zh: 」母至天竺，道成，進登第三果。

translations.literal: When his mother reached Tianzhu, she completed the Way and advanced to the third fruit.
translations.idiomatic: In India his mother reached the third fruit of arhatship.

sentences.zh: 西域諸國咸伏羅什神俊，每至講說，諸王皆長跪坐側，令羅什踐而登焉。

translations.literal: The western regions all submitted to Kumarajiva's spirit brilliance; whenever he lectured, the kings all knelt long at his side and had Kumarajiva tread on them to mount the seat.
translations.idiomatic: Western kings knelt for him to step on their backs mounting the dais.

sentences.zh: 苻堅聞之，密有迎羅什之意。

translations.literal: Fu Jian heard of him and secretly had the intent to welcome Kumarajiva.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Jian resolved to fetch him.

sentences.zh: 會太史奏云：「有星見外國分野，當有大智入輔中國。

translations.literal: Just then the grand astrologer memorialized, saying, "There is a star appearing in the foreign field division—there ought to be a great wisdom who enters and aids the Middle Kingdom."
translations.idiomatic: Court astrologers reported a star over foreign fields—a sage would aid China.

sentences.zh: 」堅曰：「朕聞西域有鳩摩羅什，將非此邪？

translations.literal: Jian said, "I have heard that in the Western Regions there is Kumarajiva—could it not be this?"
translations.idiomatic: Fu Jian guessed it meant Kumarajiva.

sentences.zh: 」乃遣驍騎將軍呂光等率兵七萬，西伐龜茲，謂光曰：「若獲羅什，即馳驛送之。

translations.literal: Thereupon he dispatched General Who Charges Cavalry Lu Guang and others leading seventy thousand troops to campaign west against Kucha, telling Guang, "If you obtain Kumarajiva, immediately send him post-haste."
translations.idiomatic: He sent Lu Guang with seventy thousand men to seize Kumarajiva alive.

sentences.zh: 」光軍未至，羅什謂龜茲王白純曰：「國運衰矣，當有勍敵從日下來，宜恭承之，勿抗其鋒。

translations.literal: Before Guang's army arrived, Kumarajiva told the king of Kucha, Bai Chun, "The state's fortune declines; there will be a mighty foe coming from beneath the sun—you ought respectfully to receive him; do not resist his edge."
translations.idiomatic: Kumarajiva warned King Bai Chun to yield to Lu Guang.

sentences.zh: 」純不從，出兵距戰，光遂破之，乃獲羅什。

translations.literal: Chun did not follow, sent troops to resist battle, and Guang thereupon defeated him and obtained Kumarajiva.
translations.idiomatic: Bai Chun fought and lost; Lu Guang took the monk.

sentences.zh: 光見其年齒尚少，以凡人戲之，強妻以龜茲王女，羅什距而不受，辭甚苦至。

translations.literal: Guang saw he was still young in years and toyed with him as a common man, forced him to marry the king of Kucha's daughter; Kumarajiva resisted and would not accept, his refusal extremely bitter.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Guang mocked his youth, forced a royal bride on him; he refused bitterly.

sentences.zh: 光曰：「道士之操不逾先父，何所固辭？

translations.literal: Guang said, "A monk's conduct does not surpass your late father's—why so stubborn a refusal?"
translations.idiomatic: Lu Guang sneered that monastic vows had not stopped his father.

sentences.zh: 」乃飲以醇酒，同閉密室。

translations.literal: Thereupon he made him drink strong wine and locked him together in a secret room.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Guang drunk him and locked him with the princess.

sentences.zh: 羅什被逼，遂妻之。

translations.literal: Kumarajiva pressed by force, then married her.
translations.idiomatic: Coerced, Kumarajiva wed her.

sentences.zh: 光還，中路置軍於山下，將士已休，羅什曰：「在此必狼狽，宜徙軍隴上。

translations.literal: On the return, midway Guang encamped the army beneath a mountain; generals and soldiers had already rested; Kumarajiva said, "Here we are sure to be in straits—you ought to move the army onto the Long upland."
translations.idiomatic: Mid-march he urged moving camp uphill to avoid flood.

sentences.zh: 」光不納。

translations.literal: Guang did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Guang ignored him.

sentences.zh: 至夜，果大雨，洪潦暴起，水深數丈，死者數千人，光密異之。

translations.literal: When night came there was indeed great rain; violent flood suddenly rose; water depth several chang; several thousand died; Guang secretly marveled.
translations.idiomatic: Night brought a deluge that drowned thousands; Lu Guang marveled.

sentences.zh: 光欲留王西國，羅什謂光曰：「此凶亡之地，不宜淹留，中路自有福地可居。

translations.literal: Guang wished to keep the king in the western states; Kumarajiva told Guang, "This is a land of violent death—not fitting to linger; midway on the road there is naturally a blessed place to dwell."
translations.idiomatic: He dissuaded Lu Guang from staying in the deadly western basin.

sentences.zh: 」光還至涼州，聞苻堅已為姚萇所害，於是竊號河右。

translations.literal: When Guang returned to Liang Province, he heard Fu Jian had already been killed by Yao Chang; thereupon he arrogated title west of the River.
translations.idiomatic: Reaching Liangzhou, Lu Guang learned Fu Jian was dead and seized the Hexi throne.

sentences.zh: 屬姑臧大風，羅什曰：「不祥之風當有奸叛，然不勞自定也。

translations.literal: When a great wind struck Guzang, Kumarajiva said, "This ill wind means there will be treasonous rebellion, yet without labor it will settle of itself."
translations.idiomatic: A Guzang gale foretold brief rebellion.

sentences.zh: 」俄而有叛者，尋皆殄滅。

translations.literal: Before long there were rebels, and soon all were exterminated.
translations.idiomatic: Rebels rose and were crushed.

sentences.zh: 沮渠蒙遜先推建康太守段業為主，光遣其子纂率眾討之。

translations.literal: Juqu Mengxun first set up Jiankang governor Duan Ye as lord; Guang sent his son Zuan leading a host to chastise them.
translations.idiomatic: Juqu Mengxun raised Duan Ye; Lu Guang sent Lu Zuan against them.

sentences.zh: 時論謂業等烏合，纂有威聲，勢必全克。

translations.literal: Current opinion held Ye and cohort a rabble while Zuan had dread fame—the situation was sure to be wholly conquered.
translations.idiomatic: Court opinion expected Lu Zuan's easy victory.

sentences.zh: 光以訪羅什，答曰：「此行未見其利。

translations.literal: Guang consulted Kumarajiva; he answered, "This march does not yet show its gain."
translations.idiomatic: Kumarajiva said the campaign would not pay.

sentences.zh: 」既而纂敗于合黎，俄又郭黁起兵，纂棄大軍輕還，復為黁所敗，僅以身免。

translations.literal: Before long Zuan was defeated at Heli; before long again Guo Wu raised troops; Zuan abandoned the great army and lightly returned and was again defeated by Wu, barely escaping with his life.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Zuan lost at Heli, fled from Guo Wu's revolt, and barely survived.

sentences.zh: 中書監張資病，光博營救療。

translations.literal: Palace secretary supervisor Zhang Zi fell ill; Guang widely sought cure.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Guang spared no effort to heal Zhang Zi.

sentences.zh: 有外國道人羅叉，雲能差資病。

translations.literal: There was a foreign monk named Luocha who said he could cure Zi's illness.
translations.idiomatic: A foreign monk Luocha claimed a cure.

sentences.zh: 光喜，給賜甚重。

translations.literal: Guang was pleased and supplied him very generously.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Guang showered Luocha with gifts.

sentences.zh: 羅什知叉誑詐，告資曰：「叉不能為益，徒煩費耳。

translations.literal: Kumarajiva knew Luocha was deceitful; he told Zi, "Luocha cannot bring benefit—only vexation and expense."
translations.idiomatic: Kumarajiva exposed Luocha as a fraud.

sentences.zh: 冥運雖隱，可以事試也。

translations.literal: Though dark fate is hidden, it can be tested by an affair.
translations.idiomatic: Yet fate could be tested by a sign.

sentences.zh: 」乃以五色絲作繩結之，燒為灰末，投水中，灰若出水還成繩者，病不可愈。

translations.literal: Thereupon with five-colored silk he made a rope, knotted it, burned it to ash powder, threw it in water—if the ash coming out of water again formed a rope, the illness could not be cured.
translations.idiomatic: He burned a knotted five-color silk cord to ash and floated it—if it reknotted in water, death was certain.

sentences.zh: 須臾，灰聚浮出，復為繩，叉療果無效，少日資亡。

translations.literal: In a moment the ash gathered floating out and again became a rope; Luocha's treatment indeed had no effect; within a few days Zi died.
translations.idiomatic: The ash re-formed the rope; Luocha failed; Zhang Zi soon died.

sentences.zh: 頃之，光死，纂立。

translations.literal: Before long Guang died; Zuan succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Guang died; Lu Zuan ruled.

sentences.zh: 有豬生子，一身三頭。

translations.literal: A pig gave birth to one body with three heads.
translations.idiomatic: A sow farrowed a three-headed piglet.

sentences.zh: 龍出東箱井中，於殿前蟠臥，比旦失之。

translations.literal: A dragon came out of the east-side well, coiled sleeping before the hall; by dawn it was gone.
translations.idiomatic: A dragon left the east well, coiled in the court, vanished by dawn.

sentences.zh: 纂以為美瑞，號其殿為龍翔殿。

translations.literal: Zuan took it as an auspicious prodigy and styled his hall Dragon Soaring Hall.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Zuan called it an omen and renamed his hall Dragon Soaring.

sentences.zh: 俄而有黑龍升于當陽九宮門，纂改九宮門為龍興門。

translations.literal: Before long a black dragon ascended at the Dangyang Nine Palaces Gate; Zuan changed Nine Palaces Gate to Dragon Rising Gate.
translations.idiomatic: A black dragon at Nine Palaces gate brought the name Dragon Rising.

sentences.zh: 羅什曰：「比日潛龍出遊，豕妖表異，龍者陰類，出入有時，而今屢見，則為災眚，必有下人謀上之變。

translations.literal: Kumarajiva said, "These days lurking dragons roam abroad; the pig monster shows prodigy—dragons are yin in kind, coming and going with seasons; now they are repeatedly seen, then they are calamity misfortune—there must be change of a subordinate plotting against superiors."
translations.idiomatic: Kumarajiva read dragons and pigs as yin omens of minister murdering lord.

sentences.zh: 宜克己修德，以答天戒。

translations.literal: You ought to restrain the self and cultivate virtue to answer heaven's warning.
translations.idiomatic: He urged self-discipline to answer heaven.

sentences.zh: 」纂不納，後果為呂超所殺。

translations.literal: Zuan did not accept; afterward he was indeed killed by Lu Chao.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Zuan ignored him and died at Lu Chao's hands.

sentences.zh: 羅什之在涼州積年，呂光父子既不弘道，故蘊其深解，無所宣化。

translations.literal: Kumarajiva's years in Liang Province were many; since Lu Guang father and son did not promote the Way, therefore he stored his deep understanding and had nowhere to proclaim and convert.
translations.idiomatic: Under Lu Guang's irreligious court he hid his deepest learning.

sentences.zh: 姚興遣姚碩德西伐，破呂隆，乃迎羅什，待以國師之禮，仍使入西明閣及逍遙園，譯出眾經。

translations.literal: Yao Xing sent Yao Shoude to campaign west, defeated Lu Long, and welcomed Kumarajiva, treating him with rites of national teacher, still having him enter the West Bright Pavilion and Free Roaming Garden to translate the many sutras.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Xing destroyed Later Liang, welcomed Kumarajiva as national teacher, and set him translating in Chang'an gardens.

sentences.zh: 羅什多所暗誦，無不究其義旨，既覽舊經多有紕繆，於是興使沙門僧睿、僧肇等八百餘人傳受其旨，更出經論，凡三百餘卷。

translations.literal: Kumarajiva had much memorized by heart; none did he fail to exhaust in meaning and gist; once he perused old translations they had many errors; therefore Xing had the shramanas Seng Rui, Seng Zhao, and more than eight hundred others transmit and receive his intent, issuing anew sutras and treatises—in all more than three hundred scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: He retranslated more than three hundred scrolls with eight hundred assistants, correcting old errors.

sentences.zh: 沙門慧睿才識高明，常隨羅什傳寫，羅什每為慧睿論西方辭體，商略同異，云：「天竺國俗甚重文制，其宮商體韻，經入管弦為善。

translations.literal: The shramana Hui Rui, talented and bright, constantly followed Kumarajiva in transcription; Kumarajiva often for Hui Rui discussed western phrasing, weighing sameness and difference, saying, "The custom of the Tianzhu state greatly esteems literary form; its musical tones and rhymes, when sutras enter pipes and strings, are excellent."
translations.idiomatic: Hui Rui transcribed while Kumarajiva explained Indic metrics and how hymns suited music.

sentences.zh: 凡覲國王，必有贊德，經中偈頌，皆其式也。

translations.literal: Whenever one meets a king, there must be praise of virtue; the gathas in sutras are all models of this.
translations.idiomatic: Royal audiences required hymns—sutra verses followed that form.

sentences.zh: 」羅什雅好大乘，志在敷演，常歎曰：「吾若著筆作大乘阿毗曇，非迦旃子比也。

translations.literal: Kumarajiva elegantly loved the Great Vehicle; his intent lay in spreading exposition; he often sighed, "If I took brush to compose a Mahayana Abhidharma, I would not be matched by Katyayaniputra."
translations.idiomatic: He sighed he could outwrite Katyayani if scholars existed to hear a Great Vehicle Abhidharma.

sentences.zh: 今深識者既寡，將何所論！

translations.literal: Now those with deep knowledge are few—with whom shall I discuss!
translations.idiomatic: Few could follow his depth.

sentences.zh: 」惟為姚興著《實相論》二卷，興奉之若神。

translations.literal: Only for Yao Xing he wrote the Treatise on True Character in two scrolls; Xing honored it like a spirit.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote two fascicles on true marks for Yao Xing alone.

sentences.zh: 嘗講經於草堂寺，興及朝臣、大德沙門千有餘人肅容觀聽，羅什忽下高坐，謂興曰：「有二小兒登吾肩，欲鄣須婦人。

translations.literal: Once lecturing at Caotang Monastery, Xing and court ministers and great-virtue shramanas more than a thousand with solemn bearing watched and listened; Kumarajiva suddenly stepped down from the high seat and told Xing, "There are two boys climbing my shoulders; they want to block—must have women."
translations.idiomatic: Mid-lecture he told Yao Xing two spirits on his shoulders demanded women.

sentences.zh: 」興乃召宮女進之，一交而生二子焉。

translations.literal: Xing thereupon summoned palace women to advance to him; with one union he begot two sons.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Xing sent palace ladies; he fathered twin sons.

sentences.zh: 興嘗謂羅什曰：「大師聽明超悟，天下莫二，何可使法種少嗣。

translations.literal: Xing once told Kumarajiva, "Master, your brilliance and penetration surpass the realm—none is second; how can we allow the dharma seed so few in heirs."
translations.idiomatic: Yao Xing said his genius should not lack dharma heirs.

sentences.zh: 」遂以伎女十人，逼令受之。
