translations.literal: Thereupon with ten singing-girls he forced him to accept them.
translations.idiomatic: He forced ten courtesans on the monk.

sentences.zh: 爾後不住僧坊，別立解舍。

translations.literal: Afterward he did not dwell in the monks' quarters but separately built a lay house.
translations.idiomatic: Kumarajiva thereafter lived apart from the cloister in a private compound.

sentences.zh: 諸僧多效之。

translations.literal: The various monks for the most part imitated him.
translations.idiomatic: Many monks copied his householding.

sentences.zh: 什乃聚針盈缽，引諸僧謂之曰：「若能見效食此者，乃可畜室耳。

translations.literal: Thereupon he gathered needles filling a bowl, led the various monks and told them, "If you can imitate me and eat these, then you may keep wives."
translations.idiomatic: He filled a bowl with needles and dared the assembly to eat them like him if they wanted wives.

sentences.zh: 」因舉匕進針，與常食不別，諸僧愧服乃止。

translations.literal: Thereupon he raised a spoon and advanced the needles; it was no different from ordinary food; the various monks ashamed submitted and desisted.
translations.idiomatic: He ate them like rice until the monks, shamed, dropped the pretense.

sentences.zh: 杯渡比丘在彭城，聞羅什在長安，乃歎曰：「吾與此子戲，別三百餘年，相見杳然未期，遲有遇于來生耳。

translations.literal: The bhikshu Beidu in Pengcheng, hearing Kumarajiva was in Chang'an, then sighed, "I played with this fellow; parted more than three hundred years—meeting again is dim without date; slowly there may be meeting in a later life."
translations.idiomatic: Monk Beidu in Pengcheng sighed that he and Kumarajiva were old friends separated three centuries, reunion left to another birth.

sentences.zh: 」羅什未終少日，覺四大不愈，乃口出三番神咒，令外國弟子誦之以自救，未及致力，轉覺危殆，於是力疾與眾僧告別曰：「因法相遇，殊未盡心，方復後世，惻愴可言。

translations.literal: Kumarajiva, not yet ended within a few days, felt the four great elements not recovering; thereupon he uttered three rounds of spirit spells, ordering foreign disciples to recite them to save himself; before he could exert effort, he turned and felt peril; therefore with strained illness he took leave of the assembly of monks, saying, "Through the dharma we met—truly not yet having exhausted the heart; only in a later life—how bitterly one may speak."
translations.idiomatic: Feeling death near, he tried spells, then bade the sangha a tearful farewell to meet again in future lives.

sentences.zh: 」死于長安。

translations.literal: He died in Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 姚興於逍遙園依外國法以火焚屍，薪滅形碎，惟舌不爛。

translations.literal: Yao Xing at Free Roaming Garden according to foreign method burned the corpse with fire; when the fuel was exhausted the form broke; only the tongue did not rot.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Xing cremated him by Indian rite; only his tongue survived the fire.

sentences.zh: 僧曇霍

translations.literal: Seng Tanhuo.
translations.idiomatic: Seng Tanhuo.

sentences.zh: 沙門曇霍者，不知何許人也。

translations.literal: The shramana Tanhuo—none knew what place he was from.
translations.idiomatic: Monk Tanhuo's origin was unknown.

sentences.zh: 禿髮傉檀時從河南來，持一錫杖，令人跪曰：「此是般若眼，奉之可以得道。

translations.literal: At the time of Tufa Rutan he came from Henan holding one tin staff, making people kneel and saying, "This is the eye of prajna; honoring it can obtain the Way."
translations.idiomatic: Under Tufa Rutan he came from Henan with a tin staff, bidding folk kneel and calling it the eye of prajna.

sentences.zh: 」時人咸異之。

translations.literal: People of the time all marveled at him.
translations.idiomatic: All thought him strange.

sentences.zh: 或遺以衣服，受而投之於河，後日以還其本主，衣無所汙。

translations.literal: Some gifted him clothes; he accepted and threw them in the river; later on the day they returned to their original owners, the clothes without stain.
translations.idiomatic: Gifts of clothing he cast in the river; garments returned spotless to donors.

sentences.zh: 行步如風雲，言人死生貴賤無毫釐之差。

translations.literal: He walked like wind and cloud; speaking of men's death and life, noble and base, there was not a hair's breadth of error.
translations.idiomatic: He strode like wind, predicting life and death without fault.

sentences.zh: 人或藏其錫杖，曇霍大哭數聲，閉目須臾，起而取之，咸奇其神異，莫能測也。

translations.literal: If someone hid his tin staff, Tanhuo wailed loudly several times, closed his eyes a moment, rose and took it; all marveled at his spirit strangeness and could not fathom him.
translations.idiomatic: If his staff was hidden, he wailed briefly, then walked straight to its hiding place.

sentences.zh: 每謂傉檀曰：「若能安坐無為，則天下可定，祚胤克昌，如其窮兵好殺，禍將及己。

translations.literal: He often told Rutan, "If you can sit peacefully and do nothing, then All-under-Heaven can be settled, your fortune and heirs can flourish; if instead you exhaust armies and love killing, calamity will reach yourself."
translations.idiomatic: He urged Tufa Rutan to rule quietly or face self-ruin through war.

sentences.zh: 」傉檀不能從。

translations.literal: Rutan could not follow this.
translations.idiomatic: Rutan refused the counsel.

sentences.zh: 傉檀女病甚，請救療，曇霍曰：「人之生死自有定期，聖人亦不能轉禍為福，曇霍安能延命邪！

translations.literal: Rutan's daughter was gravely ill; he requested cure; Tanhuo said, "Men's life and death each have a fixed term; even sages cannot turn misfortune into fortune—how can Tanhuo extend life!"
translations.idiomatic: Asked to heal the princess, Tanhuo said fate could not be bought.

sentences.zh: 正可知早晚耳。

translations.literal: Only early or late can be known.
translations.idiomatic: He could only tell the hour of death.

sentences.zh: 」傉檀固請之。

translations.literal: Rutan firmly requested him.
translations.idiomatic: Rutan pressed him.

sentences.zh: 時後宮門閉，曇霍曰：急開後門，及開門則生，不及則死。

translations.literal: At the time the rear palace gate was closed; Tanhuo said, "Open the rear gate in haste—when the gate opens she lives; if it does not open in time she dies."
translations.idiomatic: With the inner gate shut he cried to open the rear gate instantly or she would die.

sentences.zh: 」傉檀命開之，不及而死。

translations.literal: Rutan ordered it opened; it did not open in time and she died.
translations.idiomatic: The gate opened too late; the princess died.

sentences.zh: 後兵亂，不知所在也。

translations.literal: Later in army turmoil none knew where he went.
translations.idiomatic: War swallowed him without trace.

sentences.zh: 台產

translations.literal: Tai Chan.
translations.idiomatic: Tai Chan.

sentences.zh: 台產，字國俊，上洛人，漢侍中崇之後也。

translations.literal: Tai Chan, courtesy name Guojun, was a native of Shangluo, a descendant of Han attendant-in-chamber Chong.
translations.idiomatic: Tai Chan, courtesy name Guojun, came from Shangluo, descended from Han's Tai Chong.

sentences.zh: 少專京氏《易》，善圖讖、秘緯、天文、洛書、風角、星算、六日七分之學，尤善望氣、占候、推步之術。

translations.literal: In his youth he specialized in the Jing lineage Changes; he was good at charts and prophecies, secret weft texts, astronomy, Luo documents, fengjiao, star reckoning, and the six-day seven-part learning; especially he was good at observing qi, omen divination, and calendrical computation arts.
translations.idiomatic: He mastered Jing Fang's Changes, apocrypha, astronomy, Luo charts, wind-angle, and calendrical arts, especially qi-watching.

sentences.zh: 隱居商洛南山，兼善經學，泛情教授，不交當世。

translations.literal: He dwelt in seclusion on South Mountain of Shang-Luo; concurrently he was good in classical learning, broadly feeling and teaching, not associating with the age.
translations.idiomatic: He taught classics in hermitage on Shangluo South Mountain, shunning office.

sentences.zh: 劉曜時，災異特甚，命公卿各舉博識直言之士一人。

translations.literal: At Liu Yao's time omens and prodigies were especially severe; he ordered dukes and ministers each to recommend one broadly learned straight-speaking gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yao's reign brought dire omens; he ordered each minister to nominate a truth-telling scholar.

sentences.zh: 其大司空劉均舉產。

translations.literal: His grand minister of works Liu Jun recommended Chan.
translations.idiomatic: Grand minister of works Liu Jun nominated Tai Chan.

sentences.zh: 曜親臨東堂，遣中黃門策問之，產極言其故。

translations.literal: Yao personally came to the east hall, sent inner yellow gates to examine him with questions, and Chan exhaustively stated the reasons.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yao questioned him at the east hall; Tai Chan explained every portent.

sentences.zh: 曜覽而嘉之，引見，訪以政事。

translations.literal: Yao read and praised him, summoned him for audience, and consulted him on governing.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yao praised his memorials and sought policy advice.

sentences.zh: 產流涕歔欷，具陳災變之禍，政化之闕，辭甚懇至。

translations.literal: Chan wept and sobbed, fully stating the harm of calamity and prodigy and the gaps in government and transformation, his words extremely earnest.
translations.idiomatic: Tai Chan wept, listing omens and policy failures with brutal honesty.

sentences.zh: 曜改容禮之，署為博士祭酒、諫議大夫，領太史令。

translations.literal: Yao changed expression and honored him, appointing him libationer of erudits, grandee remonstrant, concurrent grand astrologer.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yao honored him as erudite libationer, remonstrance grandee, and grand astrologer.

sentences.zh: 至明年而其言皆驗，曜彌重之，轉太中大夫，歲中三遷。

translations.literal: By the next year his words all verified; Yao still more esteemed him, transferring him to grand palace adviser—three promotions within the year.
translations.idiomatic: His forecasts proved within the year; Liu Yao promoted him thrice.

sentences.zh: 歷位尚書、光祿大夫、太子少師，位特進，金章紫綬，爵關中侯。

translations.literal: He successively held posts as minister, grand master of splendid brightness, junior tutor to the heir, specially advanced, golden seal and purple ribbon, marquis within the passes.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to minister, splendid brightness grandee, junior tutor, specially advanced, golden seal and purple ribbon, marquis within the passes.

sentences.zh: 史評

translations.literal: Historians' appraisal.
translations.idiomatic: Historians' appraisal.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：陳戴等諸子並該洽墳典，研精數術，究推步之幽微，窮陰陽之秘奧，雖前代京管，何以加之！

translations.literal: The court historians say: Chen, Dai, and the various gentlemen alike comprehended the tomb classics and refined numerological arts, plumbing calendrical subtlety and exhausting yin-yang's secret depths—even the former age's Jing Fang and Guan Zhong—how could one add more!
translations.idiomatic: The annalists praise Chen Xun, Dai Yang, and their peers for mastering the canon and cosmology beyond even Jing Fang and Guan Zhong.

sentences.zh: 郭黁知有晉之亡姚，去姚以歸晉，追兵奄及，致斃中途，斯則遠見秋毫，不能近知目睫。

translations.literal: Guo Wu knew there was Jin to destroy Yao; he left Yao to return to Jin—pursuing troops suddenly overtook him and brought death midway—thus he saw autumn's tip yet could not know what lay on his own eyelashes.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Wu foresaw Jin ending Yao yet died fleeing—sharp on distant stars, blind to his own peril.

sentences.zh: 澄什爰自遐裔，來游諸夏。

translations.literal: Cheng and Kumarajiva came from distant corners and roamed the various Xia.
translations.idiomatic: Fotucheng and Kumarajiva came from afar to teach China.

sentences.zh: 什既兆見星象，澄乃驅役鬼神，並通幽洞冥，垂文闡教，諒見珍於道藝，非取貴於他山，姚石奉之若神，良有以也。

translations.literal: Kumarajiva first divined star images; Cheng then commanded ghosts and spirits; both penetrated the dark and illumined the hidden, handing down writings and expounding teaching—truly they were treasured for their Dao art, not honored as borrowed stones from other hills; Yao and Shi revered them like spirits—with good reason.
translations.idiomatic: One read stars, the other mastered spirits; both taught scripture—Yao and Shi honored their arts, not mere foreign curiosities, with cause.

sentences.zh: 鮑、吳、王、幸等或假靈道訣，或受教神方，遂能厭勝禳災，隱文彰義，雖獲譏於妖妄，頗有益於世用者焉。

translations.literal: Bao, Wu, Wang, Xing, and the rest either borrowed spirit formulas or received divine recipes, thereby able to suppress ill and avert disaster, hiding text yet manifesting meaning—although they received ridicule as sorcerous, they had quite a bit that benefited worldly use.
translations.idiomatic: Bao Jing, Wu Meng, Wang Jia, and Xing Ling used charms to help the world despite charges of sorcery.

sentences.zh: 然而碩學通人，未宜枉轡。

translations.literal: Yet great learning thorough men ought not lightly to bend the carriage traces.
translations.idiomatic: True scholars should not blindly follow such paths.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：《傳》敘災祥，《書》稱龜筮。

translations.literal: The encomium says: The Documents narrate calamity and auspice; the Canon praises tortoise and milfoil.
translations.idiomatic: The verse says: the Documents record omens; the Canon praises tortoise and yarrow.

sentences.zh: 應如影響，葉若符契。

translations.literal: They respond like shadow and echo; match like tally and contract.
translations.idiomatic: They answer like shadow and echo; align like tallies matched.

sentences.zh: 怪力亂神，詭時惑世。

translations.literal: Strange powers and disordering spirits cheat the age and delude the world.
translations.idiomatic: Uncanny powers and unruly spirits deceive the age and bewilder the world.

sentences.zh: 崇尚弗已，必致流弊。

translations.literal: If one esteems and promotes them without cease, it is sure to lead to flowing abuse.
translations.idiomatic: Endless veneration of such arts invites lasting harm.
